# Schema `iam`

### `iam.organisations`
Purpose: the tenant root: identity, plan, security switches, branding, sharing policy and calendar in one row. Spec chapters 26, 37 and 56 merged.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key, UUIDv7. This is the tenant key; the RLS policy compares `id` to `app.org_id`. Other tables point here with `organisation_id → iam.organisations (id)`.
- `name` text, not null.
- `slug` citext, not null. Unique, case-insensitive. Immutable after creation (the directory is keyed on it). Check `slug ~ '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,62}$'`. Added: format check.
- `status` text, not null, default `active`. Check in (`active`, `suspended`, `closed`). Added: mirrors the directory.
- `is_system` boolean, not null, default false. Added (review 2026-10-28): marks the cell's system organisation, which holds only Silo-owned secrets such as Silo-registered OAuth clients and their sealed secrets. The system organisation is never in the directory and has no memberships (a trigger on `iam.memberships` rejects any row for it).
- `is_synthetic` boolean, not null, default false. Added (D198): Silo's synthetic organisation, one a cell (unique partial index), where the Fleet agent's release gates run their synthetic tests; never also `is_system`; frozen; inserted by `silo_auth` alone; excluded from the login and staff lookups. Its two members cannot sign in (no password, SSO-only with no provider); auth mints their sessions for the agent.
- `plan` text, not null. Check in (`standard`, `business`, `enterprise`).
- `sso_required` boolean, not null, default false.
- `mfa_required` boolean, not null, default false.
- `storage_enabled` boolean, not null, default false. Siloes master switch; requires `silo.enable`.
- `discovery_enabled` boolean, not null, default false. Requires `discovery.manage`.
- `logo_object_key` text, null. `logo_content_type` text, null. `logo_uploaded_by` uuid, null (membership). `logo_uploaded_at` timestamptz, null. Check: all four null or all four set.
- `billing_status` text, not null, default `active`. Check in (`active`, `past_due`, `suspended`, `cancelled`). Written only by the payment webhook or the staff path (chapter 75): `silo_app` has column-level `update` on every column except this one; the billing webhook service uses a separate grant.
- `view_sharing_policy` text, not null, default `explicit_only`. Check in (`open`, `scope_only`, `explicit_only`, `disabled`). Chapter 37. The default is a proposal, as the spec gives none.
- `org_wide_sharing_permitted` boolean, not null, default false.
- `external_sharing_permitted` boolean, not null, default false. Check `external_sharing_permitted = false`.
- `cell_id` text, not null. Immutable by trigger.
- `calendar_time_zone` text, not null. IANA zone, for example `Europe/London`. Chapter 26. Validated against `pg_timezone_names` by trigger.
- `financial_year_start_month` integer, null. Check 1 to 12. Null until onboarding sets it; no default is assumed.
- `financial_year_start_day` integer, not null, default 1. Check 1 to 31.
- `week_start_day` integer, not null, default 1. Check 1 to 7 (1 is Monday).
- `financial_year_label` text, null. Check in (`start_year`, `end_year`). Check: null exactly when `financial_year_start_month` is null.
- `calendar_updated_by` uuid, null (membership). `calendar_updated_at` timestamptz, null.
- `session_idle_minutes` integer, null. Check `> 0`. Added (decision 2026-10-29): the organisation's idle timeout. Null uses the cell's. The auth service takes the shorter of this and the cell's, so an organisation can shorten its sessions but never lengthen them.
- `session_absolute_minutes` integer, null. Check `> 0`. Added (decision 2026-10-29): as `session_idle_minutes`, for the absolute timeout. Check: `session_idle_minutes <= session_absolute_minutes` when both are set.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added: optimistic locking for concurrent admin edits.
Changed: chapter 26 and 37 definitions removed; chapter 37's three columns and chapter 56's two duplicates are one column each.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `slug`. The convention's `unique (organisation_id, id)` is satisfied by the primary key, since `id` is the organisation id. Unique on `((true))` partial where `is_system` (Added (review 2026-10-28): one system organisation per cell).
References: `(id, logo_uploaded_by) → iam.memberships (organisation_id, id)` and `(id, calendar_updated_by) → iam.memberships (organisation_id, id)`, both deferrable initially deferred (a membership is created after the organisation exists). `cell_id → platform.cells (id)`. Added (review 2026-10-28): cells are keyed by the text cell identifier.
Indexes: unique `slug` (SSO and slug lookups inside a cell). Foreign key indexes: `(id, logo_uploaded_by)` partial where not null; `(id, calendar_updated_by)` partial where not null.
Security: RLS enabled and forced; policy compares `id` to `app.org_id` (using and with check). Provisioning sets `app.org_id` to the new UUIDv7 before inserting. Writers: identity service (all except `billing_status`), billing webhook service (`billing_status`). Every change to `status`, `mfa_required`, `sso_required` bumps `iam.policy_versions`. Never deleted.

### `iam.users`
Purpose: one person's login identity within a cell. Spec chapter 55.2.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `first_name` text, not null. `last_name` text, not null.
- `email` citext, not null. Unique. Normalised before storage.
- `email_verified_at` timestamptz, null.
- `password_hash` text, null. Argon2id. Check: not null unless `sso_only`.
- `sso_only` boolean, not null, default false. Added: makes "required unless SSO-only" checkable.
- `password_changed_at` timestamptz, null.
- `failed_attempt_count` integer, not null, default 0. Check >= 0. Cleared on success.
- `locked_until` timestamptz, null. Set on lockout.
- `avatar_object_key` text, null. `avatar_content_type` text, null. Both null or both set.
- `status` text, not null, default `active`. Check in (`active`, `suspended`, `deprovisioned`).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `last_seen_at` timestamptz, null. Written at most once per 5 minutes per user (proposal) to avoid a write per request.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `email`.
References: none.
Indexes: unique `email` (login lookup, `iam.find_user_for_login`).
Security: not under tenant RLS; see "How the user-keyed tables are protected". Writer: auth service (`silo_auth`). Never deleted; `deprovisioned` is a status.

View `iam.member_profiles` (defined here, not a table): `select m.id as membership_id, m.organisation_id, u.first_name, u.last_name, u.email, u.avatar_object_key, u.avatar_content_type, u.status as user_status from iam.memberships m join iam.users u on u.id = m.user_id where m.organisation_id = current_setting('app.org_id')::uuid`. Serves the member list and name display in every product screen.

### `iam.password_resets`
Purpose: single-use password reset tokens. Spec chapter 55.3.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `user_id` uuid, not null.
- `token_hash` bytea, not null. Hash of a 256-bit random token; plaintext only in the email.
- `requested_from_ip_hash` bytea, null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, not null. Check `expires_at > created_at`.
- `consumed_at` timestamptz, null.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `token_hash`.
References: `user_id → iam.users (id)`.
Indexes: unique `token_hash` (consume lookup). `(user_id)` partial where `consumed_at is null` (invalidate earlier open resets when a new one is requested; foreign key index).
Security: not under tenant RLS; user-keyed RLS and `silo_auth` only. Consuming sets `consumed_at` and revokes every session of the user in the same transaction. Rows kept 30 days after expiry, then removed by the retention job as `silo_migrate` (proposal).

### `iam.mfa_factors`
Purpose: a user's TOTP or WebAuthn factor. Spec chapter 55.4.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key. Part of the AAD.
- `user_id` uuid, not null. Part of the AAD.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`totp`, `webauthn`).
- `secret_sealed` bytea, null. TOTP secret, AES-256-GCM ciphertext including tag.
- `nonce` bytea, null. 96 bits. Added: the spec lists no nonce for this table.
- `dek_wrapped` bytea, null.
- `key_version_id` uuid, null. Changed (review 2026-10-28): not part of the AAD; the KEK version is bound to `dek_wrapped` through the KMS encryption context. The AAD for `secret_sealed` is `(id, user_id, kind)`.
- `credential_id` bytea, null. WebAuthn credential id.
- `webauthn_public_key` bytea, null. Added: needed to verify assertions; not a secret.
- `sign_count` bigint, null. Added: WebAuthn clone detection.
- `confirmed_at` timestamptz, null. Usable only after confirmation.
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null. Added: factors are retired, not deleted.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `last_used_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
- `last_used_step` bigint, null. Check `>= 0`. Added (decision 2026-10-29): TOTP only, the time step of the last accepted code. A code is accepted within one step of drift either side, and only if its step is after this one; the auth service sets it by compare-and-set (`update ... where last_used_step is null or last_used_step < $step`), so a code works once, even when two logins race with it.
Check: `kind = 'totp'` requires `secret_sealed, nonce, dek_wrapped, key_version_id` not null and WebAuthn columns null; `kind = 'webauthn'` requires `credential_id, webauthn_public_key, sign_count` not null and sealed columns null. Added (decision 2026-10-29): `kind = 'totp' or last_used_step is null`.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `credential_id` where not null (login lookup by WebAuthn credential).
References: `user_id → iam.users (id)`; `key_version_id → iam.kms_key_versions (id)`.
Indexes: `(user_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null and confirmed_at is not null` (MFA challenge: usable factors of a user; foreign key index). `(key_version_id)` partial where not null (rotation: factors still on an old key, and the retire check).
Security: not under tenant RLS; user-keyed RLS and `silo_auth` only. Unwrap through the credential mediator: the auth service reads the sealed secret and the credential service opens it, recording reason `mfa_verify` in `iam.credential_unwraps` (Changed (decision 2026-10-29)); a successful challenge is recorded in `auth_events` as `mfa_satisfied` (decision 6). Factors are revoked, never deleted, so ledger rows keep their reference. Writer: auth service.

### `iam.sessions`
Purpose: opaque server-side session for a user or a service principal; Postgres is the revocation list. Spec chapter 60.1.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `token_hash` bytea, not null. Unique. Hash of a 256-bit random token.
- `user_id` uuid, null. Set for human sessions.
- `service_principal_id` uuid, null. Added: set for `api_client` sessions (decision 7). Check `num_nonnulls(user_id, service_principal_id) = 1`.
- `organisation_id` uuid, null. Added: denormalised from the active membership or principal so the sessions join tenant tables with a composite key. Null only for a pre-selection human session. Check: null exactly when `active_membership_id` and `service_principal_id` are both null.
- `active_membership_id` uuid, null. Null until the person chooses an organisation; such a session authorises nothing. Switching membership issues a new session.
- `issued_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, not null. Check `expires_at > issued_at`.
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
- `ip_hash` bytea, null. `user_agent_hash` bytea, null.
- `auth_method` text, not null. Check in (`password`, `sso`, `agent`, `synthetic`; `synthetic` added D198 for the synthetic organisation's members). Principal sessions use `agent` for agent and `api_client` principals (the spec set has no separate value).
- `mfa_satisfied_at` timestamptz, null. Where the organisation requires MFA, null means a deny on every permission.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `token_hash`; unique `(organisation_id, id)` (target of `gov.purpose_sessions`).
References: `user_id → iam.users (id)`; `(organisation_id, active_membership_id) → iam.memberships (organisation_id, id)`; `(organisation_id, service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals (organisation_id, id)`.
Indexes: unique `token_hash` (every request that misses Redis). `(user_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null` (revoke every session of a user). `(organisation_id, active_membership_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null` (member removal, SCIM deprovision, `session.revoke`). `(organisation_id, service_principal_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null` (principal revocation). `(expires_at)` partial where `revoked_at is null` (expiry sweep).
Security: Changed (implementation 2026-10-28, D20): spec 64.2 requires forced RLS on every table carrying `organisation_id`, so `enable` and `force` RLS with one policy `session_owner`: `user_id = app.user_id or organisation_id = app.org_id` (each read with `current_setting(..., true)`, empty treated as null). The auth service reaches a session as its user or within its organisation; lookups by token go through `iam.resolve_session`. Otherwise see protection list. Hot copy in Redis under TTL; revocation writes Postgres and deletes the Redis key in one operation. Writer: auth service. Rows are removed 30 days after expiry by retention (proposal).

### `iam.identity_providers`
Purpose: an organisation's SAML or OIDC provider configuration, with the metadata sealed. Spec chapter 55.5.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key. Part of the AAD.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null. Part of the AAD.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`saml`, `oidc`).
- `issuer` text, not null.
- `metadata_sealed` bytea, not null. AES-256-GCM ciphertext including tag.
- `nonce` bytea, not null. Added (96 bits).
- `dek_wrapped` bytea, not null.
- `key_version_id` uuid, not null. Changed (review 2026-10-28): not part of the AAD; the KEK version is bound to `dek_wrapped` through the KMS encryption context. The AAD for `metadata_sealed` is `(id, organisation_id, kind)`.
- `jit_provisioning` boolean, not null, default false.
- `default_role_id` uuid, null. Required when `jit_provisioning` is true (check).
- `default_scope_id` uuid, null.
- `active` boolean, not null, default false.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added. `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, issuer)`.
References: `organisation_id → iam.organisations (id)`; `(organisation_id, default_role_id) → iam.roles`; `(organisation_id, default_scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `key_version_id → iam.kms_key_versions (id)`.
Indexes: unique `(organisation_id, issuer)` (SSO assertion routing). `(organisation_id, default_role_id)`, `(organisation_id, default_scope_id)` partial where not null (foreign key indexes). `(key_version_id)` (rotation and retire check).
Security: RLS standard. Sealed columns reached only through the mediator (reason `idp`). JIT provisioning grants the default role and scope only, never clearances or purpose eligibility (enforced by the provisioning service and by the fact that it holds no insert right on `gov.clearances` or `gov.purpose_eligibility`). Writer: identity service, `org.sso.manage`.

### `iam.user_identities`
Purpose: links one SSO identity (an OIDC or SAML subject at one organisation's identity provider) to a user. Login by SSO resolves the user through this table, never by email. Spec chapters 55.5, 60. Added (review 2026-10-28): SSO needs a stable subject-to-user link that never relies on email.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `identity_provider_id` uuid, not null.
- `user_id` uuid, not null.
- `subject` text, not null. The provider's stable, non-reassignable identifier: OIDC `sub`; for Microsoft Entra ID the `tid` and `oid` pair as `tid:oid`; SAML persistent NameID. Check `length(subject) between 1 and 512`.
- `email_at_link` citext, not null. Display and audit only, never used to match.
- `linked_via` text, not null. Check in (`invitation`, `jit`, `existing_session`). How the first link was proven.
- `linked_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `last_login_at` timestamptz, null.
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null. `revoked_by` uuid, null (membership). Check: both null or both set.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, identity_provider_id, subject)` partial where `revoked_at is null`; unique `(organisation_id, identity_provider_id, user_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null`.
References: `(organisation_id, identity_provider_id) → iam.identity_providers`; `user_id → iam.users (id)`; `(organisation_id, revoked_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: unique `(organisation_id, identity_provider_id, subject)` partial (assertion lookup on every SSO login). `(user_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null` (deprovision, "linked accounts"). `(organisation_id, revoked_by)` partial where not null. `(organisation_id, identity_provider_id)` and `(user_id)`, both non-partial: FK indexes. Added (review 2026-10-28).
Security: RLS standard (the organisation is known from the SSO flow before the lookup). Privileges as for the user-keyed tables: only `silo_auth` holds `select, insert, update`; revoked from `silo_app` and `silo_report`. Linking rule: an assertion is never matched to an existing user by email. A first link needs proof: acceptance of an invitation (the token proves control of the email), JIT provisioning that creates a new user, or the person signing in with their existing method in the same flow (`existing_session`). When JIT is on and a user with the asserted email already exists in the cell, the flow requires the `existing_session` proof and never links silently. Reason: email claims can be set by the identity provider's tenant admins (the Entra "nOAuth" class of takeover). Writer: auth service.

### `iam.scim_tokens`
Purpose: bearer tokens for SCIM provisioning. Spec chapter 55.5.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `token_hash` bytea, not null. Plaintext shown once at issue. The issued token is `<organisation_id>.<random>`, so the gateway sets `app.org_id` from the prefix before the lookup.
- `created_by` uuid, not null (membership). Added. `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `last_used_at` timestamptz, null.
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, token_hash)`.
References: `organisation_id → iam.organisations (id)`; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: unique `(organisation_id, token_hash)` (token lookup). `(organisation_id, created_by)` (foreign key).
Security: RLS standard. SCIM deprovision runs in one transaction: set membership `suspended`, release the seat, revoke sessions. Writer: identity service.

### `iam.memberships`
Purpose: a user's presence in one organisation; every decision, audit row and owned resource refers to it. Spec chapter 55.6.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `user_id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `status` text, not null, default `invited`. Check in (`invited`, `active`, `suspended`, `removed`).
- `job_title` text, null.
- `invited_by` uuid, null (membership). Null for the first super admin.
- `invited_at` timestamptz, null. `joined_at` timestamptz, null. Check: `joined_at` set when status is not `invited`.
- `suspended_at` timestamptz, null. Added. `removed_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Status timestamps; cleared on reinstatement.
- `scim_external_id` text, null. Added (review 2026-10-28): the SCIM `externalId` the organisation's provisioning client uses for this member.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added. `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(user_id, organisation_id)`; unique `(organisation_id, scim_external_id)` partial where not null (Added (review 2026-10-28): SCIM lookup by `externalId`).
References: `user_id → iam.users (id)`; `organisation_id → iam.organisations (id)`; `(organisation_id, invited_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: unique `(user_id, organisation_id)` (list a user's organisations through `iam.list_user_memberships(user_id)`, a `security definer` function owned by `silo_migrate` because RLS hides other organisations; Changed (review 2026-10-28): owner was `silo_auth`, see protection layer 3, and `execute` is granted to `silo_auth` only). `(organisation_id, created_at desc)` (member list screen). `(organisation_id, status)` partial where `status <> 'removed'` (active-member counts and pickers). `(organisation_id, invited_by)` partial where not null (foreign key).
Security: RLS standard. Removal runs in one transaction (chapter 55.7): set `removed`, revoke sessions and purpose sessions, set `silenced_at` on grants, set `inactive_since` on scope memberships, leave the seat. Status changes bump `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: identity service.

### `iam.invitations`
Purpose: pending offers of membership by email. Spec chapter 55.6.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `email` citext, not null.
- `token_hash` bytea, not null. Plaintext only in the email. Issued as `<organisation_id>.<random>`.
- `role_id` uuid, not null. Role assigned on acceptance.
- `scope_id` uuid, null. Scope joined on acceptance.
- `seat_id` uuid, null. Seat reference (chapter 72).
- `invited_by` uuid, not null (membership).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `accepted_at` timestamptz, null.
- `accepted_membership_id` uuid, null. Added: ties the invitation to the membership it created. Set with `accepted_at`.
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
Check: not both `accepted_at` and `revoked_at` set.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, token_hash)`; unique `(organisation_id, email)` partial where `accepted_at is null and revoked_at is null` (one open invitation per email).
References: `(organisation_id, role_id) → iam.roles`; `(organisation_id, scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, seat_id) → billing.seats`; `(organisation_id, invited_by) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, accepted_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, created_at desc)` partial where `accepted_at is null and revoked_at is null` (pending invitations screen). Unique `(organisation_id, token_hash)` (acceptance). Foreign key indexes `(organisation_id, role_id)`, `(organisation_id, scope_id)`, `(organisation_id, seat_id)`, `(organisation_id, invited_by)`, `(organisation_id, accepted_membership_id)` (the nullable ones partial where not null).
Security: RLS standard. Writer: identity service, `member.invite`.

### `iam.scope_types`
Purpose: organisation-defined labels for scope nodes (Department, Project, Region and so on). Spec chapter 56.3.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `name` text, not null.
- `icon` text, null. `colour` text, null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added. `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, name)`.
References: `organisation_id → iam.organisations (id)`.
Indexes: unique `(organisation_id, name)` (scope type picker).
Security: RLS standard. Writer: identity service, `scope_type.manage` (super admin only).

### `iam.scopes`
Purpose: nodes of the organisation's scope tree; administrative authority is a subtree. Spec chapters 56.3 and 56.4.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `scope_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `name` text, not null.
- `parent_scope_id` uuid, null. Null means top level.
- `path` ltree, not null. Ancestor chain; each label is the scope `id` as 32 hex characters, so renaming never rewrites paths and a move rewrites only the prefix.
- `depth` integer, not null. Check `depth = nlevel(path)` and `depth between 1 and 12`.
- `archived_at` timestamptz, null.
- `created_by` uuid, not null (membership). `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added. `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `nulls not distinct (organisation_id, parent_scope_id, name)`; unique `(organisation_id, path)`.
References: `(organisation_id, scope_type_id) → iam.scope_types`; `(organisation_id, parent_scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `gist (organisation_id, path)` using `btree_gist` (subtree containment `path <@ $1` for effective admin scope and role assignment resolution). `(organisation_id, parent_scope_id)` (children list; foreign key). `(organisation_id, scope_type_id)`, `(organisation_id, created_by)` (foreign keys).
Security: RLS standard. Triggers: a move may not place a scope under its own descendant; a move rewrites `path` and `depth` of the node and every descendant in one transaction; archive requires no active scope memberships beneath. Moves bump `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: identity service, `scope.manage`.

### `iam.scope_memberships`
Purpose: many-to-many link between a membership and the scopes it sits in. Spec chapter 56.4.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `scope_id` uuid, not null.
- `is_primary` boolean, not null, default false. Display and routing only, never authorisation.
- `added_by` uuid, not null (membership). `added_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `inactive_since` timestamptz, null. Set on membership removal; excluded from resolution.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, membership_id, scope_id)`; unique `(organisation_id, membership_id)` partial where `is_primary and inactive_since is null`.
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, added_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: unique `(organisation_id, membership_id, scope_id)` (resolution step 1, scopes of a membership; the resolver filters `inactive_since is null` during the scan). `(organisation_id, scope_id)` (members of a scope; archive check). `(organisation_id, added_by)` (foreign key).
Security: RLS standard. Changes bump `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: identity service.

### `iam.permissions`
Purpose: the fixed global catalogue of atomic permission verbs. Spec chapter 57.2.
Columns:
- `id` text, not null. Primary key, for example `query.compile`. Catalogue in chapter 76.
- `category` text, not null. Includes `authorising` (chapter 60.6).
- `scopeable` boolean, not null.
- `description` text, not null. Added: shown in the role editor.
Keys: primary key `id`.
References: none.
Indexes: primary key only; the table is under a few hundred rows. `(category)` is not indexed.
Security: global catalogue, no tenant, no RLS. Seeded by migration under `silo_migrate`; `silo_app` and `silo_report` hold `select` only. Not user-creatable.

### `iam.roles`
Purpose: named bundles of permissions, as data. Spec chapter 57.2.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `name` text, not null.
- `system_role` boolean, not null, default false. Seeded roles cannot be deleted or renamed (trigger).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added. `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added. `retired_at` timestamptz, null. Added: roles are retired, not deleted, while referenced. `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, name)`.
References: `organisation_id → iam.organisations (id)`.
Indexes: unique `(organisation_id, name)` (role picker).
Security: RLS standard. Changes bump `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: identity service.

### `iam.role_permissions`
Purpose: which permissions a role contains. Spec chapter 57.2.
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `role_id` uuid, not null.
- `permission_id` text, not null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, role_id, permission_id)`. Link table: no `id`; the primary key is the tenant unique key.
References: `(organisation_id, role_id) → iam.roles`; `permission_id → iam.permissions (id)`.
Indexes: primary key serves the permission union per role (resolution step 2). `(permission_id)` (foreign key; who holds a permission, used by the authorising-category trigger).
Security: RLS standard. Trigger: inserting a permission with category `authorising` into a role held by any service principal is rejected (see `iam.service_principal_roles`). Changes bump `iam.policy_versions`.

### `iam.role_grantable_roles`
Purpose: whitelist of roles a role may assign. Spec chapter 56.7.
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `granting_role_id` uuid, not null.
- `grantable_role_id` uuid, not null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, granting_role_id, grantable_role_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, granting_role_id) → iam.roles`; `(organisation_id, grantable_role_id) → iam.roles`.
Indexes: primary key serves "roles this role may assign". `(organisation_id, grantable_role_id)` (foreign key; "who may assign this role").
Security: RLS standard. Read by the delegation trigger on `iam.role_assignments`. Bumps `iam.policy_versions`.

### `iam.role_assignments`
Purpose: gives a membership a role, organisation-wide or on one target. Spec chapter 57.2.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `role_id` uuid, not null.
- Target arc, at most one set; none set means organisation-wide (super admin tier). Changed: replaces `scope_type` and `scope_id`.
  - `on_scope_id` uuid, null (admin tier when the role is an admin role). `on_connection_id` uuid, null. `on_silo_id` uuid, null. `on_view_id` uuid, null. `on_object_type_id` uuid, null. `on_app_id` uuid, null.
- `granted_by` uuid, not null (membership).
- `granted_at_scope_id` uuid, null. Scope the granter held when issuing. Null only when a super admin issued it.
- `granted_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, null.
- `revoked_by` uuid, null (membership). `revoked_at` timestamptz, null. Check: `revoked_by` set only with `revoked_at`.
- `silenced_at` timestamptz, null. Suspension or removal; cleared on reinstatement.
Check: `num_nonnulls(on_scope_id, on_connection_id, on_silo_id, on_view_id, on_object_type_id, on_app_id) <= 1`.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, membership_id, role_id, coalesce(on_scope_id, on_connection_id, on_silo_id, on_view_id, on_object_type_id, on_app_id, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'))` partial where `revoked_at is null`.
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, role_id) → iam.roles`; `(organisation_id, on_scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, on_connection_id) → connect.connections`; `(organisation_id, on_silo_id) → siloes.siloes`; `(organisation_id, on_view_id) → workspace.saved_views`; `(organisation_id, on_object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, on_app_id) → workspace.apps`; `(organisation_id, granted_by)`, `(organisation_id, revoked_by)` → `iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, granted_at_scope_id) → iam.scopes`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, membership_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null` (resolution step 1: a membership's live assignments, including silenced so reinstatement finds them).
- `(organisation_id, on_scope_id)` partial where `on_scope_id is not null and revoked_at is null` (assignments whose scope path contains a membership's scope; admin lookup).
- `(organisation_id, granted_at_scope_id)` partial where not null (revocation authority and the orphan list: grants issued under a subtree).
- `(organisation_id, on_connection_id)`, `(organisation_id, on_silo_id)`, `(organisation_id, on_view_id)`, `(organisation_id, on_object_type_id)`, `(organisation_id, on_app_id)`, each partial where the column is not null (resolution on the resource, and foreign keys).
- `(organisation_id, role_id)` (who holds a role). `(organisation_id, granted_by)` (orphan list for the admin above, by issuer). `(organisation_id, revoked_by)` partial where not null (foreign key).
Security: RLS standard. Write-time delegation trigger (chapter 56.7), evaluated in the inserting transaction: the target scope path must be contained by the granter's scope path (`<@`); the granted role's permission set must be a subset of the granter's effective set at the target scope; no organisation-wide row unless the granter is a super admin; the role must be in `iam.role_grantable_roles` for one of the granter's roles; `clearance.grant`, `purpose.define` and `marking.declassify` roles only by a super admin. Revocation is permitted to the issuer, an admin whose subtree contains `granted_at_scope_id`, or a super admin (trigger on update of `revoked_at`). Admin revocation never cascades. Changes bump `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: identity service.

### `iam.connection_grants`
Purpose: default-deny access of a grantee to a connection. Spec chapter 57.3.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `connection_id` uuid, not null.
- Grantee arc, exactly one set. Changed: replaces `grantee_type` and `grantee_id`.
  - `grantee_membership_id` uuid, null. `grantee_scope_id` uuid, null. `grantee_role_id` uuid, null. `grantee_service_principal_id` uuid, null.
- `access` text, not null. Check in (`read`, `write`).
- `include_descendants` boolean, not null, default true. Applies only to a scope grantee (check: false or true is allowed for other grantees only when true, since it has no meaning there). The spec gives no default; true matches the stated normal case.
- `granted_by` uuid, not null (membership).
- `granted_at_scope_id` uuid, null. Null only when a super admin issued it. Load-bearing for revocation authority.
- `granted_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, null.
- `revoked_by` uuid, null (membership). `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
- `silenced_at` timestamptz, null.
Check: `num_nonnulls(grantee_membership_id, grantee_scope_id, grantee_role_id, grantee_service_principal_id) = 1`.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, connection_id, coalesce(grantee_membership_id, grantee_scope_id, grantee_role_id, grantee_service_principal_id))` partial where `revoked_at is null` (one live grant per grantee and connection; a read and a write grant to the same grantee are one row with the higher access).
References: `(organisation_id, connection_id) → connect.connections`; `(organisation_id, grantee_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, grantee_scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, grantee_role_id) → iam.roles`; `(organisation_id, grantee_service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals`; `(organisation_id, granted_by)`, `(organisation_id, revoked_by)` → `iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, granted_at_scope_id) → iam.scopes`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, connection_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null` (resolution step 3 on a connection).
- `(organisation_id, grantee_membership_id)` partial where `grantee_membership_id is not null and revoked_at is null` (a member's connections; silence and restore on removal).
- `(organisation_id, grantee_scope_id)`, `(organisation_id, grantee_role_id)`, `(organisation_id, grantee_service_principal_id)`, each partial where not null and `revoked_at is null` (the same resolution through scope, role and principal).
- `(organisation_id, granted_at_scope_id)` partial where not null (revocation authority, orphan list). `(organisation_id, granted_by)` (orphan list by issuer). `(organisation_id, revoked_by)` partial where not null (foreign key).
Security: RLS standard. Same delegation and revocation triggers as `iam.role_assignments`, plus the connection subset rule (the granter must hold the connection at that scope). Changes bump `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: identity service, `connection.create` and `admin.delegate` paths.

### `iam.field_policies`
Purpose: deny, mask or redact a source field or a property, resolved before the plan exists. Spec chapter 57.4.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `connection_id` uuid, null. `field_path` text, null. `property_id` uuid, null.
- `effect` text, not null. Check in (`deny`, `mask`, `redact`).
- `applies_to_role_id` uuid, null. `applies_to_marking_id` uuid, null. `applies_to_scope_id` uuid, null. Each present column narrows the audience (AND). All null means everyone. The spec does not state the combination rule; this is the stated assumption.
- `include_descendants` boolean, not null, default false. Meaningful with `applies_to_scope_id`.
- `created_by` uuid, not null (membership). `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added. `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
- `retired_at` timestamptz, null. Added: rows are retired, not deleted.
Check: `(connection_id is not null and field_path is not null and property_id is null) or (connection_id is null and field_path is null and property_id is not null)`.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, connection_id) → connect.connections`; `(organisation_id, property_id) → ontology.properties`; `(organisation_id, applies_to_role_id) → iam.roles`; `(organisation_id, applies_to_marking_id) → gov.markings`; `(organisation_id, applies_to_scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, connection_id, field_path)` partial where `connection_id is not null and retired_at is null` (compile-time lookup of policies for the fields a plan touches). `(organisation_id, property_id)` partial where `property_id is not null and retired_at is null` (compile-time lookup by property). `(organisation_id, applies_to_role_id)`, `(organisation_id, applies_to_marking_id)`, `(organisation_id, applies_to_scope_id)`, each partial where not null (foreign keys). `(organisation_id, created_by)`.
Security: RLS standard. Bumps `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: governance service.

### `iam.object_type_markings`
Purpose: direct markings on an object type, applying to every version of it. Spec chapters 21 and 57 merged.
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `marking_id` uuid, not null.
- `applied_by` uuid, not null (membership). `applied_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Changed: chapter 21's `element_kind` and `element_id` removed (see decision 2).
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, object_type_id, marking_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, marking_id) → gov.markings`; `(organisation_id, applied_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: primary key serves step 4 of resolution (markings on a type). `(organisation_id, marking_id)` (every type carrying a marking; retire check). `(organisation_id, applied_by)`.
Security: RLS standard. Removal is a declassification (`gov.marking_declassifications`): the row is deleted only by the declassification Action, which holds the only `delete` grant on this table, and the Action's receipt records it. Bumps `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: governance service, `marking.manage`.

### `iam.service_principals`
Purpose: non-human identities (agent, automation, api client, AI FDE) that execute but never authorise. Spec chapter 60.4.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`agent`, `automation`, `api_client`, `fde`).
- `name` text, not null.
- `certificate_fingerprint` bytea, null. Agent mTLS certificate. The certificate subject carries `organisation_id`, so the gateway sets `app.org_id` before the lookup. Required when `kind = 'agent'`.
- `secret_hash` bytea, null. Hash of a 256-bit secret; plaintext shown once. Required when `kind = 'api_client'`. The client identifier is `<organisation_id>.<id>`.
- `scope_id` uuid, null. Bounds the principal to a subtree.
- `owner_membership_id` uuid, not null. Accountable person.
- `engagement_id` uuid, null. Required exactly when `kind = 'fde'`.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, null. Required for `fde` and `api_client` (check).
- `created_by` uuid, not null (membership). `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, id, kind)` (Added (review 2026-10-28): target for `fde.fde_principals`, which pins `kind = 'fde'`); unique `(organisation_id, certificate_fingerprint)` partial where not null.
References: `(organisation_id, scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id)`, `(organisation_id, created_by)` → `iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, engagement_id) → fde.fde_engagements`.
Indexes: unique `(organisation_id, certificate_fingerprint)` (agent connection setup). `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id)` (transfer on member removal). `(organisation_id, scope_id)` partial where not null (list within an admin's subtree). `(organisation_id, engagement_id)` partial where not null. `(organisation_id, created_by)`. `(organisation_id, expires_at)` partial where `revoked_at is null and expires_at is not null` (expiry sweep emitting `service_principal_expired`).
Security: RLS standard. Revocation revokes the principal's sessions in one transaction. Writer: identity service, `service_principal.manage`.

### `iam.service_principal_roles`
Purpose: roles held by a service principal. Spec chapter 60.4.
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `service_principal_id` uuid, not null.
- `role_id` uuid, not null.
- `granted_by` uuid, not null (membership). `granted_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, service_principal_id, role_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals`; `(organisation_id, role_id) → iam.roles`; `(organisation_id, granted_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: primary key serves principal permission resolution. `(organisation_id, role_id)`, `(organisation_id, granted_by)` (foreign keys).
Security: RLS standard. Constraint trigger, deferred to commit: reject any row whose role contains a permission with category `authorising`; the mirror trigger on `iam.role_permissions` rejects adding such a permission to a role already held by a principal. Each refusal writes `principal_authorising_permission_refused`. Bumps `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: identity service.

### `iam.kms_key_versions`
Purpose: cell-level registry of key encryption key versions. Spec chapter 61.2.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `provider` text, not null. Check in (`gcp_kms`, `uk_hsm`, `pkcs11_hsm`, `vault_transit`, `local`). Changed (implementation 2026-11-01): `local` (a key in configuration) for development and tests; production refuses it in configuration. Changed (review 2026-10-28): `pkcs11_hsm` (a customer HSM over PKCS#11) and `vault_transit` (HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao transit) added for self-managed installs. Changed (decision 2026-10-29): `vault_transit` is for development only (deployment modes).
- `key_uri` text, not null. Reference only, never key material.
- `version` integer, not null.
- `status` text, not null. Check in (`active`, `decrypt_only`, `retired`).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. `activated_at` timestamptz, null. `retired_at` timestamptz, null.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(provider, key_uri, version)`; unique on `((true))` partial where `status = 'active'` (one wrapping key at a time).
References: none.
Indexes: the unique indexes above. Wrap path reads the single active row.
Security: cell-level, no tenant data, no RLS. `silo_app` has `select`. Writes by the key rotation job under `silo_migrate`. Trigger: `retired` is allowed only when no row in `connect.connection_credentials`, `iam.mfa_factors`, `iam.identity_providers` or `iam.organisation_keys` references the version. Changed (review 2026-10-28): `iam.organisation_keys` added to the check.

### `iam.organisation_keys`
Purpose: the per-organisation data keys and HMAC keys that the encrypted record-value columns and keyed hashes rely on. Added (review 2026-10-28): the build rules name these keys but no section defined them.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `purpose` text, not null. Check in (`data`, `hmac`).
- `version` integer, not null. Check `version >= 1`. The data key version carried in every ciphertext envelope header.
- `dek_wrapped` bytea, not null. The 256-bit key wrapped by the cell KEK.
- `key_version_id` uuid, not null. The KEK version that wrapped it.
- `status` text, not null, default `active`. Check in (`active`, `decrypt_only`, `retired`).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. `activated_at` timestamptz, null. `retired_at` timestamptz, null. `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, purpose, version)`; unique `(organisation_id, purpose)` partial where `status = 'active'`; unique `(organisation_id, id, purpose)` (Added (review 2026-10-28): target that lets `ontology.match_keys` pin `purpose = 'hmac'`).
References: `organisation_id → iam.organisations (id)`; `key_version_id → iam.kms_key_versions (id)`.
Indexes: unique `(organisation_id, purpose)` partial (the encrypt path reads the active key). `(key_version_id)` (KEK rotation and the retire check).
Security: RLS standard. Column-level `select` on `dek_wrapped` is revoked from `silo_app` and granted to `silo_credential` only: keys are unwrapped through the credential mediator. Created with the organisation (one `data` and one `hmac` key). Writer: credential service.

### `iam.credential_unwraps`
Purpose: append-only ledger of every unwrap of a sealed credential, with its reason. Spec chapters 61.3 and 61.9; missing in the spec's data model.
Columns:
- `id` bigint, not null, `generated always as identity`.
- `occurred_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Partition key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null. For `mfa_verify`, the organisation being logged into (Changed (decision 2026-10-29)).
- `connection_credential_id` uuid, null. Arc arm 1.
- `identity_provider_id` uuid, null. Arc arm 2.
- `mfa_factor_id` uuid, null. Arc arm 3. Added (decision 2026-10-29): the factor whose TOTP secret was opened.
- `user_id` uuid, null. Added (decision 2026-10-29): the person verifying MFA; required for `mfa_verify` (check `reason <> 'mfa_verify' or user_id is not null`).
- `reason` text, not null. Check in (`connect`, `query`, `mutation`, `read_back`, `refresh`, `probe`, `rotation`, `change_stream`, `idp`, `mfa_verify`, `sso_assert`). Changed (decision 2026-10-29): `mfa_verify` and `sso_assert` added (decision 6). `idp` and `sso_assert` are valid only with `identity_provider_id`, `mfa_verify` only with `mfa_factor_id`, all others only with `connection_credential_id` (checks).
- `calling_service` text, not null. Service name from the deployment identity.
- `correlation_id` uuid, not null. Joins to the request, plan or job.
- `membership_id` uuid, null. `service_principal_id` uuid, null. The actor; `num_nonnulls(membership_id, service_principal_id) <= 1`, both null for platform jobs (rotation).
- `key_version_id` uuid, null. Version used to unwrap; null exactly when the outcome is `held_by_agent` (D132).
- `dek_cache_hit` boolean, not null. True when the DEK came from the 5 minute or 200 use cache, so every use is logged even when KMS was not called.
- `outcome` text, not null. Check in (`ok`, `failed`, `held_by_agent`). A failed GCM open is recorded. `held_by_agent` (D132, spec 6, 10.7): a use of a login the customer keeps on the Silo Agent's host, recorded against the row standing for the field (`connect.connection_credentials`, custody `agent`); nothing opened, no key, no DEK cache.
Never holds the secret or `last_four`.
Check: `num_nonnulls(connection_credential_id, identity_provider_id, mfa_factor_id) = 1` (Changed (decision 2026-10-29): `mfa_factor_id` added).
Keys: primary key `(id, occurred_at)`. Range partitioned by month on `occurred_at`. No unique `(organisation_id, id)`: nothing references a ledger.
References: `(organisation_id, connection_credential_id) → connect.connection_credentials`; `(organisation_id, identity_provider_id) → iam.identity_providers`; `mfa_factor_id → iam.mfa_factors (id)` and `user_id → iam.users (id)` (Added (decision 2026-10-29); factors and users are never deleted); `key_version_id → iam.kms_key_versions (id)`. No foreign key for the actor columns (ledger rows must survive any later change; they hold ids only).
Indexes: `(organisation_id, connection_credential_id, occurred_at desc)` partial where not null (reviewer reads the unwraps of one credential; per-credential rate for the anomaly detector). `(organisation_id, identity_provider_id, occurred_at desc)` partial where not null. `(organisation_id, mfa_factor_id, occurred_at desc)` partial where not null (Added (decision 2026-10-29)). `(organisation_id, reason, occurred_at desc)` (per-reason rate and review). `(organisation_id, correlation_id)` (trace one request). `brin (occurred_at)`.
Security: RLS standard. Append-only: trigger rejects `update` and `delete`; `silo_app` holds `insert, select`. Writer: the credential service only (`credential.service.ts`), in the same transaction that updates `connect.connection_credentials.last_used_at` (for a connection credential). Retention: partition drop by `silo_migrate` under the audit retention period set by the audit domain.

### `iam.policy_versions`
Purpose: one monotonic counter per organisation, used as the permission cache key. Missing in the spec's data model; named in chapter 57.6 and the conventions ("keyed by policy version").
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key. Added for the tenant unique key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `version` bigint, not null, default 1. Check `version >= 1`. Only ever increases.
- `last_changed_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `last_changed_by_table` text, null. Table name that caused the latest bump, for diagnosis.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id)`.
References: `organisation_id → iam.organisations (id)`.
Indexes: unique `(organisation_id)` (every permission resolution reads this row first).
Security: RLS standard. Created in the transaction that creates the organisation, with version 1. `silo_app` holds `select` only; updates go through `iam.bump_policy_version(organisation_id, table_name)`, a `security definer` function owned by `silo_migrate` that runs `version = version + 1`, and a trigger trap rejects any update that does not increase `version`. Statement-level `after insert or update or delete` triggers call it from: `iam.memberships` (status), `iam.scopes`, `iam.scope_memberships`, `iam.roles`, `iam.role_permissions`, `iam.role_grantable_roles`, `iam.role_assignments`, `iam.connection_grants`, `iam.field_policies`, `iam.object_type_markings`, `iam.service_principals`, `iam.service_principal_roles`, `iam.organisations` (security columns), `gov.markings`, `gov.clearances`, `gov.resource_markings`, `gov.artefact_markings`, `gov.purpose_definitions`, `gov.purpose_eligibility`. Statement-level means one bump per statement, so a propagation batch bumps once. Cache rule: the key is `(organisation_id, version, membership_id, purpose session set, resource)`; because expiry does not bump the version, an entry's TTL is capped at the earliest `expires_at` among the grants and clearances that produced it. Writer: triggers only.

---

# Schema `gov`

### `gov.markings`
Purpose: organisation-defined mandatory access labels. Spec chapter 58.3.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `name` text, not null.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`classification`, `compartment`, `purpose`). Immutable by trigger.
- `rank` integer, null. Check: set only when `kind = 'classification'`.
- `description` text, not null, default ''.
- `created_by` uuid, not null (membership). `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `retired_at` timestamptz, null. Retired, never deleted, while any resource carries it.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added. `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, name)`; unique `(organisation_id, id, kind)` (target for the kind-restricting foreign keys below).
References: `organisation_id → iam.organisations (id)`; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: unique `(organisation_id, name)` (marking picker). `(organisation_id, created_by)`.
Security: RLS standard. Bumps `iam.policy_versions` (retirement). Writer: governance service, `marking.manage`.

### `gov.clearances`
Purpose: a membership or service principal's clearance for a classification or compartment marking. Spec chapter 58.3.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `membership_id` uuid, null. `service_principal_id` uuid, null. Exactly one (check `num_nonnulls = 1`).
- `marking_id` uuid, not null.
- `marking_kind` text, not null. Added. Check in (`classification`, `compartment`). Enforces that purpose markings cannot be cleared; the composite foreign key to `gov.markings (organisation_id, id, kind)` makes the value true.
- `granted_by` uuid, not null (membership). Must hold `clearance.grant`; a trigger checks it. `granted_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, null.
- `revoked_by` uuid, null (membership). `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, membership_id, marking_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null and membership_id is not null`; unique `(organisation_id, service_principal_id, marking_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null and service_principal_id is not null`.
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals`; `(organisation_id, marking_id, marking_kind) → gov.markings`; `(organisation_id, granted_by)`, `(organisation_id, revoked_by)` → `iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the two partial uniques serve step 4 (mandatory gate: a membership's or principal's live clearances). `(organisation_id, marking_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null` (who holds a marking; impact preview for declassification). `(organisation_id, granted_by)`, `(organisation_id, revoked_by)` partial where not null (foreign keys).
Security: RLS standard. Silenced by membership removal through the membership status, not by a column here (clearances resolve only for `active` memberships). Bumps `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: governance service, `clearance.grant` (super admin only, never delegable). An `fde` principal gets clearances only by explicit super admin grant and they lapse at the principal's `expires_at` (resolution rule, plus a sweep that sets `revoked_at`).

### `gov.resource_markings`
Purpose: direct markings on resources other than object types. Spec chapter 58.3.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key. Added: the spec's composite key does not work across an arc.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- Resource arc, exactly one set. Changed: replaces `resource_type` and `resource_id`.
  - `connection_id` uuid (`connect.connections`). `property_mapping_id` uuid (`ontology.property_mappings`; the spec's "field map entry"). `property_id` uuid (`ontology.properties`). `link_type_id` uuid (`ontology.link_types`). `action_type_id` uuid (`action.action_types`). `silo_id` uuid (`siloes.siloes`). `view_id` uuid (`workspace.saved_views`). `app_id` uuid (`workspace.apps`). `function_id` uuid (`ontology.functions`). `interface_id` uuid (`ontology.interfaces`; Added from chapter 21).
- `marking_id` uuid, not null.
- `applied_by` uuid, not null (membership). `applied_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Removed: `concept` was already dropped by the spec; `object_type` markings live in `iam.object_type_markings`.
Check: `num_nonnulls(connection_id, property_mapping_id, property_id, link_type_id, action_type_id, silo_id, view_id, app_id, function_id, interface_id) = 1`.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; ten partial unique indexes, one per arm: `(organisation_id, <arm>_id, marking_id)` where `<arm>_id is not null`.
References: one composite foreign key per arm, `(organisation_id, <arm>_id) → <target table>` as listed; `(organisation_id, marking_id) → gov.markings`; `(organisation_id, applied_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the ten partial uniques serve both the marking lookup per resource (step 4) and the foreign keys. `(organisation_id, marking_id)` (every resource carrying a marking; retire check). `(organisation_id, applied_by)`.
Security: RLS standard. Removal is a declassification and is deleted only by the declassification Action. Bumps `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: governance service, `marking.manage`.

### `gov.purpose_definitions`
Purpose: an approved reason for which purpose-marked data may be reached. Spec chapter 58.5.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `marking_id` uuid, not null. `marking_kind` text, not null, default `purpose`, check `marking_kind = 'purpose'`. Added; composite foreign key keeps it true.
- `name` text, not null. `description` text, not null.
- `lawful_basis` text, null. Recorded, not validated.
- `max_session_minutes` integer, not null. Check > 0.
- `requires_justification` boolean, not null, default true. `requires_approval` boolean, not null, default false.
- `status` text, not null, default `draft`. Check in (`draft`, `approved`, `suspended`, `retired`).
- `approved_by` uuid, null (membership). Holds `purpose.define`, differs from `created_by` (check `approved_by <> created_by`). `approved_at` timestamptz, null. Both set when status has been `approved`.
- `review_due_at` timestamptz, null. Overdue approved definitions are suspended by a sweep.
- `created_by` uuid, not null (membership). `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added. `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, marking_id)` partial where `status <> 'retired'`.
References: `(organisation_id, marking_id, marking_kind) → gov.markings`; `(organisation_id, approved_by)`, `(organisation_id, created_by)` → `iam.memberships`.
Indexes: unique `(organisation_id, marking_id)` partial (definition for a marking). `(organisation_id, review_due_at)` partial where `status = 'approved'` (review sweep). `(organisation_id, approved_by)`, `(organisation_id, created_by)`.
Security: RLS standard. Bumps `iam.policy_versions`. Suspension or retirement ends affected purpose sessions in the same transaction. Writer: governance service, `purpose.define` (super admin only).

### `gov.purpose_eligibility`
Purpose: who may declare a purpose. Spec chapter 58.5.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `purpose_definition_id` uuid, not null.
- Grantee arc, exactly one set. Changed: replaces `grantee_type` and `grantee_id`.
  - `grantee_membership_id` uuid, null. `grantee_role_id` uuid, null. `grantee_scope_id` uuid, null. `grantee_service_principal_id` uuid, null.
- `granted_by` uuid, not null (membership). Must hold `clearance.grant`. `granted_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, null. `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
Check: `num_nonnulls(grantee_membership_id, grantee_role_id, grantee_scope_id, grantee_service_principal_id) = 1`.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, purpose_definition_id, coalesce(grantee_membership_id, grantee_role_id, grantee_scope_id, grantee_service_principal_id))` partial where `revoked_at is null`.
References: `(organisation_id, purpose_definition_id) → gov.purpose_definitions`; grantee arms → `iam.memberships`, `iam.roles`, `iam.scopes`, `iam.service_principals`; `(organisation_id, granted_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, purpose_definition_id)` partial where `revoked_at is null` (eligibility check on declare; end sessions on revocation). `(organisation_id, grantee_membership_id)`, `(organisation_id, grantee_role_id)`, `(organisation_id, grantee_scope_id)`, `(organisation_id, grantee_service_principal_id)`, each partial where not null and `revoked_at is null` (which purposes a member can declare). `(organisation_id, granted_by)`.
Security: RLS standard. Revocation ends affected purpose sessions in the same transaction. Bumps `iam.policy_versions`. Writer: governance service, `clearance.grant`.

### `gov.purpose_sessions`
Purpose: record of a declared purpose, bounded in time and by the parent session. Spec chapter 58.5.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `membership_id` uuid, null. `service_principal_id` uuid, null. Exactly one (check).
- `session_id` uuid, not null. Never outlives the authentication session.
- `purpose_definition_id` uuid, not null.
- `app_id` uuid, null. Set when opened by a purpose-bound app.
- `justification` text, null. Never sent to a model. Required when the definition has `requires_justification` (trigger).
- `approval_chain_id` uuid, null.
- `declared_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, not null. Trigger: not later than `declared_at` plus the definition's `max_session_minutes`, and not later than the parent session's `expires_at`.
- `ended_at` timestamptz, null.
- `ended_reason` text, null. Check in (`expired`, `ended_by_user`, `session_revoked`, `eligibility_revoked`, `definition_suspended`, `membership_removed`). Set exactly when `ended_at` is set.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals`; `(organisation_id, session_id) → iam.sessions`; `(organisation_id, purpose_definition_id) → gov.purpose_definitions`; `(organisation_id, app_id) → workspace.apps`; `(organisation_id, approval_chain_id) → action.approval_chains`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, session_id)` partial where `ended_at is null` (end every purpose session with the parent session). `(organisation_id, membership_id, declared_at desc)` (the reviewer reads declarations; a member's active sessions via the partial below). `(organisation_id, purpose_definition_id)` partial where `ended_at is null` (end on suspension). `(organisation_id, expires_at)` partial where `ended_at is null` (expiry sweep). `(organisation_id, service_principal_id)`, `(organisation_id, app_id)`, `(organisation_id, approval_chain_id)`, each partial where not null.
Security: RLS standard. Postgres is the record; the hot copy is in Redis (`redis-session`, `purp:` keys; Changed (review 2026-10-28): was `redis-state`, now matching the Redis keyspaces section) under TTL equal to `expires_at`, and ending a session deletes the key in the same operation. Sessions are never extended in place. Writer: governance service, `purpose.declare`. Retention: kept with audit.

### `gov.lineage_nodes`
Purpose: immutable versioned nodes of the lineage graph. Spec chapter 59.2.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key part, UUIDv7.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`source_field`, `connector_version`, `connection`, `property`, `object_type_version`, `link_type_version`, `action_type_version`, `function_version`, `object_set`, `view`, `app_version`, `export`, `ask_prompt`, `action`, `receipt`, `scenario`, `simulation_result`, `silo`, `import_file`).
- `ref_id` uuid, not null. The referenced resource, typed by `kind`, no foreign key (decision 8).
- `version` text, not null. Version or hash (CEL source hash, manifest hash).
- `created_by_membership_id` uuid, null. `created_by_service_principal_id` uuid, null. Changed: replaces `created_by`. At most one set; neither means a platform service.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Never updated, never holds record values.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, kind, ref_id, version)`. Hash partitioned by `organisation_id`, 16 partitions, so the keys include the partition key and `gov.artefact_markings` and `gov.lineage_edges` can reference it.
References: `(organisation_id, created_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, created_by_service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals`.
Indexes: the unique index serves node lookup by resource and version, and "downstream of a resource" entry point (prefix `organisation_id, kind, ref_id`). `(organisation_id, created_by_membership_id)`, `(organisation_id, created_by_service_principal_id)`, each partial where not null (foreign keys).
Security: RLS standard. Immutable: trigger rejects `update` and `delete`; `silo_app` holds `insert, select`. The lineage writer inserts with `on conflict do nothing` to reuse an existing version. A nightly sweep reports nodes whose `ref_id` no longer resolves (never deletes). Writer: every artefact-producing service, through the lineage writer library, in the artefact's own transaction.

### `gov.lineage_edges`
Purpose: typed edges from input node to derived node. Spec chapter 59.2.
Columns:
- `id` bigint, not null, `generated always as identity`. Added (ledger convention).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Partition key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `from_node_id` uuid, not null. `to_node_id` uuid, not null. Check `from_node_id <> to_node_id`.
- `relation` text, not null. Check in (`read_via`, `maps_to`, `member_of`, `derives`, `filters_on`, `traverses`, `compiles_to`, `uses`, `exported_from`, `writes`, `receipted_by`, `reverts`, `simulates`).
Keys: primary key `(id, created_at)`. Range partitioned by month on `created_at`. Nothing references it.
References: `(organisation_id, from_node_id) → gov.lineage_nodes`; `(organisation_id, to_node_id) → gov.lineage_nodes`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, from_node_id, relation)` (downstream traversal: what a resource fed). `(organisation_id, to_node_id, relation)` (upstream traversal and marking explanation). `brin (created_at)`.
Security: RLS standard. Append-only: trigger rejects `update` and `delete`; `silo_app` holds `insert, select`. Traversal is bounded to depth 32 and a node count by the reviewer query layer. Open decision: traversal reads every attached partition, so the retention period must be the longest artefact retention; a short age-based drop would silently truncate upstream lineage of old artefacts. The audit domain sets the retention; this domain recommends no age-based drop before the longest receipt retention. Writer: lineage writer library, in the artefact's transaction.

### `gov.artefact_markings`
Purpose: markings an artefact carries, direct or inherited by propagation. Spec chapter 58.7.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key part. Added: the spec's key `(node, marking)` cannot hold a re-applied marking after removal.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `lineage_node_id` uuid, not null.
- `marking_id` uuid, not null.
- `origin` text, not null. Check in (`direct`, `inherited`).
- `inherited_from_node_id` uuid, null. Nearest upstream node carrying the marking. Required when `origin = 'inherited'`.
- `applied_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `declassification_id` uuid, null. Set with `removed_at`; row retained.
- `removed_at` timestamptz, null.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, lineage_node_id, marking_id)` partial where `removed_at is null`. Hash partitioned by `organisation_id`, 16 partitions.
References: `(organisation_id, lineage_node_id)` and `(organisation_id, inherited_from_node_id) → gov.lineage_nodes`; `(organisation_id, marking_id) → gov.markings`; `(organisation_id, declassification_id) → gov.marking_declassifications`.
Indexes: the partial unique serves the read-time check of an artefact's live markings. `(organisation_id, marking_id)` partial where `removed_at is null` (propagation walk when a marking is added upstream; impact of a marking). `(organisation_id, inherited_from_node_id)` partial where not null (declassify downstream). `(organisation_id, declassification_id)` partial where not null.
Security: RLS standard. Where a node inherits a marking by several paths, one live row exists and the lineage service recomputes the union from edges on declassification. Until a propagation walk completes, the policy service also evaluates upstream markings at read time. Bumps `iam.policy_versions` once per statement. Writer: lineage service and the artefact-producing services (direct and inherited at creation).

### `gov.marking_declassifications`
Purpose: audited removal of a marking, carried by an Action. Spec chapter 58.9.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `action_id` uuid, not null. The Action carrying the change (chapter 42).
- `lineage_node_id` uuid, not null. The resource or artefact declassified.
- `marking_id` uuid, not null.
- `apply_downstream` boolean, not null, default false.
- `justification` text, not null. Check `length(trim(justification)) > 0`.
- `readers_gaining_access_count` integer, null. Computed at preview. Check >= 0.
- `requested_by` uuid, not null (membership). Membership only, so no service principal can request it by construction.
- `approval_chain_id` uuid, null. Required before execution (check: `executed_at` set requires it).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `executed_at` timestamptz, null. `reverted_at` timestamptz, null. Check: `reverted_at` requires `executed_at`.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `(organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, action_id, lineage_node_id, marking_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, action_id) → action.mutations`; `(organisation_id, lineage_node_id) → gov.lineage_nodes`; `(organisation_id, marking_id) → gov.markings`; `(organisation_id, requested_by) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, approval_chain_id) → action.approval_chains`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, created_at desc)` partial where `executed_at is null` (pending declassifications screen). `(organisation_id, lineage_node_id)` (history of a resource). `(organisation_id, marking_id)`. `(organisation_id, requested_by)`. `(organisation_id, approval_chain_id)` partial where not null. The unique key serves the `action_id` foreign key.
Security: RLS standard. Trigger at execution: the requester holds `marking.declassify` for this marking and satisfies it; the chain has at least one approver other than the requester who satisfies the marking; self-approval is rejected regardless of policy; no principal appears as approver. Not deleted. Writer: governance service.

# Hot paths

1. **Session resolution on a Redis miss:** `iam.sessions` unique `token_hash`; then `iam.memberships` primary key.
2. **Permission cache key:** `iam.policy_versions` unique `(organisation_id)`, one row read per request.
3. **Permission resolution on a cache miss (57.6):** `iam.scope_memberships` unique `(organisation_id, membership_id, scope_id)`; `iam.scopes` `gist (organisation_id, path)`; `iam.role_assignments` `(organisation_id, membership_id) where revoked_at is null` and `(organisation_id, on_scope_id)`; `iam.role_permissions` primary key; `iam.connection_grants` `(organisation_id, connection_id) where revoked_at is null` and the grantee partial indexes.
4. **Mandatory gate:** `gov.clearances` partial uniques by membership or principal; `gov.resource_markings` per-arm partial uniques; `iam.object_type_markings` primary key; `gov.artefact_markings` partial unique by node.
5. **Field policy lookup at compile:** `iam.field_policies` `(organisation_id, connection_id, field_path) where retired_at is null` and `(organisation_id, property_id)`.
6. **Lineage traversal:** `gov.lineage_edges` `(organisation_id, from_node_id, relation)` and `(organisation_id, to_node_id, relation)`, with `gov.lineage_nodes` unique `(organisation_id, kind, ref_id, version)` as entry point.
# Platform and audit schemas: build-ready design

Schemas `audit` and `platform`. Spec chapters 5 to 13 (part-02), 63 and 64 (part-09), 2.6 (part-01). Global rules are in `00_conventions.md` and are not repeated here except where this domain departs from them.

Tables (13): `audit.auth_events`, `audit.audit_events`, `audit.chain_heads`, `audit.partition_seals`, `platform.cells`, `platform.operators`, `platform.operator_access_sessions`, `platform.outbox`, `platform.model_calls`, `platform.tenant_migrations`, `platform.tenant_migration_tables`, `platform.org_exports`, `platform.org_export_items`.

## Relationships

- `audit.audit_events.(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`, or `service_principal_id → iam.service_principals`, or `operator_id → platform.operators`, or `system_service` (exclusive arc).
- `audit.audit_events.(organisation_id, operator_access_session_id) → platform.operator_access_sessions` (every request made under break-glass carries the session).
- `audit.audit_events.(organisation_id, purpose_session_id) → gov.purpose_sessions`.
- `audit.audit_events.source_event_id` equals `platform.outbox.id` of the row that produced it (idempotency key, not an FK).
- `audit.chain_heads.(organisation_id) → iam.organisations` and its head hash equals the `row_hash` of `audit.audit_events` at `last_chain_seq`.
- `platform.operator_access_sessions.operator_id → platform.operators`; `(organisation_id, approved_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
- `platform.tenant_migrations.source_cell_id, destination_cell_id → platform.cells`; `iam.organisations.cell_id → platform.cells`; `directory.organisation_directory.cell_id → directory.cells (id)` (the directory database's own copy of the cells registry; Changed (review 2026-10-28): was named `iam.organisation_directory` and pointed at `platform.cells`).
- `platform.tenant_migration_tables.(organisation_id, migration_id) → platform.tenant_migrations`.
- `platform.org_exports.(organisation_id, requested_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `platform.org_export_items.(organisation_id, export_id) → platform.org_exports`; `platform.org_export_items.(organisation_id, omitted_marking_id) → gov.markings`.
- `platform.model_calls.correlation_id` joins to `audit.audit_events.correlation_id` and to `billing.token_transactions` (no FK, ledger to ledger).

## Decisions that depart from or extend the spec

1. Ch 63.6 `operator_access_grants` and ch 13.3 `operator_access_sessions` are one table: `platform.operator_access_sessions`. The ch 13.3 vocabulary (purpose, level metadata_read, tenant_read, tenant_act, two staff approvers, customer approval by policy, recording reference, resource count) replaces the ch 63.6 levels. The ch 63.6 sentence "no level reads record values" conflicts with `tenant_read`; this design follows ch 13.3 and the brief. Every other part of the old table is kept. The old `audit.operator_access_grants` is not created.
2. Operator access moves from schema `audit` to `platform`, as the brief directs. The audit trail of access is still the events `operator_access_*` in `audit.audit_events`.
3. `audit.audit_events` is sub-partitioned: list on `retention_class`, then range by month on `occurred_at`. The spec's open decision proposes seven years for administration events and 400 days for high-volume events. Retention is a partition drop, so the two classes must live in different partitions. The primary key therefore carries both partition keys (see the table). If the decision is later made uniform, all rows use class `standard` and nothing else changes.
4. Cell-level and release-level events (`cell_created`, `cell_placement_closed`, `directory_entry_changed`, all Fleet `release_*` and `rollout_*` events) have no organisation. They are written by fleet-control and the directory to their own logs, not to `audit.audit_events`, which stays tenant-scoped with `organisation_id not null`. Events that name an organisation (`tenant_placed`, `tenant_migration_*`, `tenant_source_purged`) are written here.
5. Fleet (ch 11) and the Silo Agent (ch 10) name no tables in the spec chapters in my domain. Release registry, channels, waves and artefacts live in fleet-control in the global tier; agents, pools and certificates are covered by the Connect domain. No Fleet or agent tables are defined here.
6. `credential_unwraps` is listed in `00_conventions.md` as `iam.credential_unwraps`, and `policy_versions` belongs to identity. Neither is defined here, though the stress test lists them under platform. The identity author must define both.
7. Convention extension requested: one extra database role, `silo_outbox_relay`, with `select` and `update` (columns `published_at`, `attempts`, `next_attempt_at`, `last_error_category`, `dead_lettered_at`) on `platform.outbox` only. The relay must read across organisations, which `silo_app` cannot do under RLS, and the spec forbids giving `silo_app` bypass. Details under `platform.outbox`.

---

## Schema audit

### `audit.auth_events`
Purpose: append-only ledger of authentication and administration events written by the auth path (login, lockout, MFA, sessions, membership, scopes, roles, grants, federation, seats). Spec chapter 63.1.
Columns:
- `id` bigint, not null, `generated always as identity`. Changed: spec says bigserial; conventions require identity on ledgers.
- `occurred_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Partition key. Spec: "indexed with organisation".
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null. Login routing resolves the organisation before the cell is called, so it is always known.
- `user_id` uuid, null. Set for authentication events. Null for `login_failed` against an unknown address (no plaintext email is ever stored).
- `membership_id` uuid, null. The acting membership when one exists.
- `service_principal_id` uuid, null. Spec: new in this version. The acting principal for non-human events.
- `event` text, not null. From the chapter 77 catalogue. No check list (about 570 values); validated against the registry at write time. Spec chapter 63.3 lists the authentication and administration set.
- `detail` jsonb, not null, default `'{}'`. References and counts only, schema-validated per event. Check: `jsonb_typeof(detail) = 'object'` and `octet_length(detail::text) <= 65536`.
