- `ip_hash` bytea, null. Keyed hash of the client address. Check: length 32 when not null.
- `correlation_id` uuid, null. Added: ties an event to the request that raised it.
Keys: primary key `(id, occurred_at)`. `unique (organisation_id, id, occurred_at)` (partition key must be included; the standard `unique (organisation_id, id)` cannot be declared on a partitioned ledger).
References: `(organisation_id)` → `iam.organisations(id)`; `user_id → iam.users(id)` (users are not a tenant table, plain FK); `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals`. Check: `num_nonnulls(membership_id, service_principal_id) <= 1`. User and membership may both be set; membership and principal never both.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, occurred_at desc)`: Governance page log, default sort.
- `(organisation_id, event, occurred_at desc)`: reviewer filter by event, and the "read first" events (`admin_delegated`, `scope_moved` and the other four).
- `(organisation_id, user_id, occurred_at desc) where user_id is not null`: a member's login history and lockout review.
- `(organisation_id, membership_id, occurred_at desc) where membership_id is not null`: audit export filtered by membership.
- `(organisation_id, service_principal_id) where service_principal_id is not null`: "service principals run" in the access log (FK index).
- BRIN on `occurred_at`: partition scans for sealing and export.
Security: RLS standard. Append-only (trigger rejects update and delete; grants `insert, select` to `silo_audit_writer`, `select` to `silo_app`). Written by the auth service through `silo_audit_writer`, inside the transaction that sets `app.org_id`. Partitioned monthly by `occurred_at`; each closed partition gets a row in `audit.partition_seals`. Retention: seven years by default (open decision, ch 63.4); partition drop by `silo_migrate`, recorded as counts only. No row-level hash chain on this table: several auth pods write concurrently and a per-row chain would serialise login. Tamper detection is the partition seal.

### `audit.audit_events`
Purpose: the main append-only ledger of every product, governance, platform and operator audit event, written from the durable bus. Spec chapters 8.1, 7.5 (audit service), 63.1, 63.3, 63.6, 13.5.
Columns:
- `id` bigint, not null, `generated always as identity`.
- `occurred_at` timestamptz, not null. Time of the originating transaction (copied from `platform.outbox.created_at`), not of insertion. Partition key.
- `retention_class` text, not null, default `'standard'`. Values: `standard` (seven years), `high_volume` (400 days: query events, `host_probed`, and any event the catalogue marks high volume). Set from the catalogue by the audit writer. Sub-partition key. Added.
- `source_event_id` uuid, not null. The `platform.outbox.id` that carried the event. Consumers are idempotent on it (bus-durable is at least once). Added.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `event` text, not null. Chapter 77 catalogue name. No check list; the Zod registry rejects unknown events and rejects any schema containing a record-value type.
- `membership_id` uuid, null. Actor arm 1.
- `service_principal_id` uuid, null. Actor arm 2.
- `operator_id` uuid, null. Actor arm 3: Silo staff acting under break-glass. Added.
- `system_service` text, null. Actor arm 4: a named service acting on its own (expiry sweeps, schedulers, `approval_expired`, retention). Added because several spec events have no human or principal actor. Check: value is one of the service names in chapter 7.
- Check: `num_nonnulls(membership_id, service_principal_id, operator_id, system_service) = 1`.
- `subject_membership_id` uuid, null. The membership acted upon, where the event has one (`member_suspended`, `role_granted`, `clearance_granted`). Added.
- `scope_id` uuid, null. The scope the event concerns. Needed for "admins for their subtree" and for export filtered by scope (ch 63.5, 63.7). Added.
- `resource_type` text, null. Spec column. Descriptive name of the subject table, for example `connection`, `artefact`, `receipt`.
- `resource_id` uuid, null. Spec column. Documented exception to the exclusive-arc rule: the ledger records history of about 570 event types across most tables, rows must survive the purge of the thing they describe, and a foreign key would block retention. Integrity is held by the schema registry (type and id are validated per event) and by the rule that ledgers carry no FKs into live data other than actors and sessions. Check: `(resource_type is null) = (resource_id is null)`.
- `purpose_session_id` uuid, null. Spec column. The declared purpose in force.
- `operator_access_session_id` uuid, null. The break-glass session the request was tagged with (ch 13.3). Added.
- `correlation_id` uuid, not null. Spec column. Request-wide id shared with `platform.model_calls`, receipts and traces.
- `detail` jsonb, not null, default `'{}'`. References and counts only (plan id, types, connection ids, row counts, receipt id, byte counts). Check: object, `octet_length(detail::text) <= 65536` (bus-durable message limit). Never values.
- `ip_hash` bytea, null. Length 32 when set. Kept for parity with `auth_events`.
- `chain_seq` bigint, not null. Position in the organisation's hash chain, starting at 1. Added.
- `prev_hash` bytea, not null. `row_hash` of the previous event in the same organisation; for `chain_seq = 1`, SHA-256 of the organisation id bytes. Length 32. Added.
- `row_hash` bytea, not null. SHA-256 over `prev_hash` plus a canonical serialisation of every other column except `id`, `recorded_at` and `row_hash`. Length 32. Added. Changed (implementation 2026-10-29): the serialisation is fixed as SHA-256 of the bytes `silo.audit_events.v1`, a zero byte, `prev_hash`, then RFC 8785 canonical JSON of every other column keyed by column name, with timestamps as UTC ISO 8601 with six fractional digits and `Z`, bytea as lowercase hex and `chain_seq` as a decimal string (`app/server/src/utils/auditChain.util.ts`). A closed partition's seal is a running SHA-256 over its rows' digests in `id` order, starting from SHA-256 of `silo.partition_seal.v1`.
- `recorded_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Insertion time, to measure bus lag (alert at 5 minutes). Added.
Keys: primary key `(id, retention_class, occurred_at)` (Postgres requires every partition key in the key; this departs from the convention of `(id, occurred_at)` for the reason in Decision 3). `unique (organisation_id, source_event_id, retention_class, occurred_at)` (Changed (implementation 2026-10-28, D19): Postgres requires every partition key of every level in a unique key, so `retention_class` is included; the class is fixed per event, so a redelivery still collides) (idempotent redelivery; `occurred_at` is identical on redelivery). `unique (organisation_id, chain_seq, retention_class, occurred_at)` (Changed (implementation 2026-10-28, D19): includes `retention_class` for the same reason; `chain_seq` is assigned by the single writer under an advisory lock, so this key is a backstop).
References:
- `(organisation_id)` → `iam.organisations(id)`.
- `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
- `(organisation_id, service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals`.
- `operator_id → platform.operators(id)` (operators are not a tenant table, plain FK).
- `(organisation_id, subject_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
- `(organisation_id, scope_id) → iam.scopes`.
- `(organisation_id, purpose_session_id) → gov.purpose_sessions`.
- `(organisation_id, operator_access_session_id) → platform.operator_access_sessions`.
- Exclusive arc for the actor is the check above.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, occurred_at desc)`: Governance page default list.
- `(organisation_id, event, occurred_at desc)`: reviewer filter by event, "read first" events, `operator_access_started`, `agent_write_grant_refused`, `tenant_migration_completed`.
- `(organisation_id, membership_id, occurred_at desc) where membership_id is not null`: export and view filtered by membership (ch 63.5).
- `(organisation_id, scope_id, occurred_at desc) where scope_id is not null`: scope admins' subtree view and export by scope.
- `(organisation_id, resource_type, resource_id, occurred_at desc) where resource_id is not null`: history of one resource (artefact opened, connection changed), and the "resources touched" list.
- `(organisation_id, correlation_id)`: trace one request from a receipt or model call to its events.
- `(organisation_id, service_principal_id, occurred_at desc) where service_principal_id is not null`: "service principals run" in the access log (FK index).
- `(organisation_id, purpose_session_id) where purpose_session_id is not null`: "purpose sessions declared" and per-session audit (FK index).
- `(organisation_id, operator_access_session_id) where operator_access_session_id is not null`: customer view of every resource an operator touched; used to maintain `resources_touched_count` (FK index).
- `(organisation_id, subject_membership_id) where subject_membership_id is not null`: events about one member (FK index).
- `(organisation_id, chain_seq desc)`: the writer finds the previous hash with `limit 1`; the verifier walks the chain. Covered by the unique constraint on `(organisation_id, chain_seq, occurred_at)`, so no separate index.
- BRIN on `occurred_at`: seal and export scans.
Security: RLS standard. Append-only: trigger rejects update and delete; `silo_audit_writer` has `insert, select`; `silo_app` has `select` only. Written by the audit service only, consuming `audit.events` from bus-durable (ordering key `organisation_id`, so one consumer per organisation at a time, which makes the chain single-writer). The consumer sets `app.org_id` per batch, takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on the organisation, reads the latest `row_hash`, then inserts the batch in order. Partitioned list on `retention_class`, then monthly on `occurred_at`; every closed monthly partition is sealed in `audit.partition_seals`. Retention is a partition drop by `silo_migrate` through an audited job. Cancellation: audit is exported to the customer and purged, recorded as counts only (ch 63.4). Reads honour the reader's markings through the policy service; rows whose resource the reviewer cannot see are returned with `resource_type` and `resource_id` withheld and counted (ch 63.5). An audit write failure aborts the originating change because the event is in the outbox in the same transaction (see `platform.outbox`).
Event families written here, with the events this domain adds: `tenant_placed`, `tenant_migration_requested`, `tenant_migration_approved`, `tenant_migration_started`, `tenant_migration_completed`, `tenant_migration_aborted`, `tenant_source_purged` (ch 6.7); `operator_access_requested`, `operator_access_approved`, `operator_access_denied`, `operator_access_started`, `operator_access_resource_touched`, `operator_access_ended`, `operator_access_expired`, `operator_access_emergency` (ch 13.5 and 63.6; the emergency event is kept from ch 63.6), `redaction_violation_detected`, `incident_declared`, `incident_resolved`, `audit_chain_head_published` (ch 13.5); `org_export_requested`, `org_export_completed` (ch 2.6); `model_call_made`, `model_call_refused` (ch 62.8).

### `audit.chain_heads`
Purpose: one row per organisation per day recording the closing hash-chain head, which is published to the customer's audit view. Spec chapters 13.4, 63.1 ("daily hash-chain head published to the customer's audit view"). Added, because the spec requires the head to be published but defines no storage.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. UUIDv7.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `head_date` date, not null. UTC day closed.
- `last_chain_seq` bigint, not null. Highest `audit_events.chain_seq` for the organisation at close.
- `head_hash` bytea, not null. `row_hash` of that event. Length 32.
- `event_count` bigint, not null. Events recorded that day.
- `closed_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `published_at` timestamptz, null. When shown on the customer's audit view; set with the `audit_chain_head_published` event.
Keys: primary key `id`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, head_date)`.
References: `(organisation_id) → iam.organisations(id)`.
Indexes:
- The unique `(organisation_id, head_date)` serves the Governance page (latest heads, backward scan) and the daily close job. No further index.
Security: RLS standard. Insert-only apart from setting `published_at` once (trigger allows only null to value on that column); grants `insert, select, update (published_at)` to `silo_audit_writer`, `select` to `silo_app`. Written by the audit service's daily close job. No partitioning (one row per organisation per day); retention follows audit retention and is removed with organisation purge by `silo_migrate`.

### `audit.partition_seals`
Purpose: running hash and row count written when a ledger partition closes, so removal of a row from a closed partition is detectable; also gives reviewers the partition hashes in exports. Spec chapter 63.1 and 63.5. Added.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. UUIDv7.
- `ledger` text, not null. Values: `audit.auth_events`, `audit.audit_events`, `platform.model_calls`, `iam.credential_unwraps`.
- `partition_name` text, not null. For `audit.audit_events` this is the leaf (class plus month).
- `range_start` timestamptz, not null.
- `range_end` timestamptz, not null.
- `row_count` bigint, not null.
- `running_hash` bytea, not null. SHA-256 chained over rows in primary key order, computed at close. Length 32.
- `sealed_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `dropped_at` timestamptz, null. Set when retention drops the partition; the seal row stays as the record that the drop was lawful and complete.
Keys: primary key `id`; `unique (ledger, partition_name)`.
References: none (not a tenant table; no `organisation_id`).
Indexes: the unique constraint serves the sealing job (is this partition sealed). `(ledger, range_start)`: reviewer export selects the seals for a period (ch 63.5).
Security: not under RLS; it holds no tenant data, only table names, counts and hashes (the migration check exempts it by name, as it does `permissions`). Grants: `silo_audit_writer` has `insert, select`; `dropped_at` is set by `silo_migrate` only. `silo_app` has `select`. Trigger rejects any other update and all deletes. Written by the sealing job at the first run after a partition's range ends. Not partitioned.

---

## Schema platform

### `platform.cells`
Purpose: registry of cells with residency, hostname, whether placement is open and daily counts. Spec chapters 6.1, 6.2, 6.3. Identified by the stress test as missing.
Columns:
- `id` text, not null. Primary key. The cell identifier, such as `uk-lon-1`, `eu-fra-1`, `us-va-1`, `uk-sov-1`, `ded-<name>`. Check `id ~ '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$'`. This is what hostnames and OAuth callbacks encode, and the value held in `iam.organisations.cell_id` and `directory.organisation_directory.cell_id`. Changed (review 2026-10-28): replaces `id uuid` and the separate `code` column. A documented exception to the UUIDv7 rule: cell identity is shared across databases and appears in hostnames and OAuth callbacks.
- `kind` text, not null. Check: `commercial`, `sovereign`, `dedicated`, `self_managed`. Changed (review 2026-10-28): `self_managed` added for customer-run installs (build rules, Deployment modes).
- `residency` text, not null. Check: `uk`, `eu`, `us`, plus any contracted residency added by migration (open set; the check lists the current three and is extended by Fleet).
- `location` text, not null. For example `London, GCP europe-west2`.
- `hosting` text, not null. Check: `gke`, `conformant_kubernetes`, `customer_cloud`, `customer_premises`.
- `hostname` text, not null. Base hostname of the cell. Unique.
- `placement_open` boolean, not null, default false. Opens only after the synthetic tenant lifecycle passes (ch 6.3).
- `organisation_limit` integer, not null, default 2000. `connection_limit` integer, not null, default 50000. Placement limits (ch 6.3). Added.
- `organisation_count` integer, not null, default 0. `connection_count` integer, not null, default 0. `counts_at` timestamptz, null. Daily counts (ch 6.1). Meaningful for the local cell only; other rows carry the last registry push.
- `is_local` boolean, not null, default false. True for the row describing the cell this database belongs to. Added. Partial unique index guarantees one local row.
- `status` text, not null, default `provisioning`. Check: `provisioning`, `active`, `closed_to_placement`, `draining`, `retired`. Added.
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Optimistic lock for Fleet configuration pushes. Added.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `hostname`. Changed (review 2026-10-28): unique `code` removed with the column. No `organisation_id`, so not a tenant table.
References: none.
Indexes:
- `unique (is_local) where is_local` : exactly one local cell.
- `(residency, kind) where placement_open` : placement picks the open cell in a residency with most headroom (ch 6.4); the table is small, the index documents the query and is the only one.
Security: not under RLS (global registry, no tenant data; ch 6.2). `silo_app` has `select`; written by `silo_migrate` during Fleet releases and by the cell lifecycle job for counts (`update (organisation_count, connection_count, counts_at)` granted to `silo_app`). The same definition exists in the directory database, where it holds all cells. In a commercial cell it holds the full registry delivered with the release configuration so migration source and destination resolve by FK. In a sovereign cell it holds the local cell and sovereign destinations only; no sovereign data flows to the shared directory. Retired cells are never deleted.

### `platform.operators`
Purpose: Silo staff identities known to a cell, referenced by break-glass sessions and operator audit events. Spec chapter 13.3, 13.4, 63.6 ("Silo staff identity in the cell's operator directory"). Stress test: no operators table.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. UUIDv7.
- `idp_subject` text, not null. Subject of the staff identity provider. Unique. No email or password is held.
- `display_name` text, not null. Shown to the customer in the access log ("the named person").
- `clearance` text, not null. Check: `bpss`, `sc`, `dv`. Personnel vetting, ch 65.4.
- `uk_resident` boolean, not null.
- `sovereign_access_listed` boolean, not null, default false. On the sovereign access list. Check: true requires `uk_resident` and `clearance in ('sc','dv')`.
- `status` text, not null, default `active`. Check: `active`, `suspended`, `removed`.
- `last_reviewed_at` timestamptz, null. Quarterly access review (ch 13.4). `last_reviewed_by` uuid, null → `platform.operators(id)`. Added.
- `removed_at` timestamptz, null. Set on departure; the row is never deleted because sessions and audit reference it.
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `id`; unique `idp_subject`.
References: `last_reviewed_by → platform.operators(id)`.
Indexes:
- `unique (idp_subject)`: staff sign-in lookup.
- `(last_reviewed_at) where status = 'active'`: the quarterly review sweep lists operators overdue.
Security: not under RLS (no `organisation_id`; one directory per cell). It holds no customer data. `silo_app` has `select`; only admin-portal writes (`insert, update`). No `delete` grant. Customer-facing pages never join this table: names are copied to the session row (see below).

### `platform.operator_access_sessions`
Purpose: customer-visible break-glass sessions by which a named Silo operator accesses one organisation; replaces `operator_access_grants`. Spec chapters 13.3, 13.5, 63.6, 63.7, 6.5 (sovereign variants).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. UUIDv7.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `operator_id` uuid, not null → `platform.operators`. The requesting operator (spec: `operator_id`).
- `operator_display_name` text, not null. Snapshot of the name at request time so the tenant view needs no join to `platform.operators`. Added.
- `purpose` text, not null. Check: `support_request`, `incident_response`, `legal_obligation`, `security_investigation`.
- `access_level` text, not null. Check: `metadata_read`, `tenant_read`, `tenant_act`. Changed: replaces `metadata_only`, `connection_diagnostics` (Decision 1). No level permits unwrapping credentials or approving an Action, enforced in policy.
- `reason` text, not null. Kept from spec. Free text, no record values (admin-portal rejects value patterns).
- `ticket_reference` text, not null. Support ticket or incident id. Added from ch 13.3 ("reason, ticket, scope, duration"); the spec's `reason` described a ticket reference, so both are kept.
- `scope_note` text, null. Scope requested, in words. Added from ch 13.3.
- `status` text, not null, default `requested`. Check: `requested`, `approved`, `denied`, `active`, `ended`, `expired`, `cancelled`. Added.
- `requested_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `emergency` boolean, not null, default false. Kept. When true, `staff_second_approver_operator_id` is required and the customer's super admins are notified at once (`operator_access_emergency`).
- `customer_approval_required` boolean, not null. Snapshot of `org.operator_access.policy` and the contract at request time; always true for sovereign cells. Added.
- `staff_approver_operator_id` uuid, null → `platform.operators`. The second staff approval. `staff_approved_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
- `staff_second_approver_operator_id` uuid, null → `platform.operators`. Emergency only. Added.
- `approved_by_membership_id` uuid, null. Kept. Customer super admin or named security contact who approved. Null only when `customer_approval_required` is false or `emergency` is true.
- `customer_decided_at` timestamptz, null. `denied_reason` text, null. Added.
- `starts_at` timestamptz, null. `expires_at` timestamptz, null. Set on approval.
- `ended_at` timestamptz, null. `ended_reason` text, null. Check: `ended`, `expired`, `revoked`. Added.
- `recording_reference` text, null. Object key of the session recording in object-backup (terminal sessions, ch 13.3). `recording_retained_until` timestamptz, null (12 months). Added.
- `resources_touched_count` integer, not null, default 0. Maintained from `operator_access_resource_touched` events. Added from ch 13.3.
- `created_at` is `requested_at`; `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Checks:
- Operator distinctness: `staff_approver_operator_id`, `staff_second_approver_operator_id` and `operator_id` pairwise different when set.
- Window: when `starts_at` is set, `expires_at > starts_at` and `expires_at - starts_at <= interval '4 hours'`.
- Approvals: `status in ('approved','active','ended','expired')` requires `staff_approver_operator_id` not null; plus `approved_by_membership_id` not null unless `customer_approval_required = false` or `emergency`; plus second approver when `emergency`.
- Level: `access_level = 'tenant_act'` requires `customer_approval_required` true or `emergency` false. Sovereign cell sessions require the operator's `sovereign_access_listed`, enforced by the service because it spans two tables.
Keys: primary key `id`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id) → iam.organisations(id)`; `operator_id`, `staff_approver_operator_id`, `staff_second_approver_operator_id → platform.operators(id)`; `(organisation_id, approved_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, requested_at desc)`: the tenant's operator access list on the Governance page.
- `(organisation_id, status) where status in ('requested','approved','active')`: pending approvals shown to super admins and the "is anyone in the tenant now" check.
- `(expires_at) where status = 'active'`: expiry sweep that ends sessions at the bound and emits `operator_access_expired`.
- `(organisation_id, operator_id)`: FK index; per-operator history for the quarterly review.
- `(organisation_id, approved_by_membership_id) where approved_by_membership_id is not null`: FK index.
Security: RLS standard (visible to the tenant, as the spec requires). Writers: admin-portal creates and advances staff steps (it sets `app.org_id` of the target organisation); the governance API updates only the customer decision columns (`approved_by_membership_id`, `customer_decided_at`, `denied_reason`) on behalf of a holder of `org.operator_access.approve`. Rows are never deleted. Each status change emits its `operator_access_*` event through the outbox in the same transaction. Every request made during a session is tagged with the session id in `audit.audit_events.operator_access_session_id`. `silo_report` may read the replica only for an organisation with an active session (policy in admin-portal; the database role is unchanged).

### `platform.outbox`
Purpose: transactional outbox; a service that changes pg-control writes its durable event here in the same transaction and a relay publishes it to bus-durable. Spec chapters 9.2, 7.5, 12.2, 12.4.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. UUIDv7. This is the event identifier consumers dedupe on and becomes `audit_events.source_event_id`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Partition key (daily). Becomes `audit_events.occurred_at`. Use `transaction_timestamp()` so it equals the change's commit time basis.
- `seq` bigint, not null, `generated always as identity`. Strictly increasing publish order across the table; the relay publishes per `ordering_key` in `seq` order. Not a key. Added.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `topic` text, not null. Check: `audit.events`, `metering.usage`, `control.policy`, `control.connection`, `control.agent`, `control.action`, `siloes.capture`. (`control.release` is published by Fleet, not by pg-control.)
- `ordering_key` text, not null. The bus ordering key as text: the organisation id for `audit.events`, `metering.usage`, `control.policy`, `siloes.capture`; the connection id for `control.connection`; the agent id for `control.agent`; the action id for `control.action`. This is a routing value, not a reference.
- `event` text, not null. Event name from the catalogue.
- `schema_version` integer, not null, default 1. Version of the registered Zod schema.
- `payload` jsonb, not null. References and counts only. Check: object, `octet_length(payload::text) <= 65536` (64 KB bus-durable limit). The producer client refuses a payload that fails its schema before insert.
- `correlation_id` uuid, not null.
- `published_at` timestamptz, null. Set by the relay on broker acknowledgement.
- `attempts` integer, not null, default 0. `next_attempt_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. `last_error_category` text, null (category only; broker or driver messages can carry values). Backoff state.
- `dead_lettered_at` timestamptz, null. Set when 7 days pass unacknowledged (ch 9.1); raises an alert.
Keys: primary key `(id, created_at)`. `unique (organisation_id, id, created_at)`.
References: `(organisation_id) → iam.organisations(id)`.
Indexes (all partial on unpublished rows, because the table is mostly published rows):
- `(organisation_id, seq) where published_at is null and dead_lettered_at is null`: relay drains one organisation in order; producers count pending rows per organisation against the declared bound ("at their bound, writes stop", ch 7.5, 12.4).
- `(next_attempt_at, seq) where published_at is null and dead_lettered_at is null`: global relay sweep of due rows.
- `(created_at) where published_at is null`: oldest-pending age; pages on-call when `audit.events` backlog exceeds 5 minutes (ch 9.4).
Security: RLS standard for `silo_app` (services insert under the transaction's `app.org_id`). Changed (implementation 2026-10-28, D21): no second policy. The relay works only through three `security definer` functions owned by `silo_migrate`, with `execute` granted to `silo_outbox_relay`: `platform.outbox_claim(limit, lease)` claims the head of each ordering key (so events of one key publish strictly in sequence, using a partial index on `(topic, ordering_key, seq)`), `platform.outbox_mark_published(ids, created_ats)`, and `platform.outbox_mark_failed(...)`, which dead-letters after 7 days; and (D197) `platform.outbox_backlog()`, what waits to be published (up to 100,000) and the oldest's age, which the relay reports to the cell's Fleet agent for its audit outbox gate. The relay holds no table privilege, so it cannot run arbitrary queries across organisations. (Superseded text: a second policy `relay_sweep` for `silo_outbox_relay`, `using (true)`; the relay reads all organisations and updates publication state, nothing else (Decision 7). Not append-only (publication columns update). Partitioned daily by `created_at`; the partition drop is run by `silo_migrate` only after all rows in it are published or dead-lettered, 14 days after the day ends; a partition with unpublished rows is never dropped and raises an alert. The per-organisation bound and the per-cell total bound are cell configuration visible to the customer; overflow refuses the producer, which fails the originating change. Written by every service.

### `platform.model_calls`
Purpose: append-only metadata of every model call (tokens, model, prompt hash), never prompt text or output, which settles measured cost per compile. Spec chapters 7.5, 7.8, 62.8, 8.5.
Columns:
- `id` bigint, not null, `generated always as identity`.
- `occurred_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Partition key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `call_id` uuid, not null. Idempotency id issued by model-gateway; a retried delivery cannot double count. Added.
- `correlation_id` uuid, not null. Joins all calls of one compile or one FDE task, and the audit events and `billing.token_transactions` rows of the same request.
- `caller_service` text, not null. Check: `compile`, `resolution`, `recognition`, `fde-orchestrator`, `siloes-import`, `connect-registry` (the callers named in ch 7.5).
- `request_type` text, not null. Check: `vocabulary`, `document_extraction` (ch 7.8). Document extraction is the carve-out and is only possible when the organisation enabled it.
- `model` text, not null. Model identifier as returned by the provider or self-hosted deployment.
- `model_route` text, not null. Fleet route name (routes never leave the residency). Added.
- `input_tokens` integer, not null. `output_tokens` integer, not null. `thinking_tokens` integer, not null, default 0. Each `>= 0`.
- `prompt_hash` bytea, not null. SHA-256 of the assembled prompt. Length 32. Never the prompt.
- `outcome` text, not null. Check: `ok`, `refused`, `error`. Refused corresponds to `model_call_refused`.
- `refusal_category` text, null. Check when set: `redaction_match`, `record_value_field`, `concurrency_bound`, `length_bound`, `extraction_not_enabled`. Required when `outcome = 'refused'`. Added.
- `latency_ms` integer, null. Added.
- `provider_cost` numeric(14,8), null. Added (D106): what the provider charges for the call at its route's prices (input, and output with thinking, per million tokens, from the route's configuration); null where the route names no price, so an unpriced call is never counted as free.
Note: the document extraction file reference and byte count live in the `extraction_carveout_used` audit event, not here, so this table stays value-free.
Keys: primary key `(id, occurred_at)`; `unique (organisation_id, call_id, occurred_at)`.
References: `(organisation_id) → iam.organisations(id)`. No other FKs (ledger).
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, correlation_id)`: measured cost per compile (sum tokens by correlation id) and reconciliation with metering.
- `(organisation_id, occurred_at desc)`: per-organisation usage list and daily token limits check (ch 7.5 metering).
- BRIN on `occurred_at`: cell-wide cost reports by model and route.
Security: RLS standard. Append-only (trigger rejects update and delete). Written by model-gateway only; grants `insert, select` to `silo_audit_writer` (model-gateway writes through it so the ledger shares the audit grants), `select` to `silo_app` and `silo_report`. Partitioned monthly by `occurred_at`; sealed in `audit.partition_seals`; retention follows audit retention for cost analysis (default 13 months, an assumption pending the retention decision) by partition drop. Never contains prompts, completions, document contents or record values (a value here is a SEV1, ch 8.5).

### `platform.tenant_migrations`
Purpose: one row per cell-to-cell move of an organisation, with approvals, window, stage timestamps and checksums at both ends. Spec chapter 6.4, 6.7.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. UUIDv7.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `source_cell_id` text, not null → `platform.cells (id)`. `destination_cell_id` text, not null → `platform.cells (id)`. Check: different. Changed (review 2026-10-28): uuid to text, because cells are keyed by the text cell identifier.
- `reason` text, not null. Check: `residency_change`, `rebalancing`, `promotion_dedicated`, `promotion_sovereign` (the three permitted reasons, with promotion split by target).
- `status` text, not null, default `requested`. Check, in order: `requested`, `approved`, `scheduled`, `read_only`, `exporting`, `importing`, `verifying`, `reauthorising`, `directory_updated`, `source_read_only`, `source_purged`, `completed`, `aborted`. Mirrors the stage list in ch 6.4.
- `requested_by_membership_id` uuid, not null → memberships. Holder of `org.migration.request` (super admin).
- `approved_by_membership_id` uuid, null → memberships. Holder of `org.migration.approve`; required for `rebalancing`, residency change and promotion.
- `security_officer_operator_id` uuid, null → `platform.operators`. Required for `residency_change`. `sovereign_security_officer_operator_id` uuid, null → operators. Required for `promotion_sovereign`.
- `notice_given_at` timestamptz, null. Required for `rebalancing` (30 days' notice). `customer_objected_at` timestamptz, null; `objection_note` text, null. Added.
- `window_starts_at` timestamptz, null; `window_ends_at` timestamptz, null. The approved window.
- `read_only_at`, `export_started_at`, `export_completed_at`, `import_started_at`, `import_completed_at`, `verified_at`, `connections_reauthorised_at`, `directory_updated_at` timestamptz, null. Stage timestamps. Added.
- `source_read_only_until` timestamptz, null. Set to `directory_updated_at + 30 days`. `source_purged_at` timestamptz, null. `purge_receipt_object_key` text, null. Added from "source purge with receipt".
- `bundle_object_key` text, null; `bundle_checksum` bytea, null, length 32 (SHA-256 of the encrypted bundle); `destination_key_id` text, null (identifier of the destination import key; the key itself is never stored). Added.
- `connections_pending_reauthorisation` integer, null. Count of connections left to re-authorise. Credentials are never migrated (ch 6.4). Added.
- `aborted_at` timestamptz, null; `abort_reason` text, null (category). `completed_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Checks: reason-specific approvals as above; `completed` requires `verified_at`, `directory_updated_at` and every `tenant_migration_tables.matched = true` (enforced by the migration service, which updates status only after reading the child rows); the sovereign source forbids a commercial destination unless `approved_by_membership_id` is set (customer's written instruction), checked by the service across the two cell rows.
Keys: primary key `id`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; partial unique `(organisation_id) where status not in ('completed','aborted')`: one live migration per organisation.
References: `(organisation_id) → iam.organisations(id)`; `source_cell_id`, `destination_cell_id → platform.cells(id)`; `(organisation_id, requested_by_membership_id)`, `(organisation_id, approved_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `security_officer_operator_id`, `sovereign_security_officer_operator_id → platform.operators(id)`.
Indexes:
- The partial unique index serves "is a migration in progress" for the write-pause (Actions and Crons check it) and the Governance page.
- `(organisation_id, created_at desc)`: migration history list.
- `(status, window_starts_at) where status in ('approved','scheduled')`: migration runner picks the next due window.
- `(source_read_only_until) where status = 'source_read_only'`: purge sweep after 30 days.
- `(organisation_id, requested_by_membership_id)`: FK index.
Security: RLS standard. Written by the migrations service (and by `silo_migrate` for export and import under `bypassrls`, which also holds the destination copy). The source cell holds the authoritative row; the destination receives a copy inside the bundle and fills its own counts. Receipts and audit move with the tenant; this row is part of what moves. Status changes emit the `tenant_migration_*` events. Not append-only. Retained indefinitely with audit.

### `platform.tenant_migration_tables`
Purpose: per-table row counts and checksums at both ends of a migration, so `tenant_migration_completed` can show nothing was lost or added. Spec chapter 6.4 ("per-table row counts at both ends"), 6.7. Added as a child table in place of a jsonb column, so each table can be queried and constrained.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. UUIDv7.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `migration_id` uuid, not null.
- `schema_name` text, not null; `table_name` text, not null.
- `source_row_count` bigint, null; `source_checksum` bytea, null (length 32; checksum over the exported rows in primary key order). Set at export.
- `destination_row_count` bigint, null; `destination_checksum` bytea, null. Set at import verification.
- `matched` boolean, null. True when counts and checksums are equal; null until both sides are present. Check: when not null, equals the comparison.
- `verified_at` timestamptz, null. `created_at` timestamptz, not null.
Keys: primary key `id`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, migration_id, schema_name, table_name)`.
References: `(organisation_id, migration_id) → platform.tenant_migrations`.
Indexes:
- The unique key serves the per-table comparison.
- `(organisation_id, migration_id) where matched is distinct from true`: finds mismatched or unverified tables before `verified_at` can be set.
Security: RLS standard. Written by the migrations service and `silo_migrate`; only the count, checksum, `matched` and `verified_at` columns change after insert. Retained with the migration. Contains table names, counts and hashes only, no values.

### `platform.org_exports`
Purpose: organisation exit export jobs with status, contents manifest and receipt. Spec chapter 2.6; stress test: no table for export jobs.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. UUIDv7.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `requested_by_membership_id` uuid, not null. Holder of `org.export` (super admin only).
- `status` text, not null, default `requested`. Check: `requested`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`. Added.
- `billing_status_at_request` text, not null. Snapshot of `iam.organisations.billing_status`. Exports run in suspended and cancelled states within the retention window and are never withheld; the snapshot records which state applied. Added.
- `format_version` text, not null. Version of the published export schema (ontology JSON schema, manifest schema). Added.
- `clearance_snapshot_at` timestamptz, not null. Time at which the requester's clearances were resolved; markings omit what the requester cannot see ("exports respect markings"). Added.
- `requested_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`; `started_at`, `completed_at`, `failed_at` timestamptz, null.
- `failure_category` text, null. Category only, no source message.
- `manifest_object_key` text, null; `manifest_sha256` bytea, null. The contents manifest object in object-files. The same data is queryable in `platform.org_export_items`.
- `bundle_object_key` text, null; `bundle_bytes` bigint, null; `bundle_sha256` bytea, null. The assembled export archive.
- `item_count` integer, null; `omitted_item_count` integer, null. Counts of included and of marking-omitted artefacts.
- `receipt_object_key` text, null; `receipt_sha256` bytea, null; `receipt_issued_at` timestamptz, null. The receipt: counts, hashes and named omissions, issued when the job completes (`org_export_completed`).
- `created_at` is `requested_at`; `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `id`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; partial unique `(organisation_id) where status in ('requested','running')`: one export at a time per organisation.
References: `(organisation_id) → iam.organisations(id)`; `(organisation_id, requested_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, requested_at desc)`: export history list.
- The partial unique index serves "is an export already running".
- `(organisation_id, requested_by_membership_id)`: FK index.
- `(started_at) where status = 'running'`: sweep for stuck jobs.
Security: RLS standard. Written by the files/export worker (render sandbox has no network except object-files). Not append-only; terminal statuses are final (trigger rejects status change out of `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`). The bundle sits in object-files under the organisation prefix, retained indefinitely by default, and is purgeable only with an organisation purge. Emits `org_export_requested` and `org_export_completed`. A failed export event is not in the spec catalogue; it is proposed as `org_export_failed` and needs adding to chapter 77.

### `platform.org_export_items`
Purpose: one row per artefact family file in an export, with format, hash and counts, plus named omissions where a marking removed an artefact. Spec chapter 2.6 table of artefacts and the binding rule on markings. Added as the contents manifest in queryable form.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. UUIDv7.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `export_id` uuid, not null.
- `family` text, not null. Check: `connector_manifests`, `ontology`, `resolution`, `applications`, `views`, `crons`, `scenarios`, `receipts`, `audit`, `siloes_transitions`, `siloes_imports`, `siloes_index`. (Receipts and audit are separate files, both JSON Lines.)
- `artefact_name` text, not null. Descriptive name of the artefact or file as shown in the manifest and the receipt. A snapshot for the reader, not a reference.
- `format` text, not null. Check: `yaml`, `json`, `jsonl`, `csv`, `parquet`, `original`.
- `status` text, not null. Check: `included`, `omitted_marking`.
- `omitted_marking_id` uuid, null. The marking that caused the omission. Check: not null iff `status = 'omitted_marking'`.
- `bundle_path` text, null; `object_key` text, null; `sha256` bytea, null (length 32); `bytes` bigint, null; `row_count` bigint, null. Null for omitted items; required for included items.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null.
Keys: primary key `id`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, export_id, family, artefact_name)`.
References: `(organisation_id, export_id) → platform.org_exports`; `(organisation_id, omitted_marking_id) → gov.markings`.
Indexes:
- The unique key serves the manifest listing for one export.
- `(organisation_id, omitted_marking_id) where omitted_marking_id is not null`: FK index; which exports omitted artefacts under a marking.
Security: RLS standard. Insert-only after the export job completes the item (trigger rejects update except the job's own completion fields while the parent is `running`). Written by the export worker. The omitted `artefact_name` is shown only to the requester, who is a super admin without clearance on it, as the spec requires ("named as omitted"). Contains names, hashes and counts, no record values; exported data itself stays in object-files.

---

## Hot paths

1. Governance audit list and filters: `audit.audit_events (organisation_id, occurred_at desc)`, with `(organisation_id, event, occurred_at desc)` for the "read first" events and `(organisation_id, membership_id, occurred_at desc)` for member filters.
2. Audit writer finding the previous chain hash on every insert batch: `unique (organisation_id, chain_seq, retention_class, occurred_at)` on `audit.audit_events`, read with `order by chain_seq desc limit 1`; and the idempotent redelivery check on `unique (organisation_id, source_event_id, retention_class, occurred_at)`.
3. Outbox relay: `platform.outbox (organisation_id, seq) where published_at is null and dead_lettered_at is null` for ordered drain, and `(created_at) where published_at is null` for the 5-minute backlog alarm. These also gate every producer's pending-bound check, so they sit on the write path of every change.
4. Operator access: `platform.operator_access_sessions (organisation_id, status) where status in ('requested','approved','active')` for the approval queue and active-session check, and `(expires_at) where status = 'active'` for the expiry sweep. The per-request tag lookup is by primary key.
5. Cost per compile: `platform.model_calls (organisation_id, correlation_id)`.
6. Write pause during migration: `platform.tenant_migrations` partial unique `(organisation_id) where status not in ('completed','aborted')`, read by Actions and Crons before they start.
# Schema `connect`: build-ready design

Source: spec chapters 14 to 20 (part-03.html), agent rules in chapter 10 (part-02.html), `00_conventions.md`, stress-test findings. 23 tables: the 18 in `tables.json` plus five defined here (`connectors`, `agents`, `agent_pools`, `agent_enrolment_tokens`, `connector_promotions`).

## Relationships

- `connect.connections.connector_id → connect.connectors` (catalogue reference rule below)
- `connect.connections.manifest_id → connect.connector_manifests` (current version in use)
- `connect.connector_manifests.connector_id → connect.connectors`
- `connect.connections.agent_pool_id → connect.agent_pools`
- `connect.agents.pool_id → connect.agent_pools`
- `connect.agent_pools.approved_by → iam.memberships`
- `connect.agent_rollouts.release_id → connect.agent_releases`
- `connect.agents.service_principal_id → iam.service_principals`
- `connect.connection_credentials.connection_id → connect.connections`
- `connect.connection_credentials.key_version_id → iam.kms_key_versions`
- `connect.oauth_clients.client_secret_credential_id → connect.connection_credentials`
- `connect.oauth_pending_flows.connection_id → connect.connections`
- `connect.webhook_endpoints.secret_credential_id → connect.connection_credentials`
- `connect.probe_runs`, `conformance_runs`, `heal_proposals` `.connection_id → connect.connections`; `.manifest_id → connect.connector_manifests`
- `connect.change_stream_subscriptions.cron_id → automation.automations`; `.silo_id → siloes.siloes`
- `connect.cdc_slots.agent_pool_id → connect.agent_pools`
- `connect.discovery_authorisations.agent_id → connect.agents`; `.approval_chain_id → action.approval_chains`
- `connect.discovery_runs.authorisation_id → connect.discovery_authorisations`
- `connect.discovery_findings.run_id → connect.discovery_runs`; `.ontology_proposal_id → ontology.ontology_proposals`
- `connect.discovery_probes.run_id → connect.discovery_runs`
- `connect.discovery_run_hosts.run_id → connect.discovery_runs`
- `connect.industrial_endpoints.connection_id → connect.connections`; `.agent_pool_id → connect.agent_pools`
- `connect.writable_points.connection_id → connect.connections`
- `connect.connector_promotions.connector_id → connect.connectors`
- `iam.connection_grants.connection_id → connect.connections` (table owned by `iam`, chapter 57; the grantee exclusive arc is specified in the `iam` design, not here)

## Rules that apply to the whole schema

**Catalogue reference rule (mixed global and tenant tables).** `connect.connectors` and `connect.connector_manifests` hold two kinds of row: global catalogue rows (`organisation_id` null, Silo-authored or promoted community connectors, readable by every tenant) and private rows (`organisation_id` set, visible only to that organisation). Changed: the spec put catalogue manifests under a "Silo catalogue organisation"; they now use null, which is the one marker for "global" in this schema. Added (review 2026-10-28): catalogue rows carry no secrets and use a null organisation; Silo-owned rows that carry secrets live under the system organisation (`iam.organisations.is_system`).
- A composite tenant foreign key cannot point at a global row, because `organisation_id` is null. Every column that references a connector or a manifest from a tenant table (`connections.connector_id`, `connections.manifest_id`, `oauth_clients.connector_id`, `oauth_pending_flows` via its connection, `probe_runs.manifest_id`, `conformance_runs.manifest_id`, `heal_proposals.from_manifest_id`, `writable_points.manifest_id`) is therefore a plain foreign key on `id` alone, with `on delete restrict`. This is a deliberate, documented exception to the composite-key rule, limited to these two target tables.
- Integrity that the composite key would give is supplied by one constraint trigger, `connect.assert_catalogue_visible()`, attached to each referencing table on insert and update of the referencing column: it rejects the row unless the target's `organisation_id` is null or equals the row's `organisation_id`. It also checks that a manifest belongs to the connector named in the same row where both are present. Tenant A can never reference tenant B's private connector or manifest, even by guessing a UUID.
- Within `connector_manifests`, version-to-connector integrity is a real composite key: `unique (connector_id, id)`, used by `connections` as `(connector_id, manifest_id)`.
- Policy shape for both mixed tables (RLS enabled and forced), two policies instead of the standard one:
  - Read policy (`for select`): `using (organisation_id is null or organisation_id = (select current_setting('app.org_id')::uuid))`.
  - Write policy (`for insert, update, delete`): `using (organisation_id = (select current_setting('app.org_id')::uuid)) with check (organisation_id = (select current_setting('app.org_id')::uuid))`, with the extra `connectors` check given in its section. A tenant therefore cannot insert, update or delete a global row, and cannot create a row that is global.
  - Global rows are written only by `silo_migrate` (Fleet catalogue release, Silo promotion review). No tenant-facing role has `delete` on either table; withdrawal is a status change.
  - Changed (review 2026-10-28): both policies use the scalar subquery form of the build rules.

**Sweeps.** Every scheduled sweep named below (expired flows, stale subscriptions, missed heartbeats, credential refresh, authorisation expiry) iterates organisations and runs `set local app.org_id` per organisation, never with `bypassrls`. All sweep indexes therefore lead with `organisation_id`.

**Lookups before the organisation is known.** Four entry points arrive carrying only a secret and cannot set `app.org_id` first: the OAuth callback (`state_hash`), an inbound webhook (path token hash), an agent mTLS connection (certificate fingerprint), and an agent enrolment (token hash). Each uses a `security definer` function owned by `silo_migrate`, `execute` granted to `silo_app` only, which finds the row by its globally unique secret hash and returns only the identifiers needed to set `app.org_id`. Everything after the lookup runs under normal RLS. Names: `connect.resolve_oauth_flow`, `connect.resolve_webhook`, `connect.resolve_agent`, `connect.resolve_enrolment_token`.

**Hot state kept out of Postgres.** Agent heartbeats (every 10 seconds), CDC lease renewals, and change-stream `last_delta_at` would each write one row many times a minute. The live values are held in `redis-state` (persistence disabled, chapter 9). Postgres columns for them are flushed at most once per 60 seconds and on every status change. After a state-plane restart the sweeps read the Postgres values and the live values rebuild within one heartbeat interval. Any such column carries `fillfactor 70` on its table so the updates stay heap-only.

**Retention values marked "proposed"** are not in the spec and need a product decision.

---

### `connect.connectors`

Purpose: the catalogue entry for one kind of source system; prebuilt, community or private; the thing `connections` and manifests belong to. Spec chapters 14, 16. New table (stress-test finding, critical).

Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. UUIDv7.
- `organisation_id` uuid, **null**. Null means a global catalogue row (Silo-authored prebuilt, or promoted community). Not null means a private connector owned by that organisation.
- `kind` text, not null. `prebuilt`, `community`, `private`.
- `slug` text, not null. Lower-case, `[a-z0-9-]`, stable machine name (for example `hubspot`).
- `name` text, not null. Display name.
- `provider` text, not null. Vendor or product the connector speaks to.
- `description` text, null.
- `trust_tier` text, not null. `private`, `community`, `verified`, `certified`. Promotion order private, community, verified, certified (17.1).
- `source_route` text, not null. Route the connector was built by: `catalogue`, `ai`, `visual`.
- `status` text, not null, default `draft`. `draft` (half-built, opens in the visual builder, 16.4), `active`, `deprecated`, `withdrawn`. Added.
- `author_organisation_id` uuid, null. Organisation that authored a community connector; the payee of the 70 percent marketplace share (16.5). Null for Silo-authored. For `private` it equals `organisation_id`. Added. Plain reference to `iam.organisations (id)` (the author may be a different tenant from the reader; no tenant data is exposed by the id).
- `derived_from_connector_id` uuid, null. Source connector when this row was created by promotion (private to community) or by a fork (catalogue connector copied to a private one when a tenant repair is needed, see `connect.heal_proposals`). Added.
- `derivation` text, null. `promotion`, `fork`. Set exactly when `derived_from_connector_id` is set.
- `created_by_membership_id` uuid, null. Arc member 1.
- `created_by_service_principal_id` uuid, null. Arc member 2.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Optimistic lock for concurrent edits in the builders. Added.

Changed: the spec had no table; `trust_tier` and `provider` also exist on `connections` (kept there, see that table).

Checks:
- `kind = 'private'` implies `organisation_id` not null, `trust_tier = 'private'`, `author_organisation_id = organisation_id`.
- `kind in ('prebuilt','community')` implies `organisation_id` null and `trust_tier <> 'private'`.
- `kind = 'prebuilt'` implies `author_organisation_id` null. `kind = 'community'` implies `author_organisation_id` not null.
- `(derived_from_connector_id is null) = (derivation is null)`.
- Created-by arc: if `organisation_id` is not null then `num_nonnulls(created_by_membership_id, created_by_service_principal_id) = 1`; if null then both are null (global rows are written by `silo_migrate`).

Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (id)` is the primary key and is the target of the plain references from tenant tables; `unique (organisation_id, id)` (not enforcing for global rows, kept for the composite references from `connector_promotions`); `unique (author_organisation_id, id)` (Added (review 2026-10-28): target for `billing.marketplace_payouts`).

References:
- `(organisation_id, created_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, created_by_service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals`. Both inert when `organisation_id` is null.
- `author_organisation_id → iam.organisations (id)`.
- `derived_from_connector_id → connect.connectors (id)`; catalogue reference rule trigger applies (a private row may derive only from a global row or from itself-organisation rows).

Indexes:
- Unique `(slug)` where `organisation_id is null`: one global connector per slug; serves catalogue lookup by slug.
- Unique `(organisation_id, slug)` where `organisation_id is not null`: private slug uniqueness per tenant.
- `gin (name gin_trgm_ops)`: connector picker search in the build and connect screens (conventions rule 4). Global and private rows share the index; RLS filters.
- `(trust_tier, kind)` where `organisation_id is null and status = 'active'`: catalogue browse filtered by tier. Deliberately without `organisation_id` because it is the global partition.
- `(organisation_id, created_at desc)` where `organisation_id is not null`: "my private connectors" list.
- `(author_organisation_id)` where `kind = 'community'`: marketplace payout calculation per author (billing reads it).
- `(derived_from_connector_id)` where not null: foreign key index and lineage lookup.

Security: mixed global and tenant table; policies as in the catalogue reference rule. Extra write-policy conditions: `with check` also requires `kind = 'private' and trust_tier = 'private'`, so a tenant can neither mint a community connector nor raise a tier. Triggers: `trust_tier` may change only by `silo_migrate`, one step upward at a time, except withdrawal; `kind`, `organisation_id` and `slug` are immutable after insert. Written by `connect-builder` (private rows) and Fleet catalogue release or the Silo promotion review (global rows). `updated_at` trigger. No hard delete.

---

### `connect.connector_manifests`

Purpose: one immutable, versioned manifest document for a connector; no secrets. Spec chapter 14.8.

Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, **null**. Changed: was "Silo catalogue organisation" for catalogue manifests; now null for global manifests, equal to the connector's `organisation_id` otherwise (enforced by the catalogue reference rule trigger).
- `connector_id` uuid, not null.
- `version` text, not null. Semver, check against the semver pattern.
- `document` jsonb, not null. Validated manifest; no secrets.
- `document_hash` bytea, not null. SHA-256 of the canonical document. Added; lets the immutability trigger and the signing step (chapter 15 status, "expression signing") detect change.
- `schema_version` text, not null. Manifest schema version it validated against.
- `source_route` text, not null. `catalogue`, `ai`, `visual`.
- `parent_version_id` uuid, null. Version this was derived from (same connector).
- `first_used_at` timestamptz, null. Set on first query or write.
- `created_by_membership_id` uuid, null. Arc member 1. Changed: spec column `created_by` ("membership or service principal") replaced by an exclusive arc.
- `created_by_service_principal_id` uuid, null. Arc member 2.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `superseded_at` timestamptz, null.

Checks: arc as in `connectors` (exactly one when `organisation_id` is not null, none when null).

Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (connector_id, version)`; `unique (connector_id, id)` (target of `(connector_id, manifest_id)` from `connections`); `unique (organisation_id, id)`.

References: `connector_id → connect.connectors (id)` (plain; catalogue reference rule); `(connector_id, parent_version_id) → connect.connector_manifests (connector_id, id)`; `(organisation_id, created_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, created_by_service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals`.

Indexes:
- Unique `(connector_id)` where `superseded_at is null`: exactly one current version per connector; serves "current manifest of this connector" and runtime manifest resolution.
- `(organisation_id, connector_id, created_at desc)` where `organisation_id is not null`: version history screen for a private connector.
- `(connector_id, parent_version_id)` where `parent_version_id is not null`: foreign key index; derivation walk in the history view.
- `(organisation_id, created_by_membership_id)` where not null: foreign key index.

Security: mixed table, policies as in the catalogue reference rule. Row immutability trigger: once `first_used_at` is set, only `superseded_at` may change; `document`, `document_hash`, `version` and `schema_version` are never updatable after the first use. Setting `first_used_at` is the only permitted update to a previously unused row apart from `superseded_at` and a draft `document` edit by the author. Note: the conformance summary of 17.2 is written into `document` before first use; later runs live in `connect.conformance_runs`, since the row is immutable afterwards. Written by `connect-builder`; global rows by Fleet or the Silo promotion review.

---

### `connect.connector_promotions`

Purpose: a request to promote a private connector to community, and the Silo review of it. Spec chapter 16.5, audit events `connector_promotion_requested` and `connector_promotion_reviewed`. New table (stress-test finding, medium; review process is an open decision in 16.7).

Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null. Requesting organisation.
- `connector_id` uuid, not null. The private connector.
- `manifest_id` uuid, not null. The private manifest version offered.
- `status` text, not null, default `requested`. `requested`, `in_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`.
- `requested_by` uuid, not null. Membership holding `connector.promote`.
- `requested_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `reviewer_ref` text, null. Silo operator identity from the `directory` database; not a foreign key because the directory is another database.
- `reviewed_at` timestamptz, null.
- `review_notes` text, null. Written by Silo; must not quote customer values.
- `promoted_connector_id` uuid, null. The new global connector created with every organisation-specific value stripped.
- `promoted_manifest_id` uuid, null. Its stripped manifest.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().

Checks: `status = 'approved'` implies both promoted ids not null; `status in ('approved','rejected')` implies `reviewed_at` and `reviewer_ref` not null.

Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.

References: `(organisation_id, connector_id) → connect.connectors`; `(organisation_id, requested_by) → iam.memberships`; `manifest_id → connect.connector_manifests (id)`, `promoted_connector_id → connect.connectors (id)`, `promoted_manifest_id → connect.connector_manifests (id)` (plain; catalogue reference rule, the promoted ids point at global rows).

Indexes:
- Unique `(organisation_id, connector_id)` where `status in ('requested','in_review')`: one open promotion per connector.
- `(organisation_id, created_at desc)`: the tenant's promotion list.
- `(status, requested_at)` where `status in ('requested','in_review')`: Silo review queue across tenants (read by operator tooling as `silo_migrate`; the one deliberate index without `organisation_id`).
- `(organisation_id, requested_by)`: foreign key index.

Security: RLS standard for the tenant. The review step and the creation of the promoted global rows run as `silo_migrate` (operator tooling). A tenant can insert and withdraw a request but cannot set any `reviewed_*` or `promoted_*` column (column-level grant). Retention: kept for the life of the connector (payout evidence).

---

### `connect.connections`

Purpose: a configured instance of a connector for one organisation; default deny until granted. Spec chapter 14.7, 14.8.

Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `connector_id` uuid, not null. Logical connector the manifests belong to.
- `manifest_id` uuid, not null. Current manifest version in use.
- `name` text, not null.
- `provider` text, not null. Denormalised from `connectors.provider` at creation; read-only afterwards.
- `trust_tier` text, not null. `private`, `community`, `verified`, `certified`. Changed: kept as a denormalised snapshot of `connectors.trust_tier`; the connector row is the source of truth and the `connect` service updates this column when a promotion lands.
- `owning_scope_id` uuid, not null.
- `owning_membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `policy_authority` text, not null, default `owner_set`. `owner_set`, `delegated`, `locked`.
- `policy_authority_granted_to` uuid, null. Membership. A single column on the connection, so it is unique per connection by construction.
- `policy_authority_set_by` uuid, null. Membership. Null until a super admin sets a non-default mode.
- `policy_authority_set_at` timestamptz, null.
- `status` text, not null, default `draft`. `draft`, `probing`, `verified`, `active`, `halted`, `revoked`.
- `writes_enabled` boolean, not null, default false. True only after the write-verify-undo conformance class passes (17.1).
- `agent_pool_id` uuid, null. Set when the manifest transport is an agent transport.
- `credential_custody` text, not null, default `cell`. `cell`, `agent`. Through the Silo Agent (spec 10.7): `cell` keeps the login sealed here and passes it per piece of work, sealed to the agent running it; `agent` keeps it on the agent's host, the cell holds none, and each use is recorded `held_by_agent`. Always `cell` without an agent pool (check); frozen at creation. Added (implementation 2026-11-17, D132).
- `created_by` uuid, not null. Membership.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `last_healthy_at` timestamptz, null.
- `halted_reason` text, null.
- `halted_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Removal is a status change plus this timestamp.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added; optimistic lock for concurrent ownership, policy and rename edits.

Checks:
- `(policy_authority = 'delegated') = (policy_authority_granted_to is not null)`.
- `policy_authority <> 'owner_set'` implies `policy_authority_set_by` and `policy_authority_set_at` not null.
- `writes_enabled` implies `status in ('active','halted')`.
- `status = 'halted'` implies `halted_reason` and `halted_at` not null; `status = 'revoked'` implies `revoked_at` not null.
- Status transition trigger allows only: draft to probing; probing to verified or draft; verified to active; active to halted; halted to active (resume); any state to revoked; revoked is terminal.

Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id, connector_id)` (target for `oauth_pending_flows`).

References:
- `connector_id → connect.connectors (id)` and `(connector_id, manifest_id) → connect.connector_manifests (connector_id, id)`, both under the catalogue reference rule.
- `(organisation_id, owning_scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, owning_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, policy_authority_granted_to) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, policy_authority_set_by) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.
- `(organisation_id, agent_pool_id) → connect.agent_pools`.

Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, created_at desc)`: connections list screen.
- `(organisation_id, owning_scope_id)` where `revoked_at is null`: connections owned within a scope subtree; also used by grant resolution.
- `(organisation_id, owning_membership_id)` where `revoked_at is null`: "my connections", transfer of ownership.
- `(organisation_id, connector_id)`: foreign key index; connections per connector.
- `(organisation_id, manifest_id)`: connections on a manifest version; used when a repair supersedes a version.
- `(organisation_id, agent_pool_id)` where `agent_pool_id is not null`: connections per pool, for the pool page and the single-agent warning.
- `(organisation_id, policy_authority_granted_to)` where not null: foreign key index; revoking a delegated admin.
- `(organisation_id, last_healthy_at)` where `status = 'active'`: weekly re-check and health sweep (17.3).
- `(organisation_id, created_by)`, `(organisation_id, policy_authority_set_by)`: foreign key indexes.

Security: RLS standard. Written by `connect` service. Revoking a connection revokes its credentials in the same transaction (14.7). Access to a connection is decided by `iam.connection_grants`, not by this table. Halting a connection also updates dependent subscriptions, Crons and clones through events, not triggers.

---

### `connect.connection_credentials`

Purpose: one sealed secret belonging to a connection (or to an OAuth client); ciphertext only, never plaintext. Spec chapter 15.2, 15.5 and chapter 61. **Merged**: the definitions in chapter 15 (here) and chapter 61 (listed under `iam`) are one table, owned by `connect`; the `iam` entry is removed.

Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Part of the additional authenticated data (AAD).
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null. Part of the AAD.
- `connection_id` uuid, null. Null only for OAuth client secrets and registration tokens (see `purpose`).
- `purpose` text, not null, default `connection_auth`. `connection_auth` (includes webhook signing secrets, a connection credential per 18.8), `oauth_client_secret`, `oauth_registration_token`. Added, so oauth client secrets share the sealing scheme.
- `field_name` text, not null. Manifest auth field this seals.
- `custody` text, not null, default `cell`. `cell` (sealed here) or `agent` (secret stays in the customer's key store; the cell holds no secret, chapter 10.7). Added.
- `ciphertext` bytea, null. AES-256-GCM ciphertext including the tag. Changed: spec chapter 15 `sealed_blob`, chapter 61 `ciphertext`; the chapter 61 name is kept.
- `nonce` bytea, null. 96 bits, fresh per seal.
- `dek_wrapped` bytea, null. The per-credential 256-bit DEK wrapped by the KEK (Google Cloud KMS, or UK HSM in the sovereign cell).
- `key_version_id` uuid, null. Changed: chapter 15 `key_ref` (text) and chapter 61 `key_version_id` (uuid) merged to the uuid reference.
- `last_four` text, null. The only clear-text fragment; at most 4 characters; computed inside the credential service `store` function. Null when custody is `agent`.
- `auth_strategy` text, not null. Strategy declared by the manifest (chapter 15.1).
- `granted_scopes` text[], not null, default empty. Checked against required scopes after OAuth token exchange.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, null.
- `refreshed_at` timestamptz, null.
- `refresh_failure_count` integer, not null, default 0. A failure surfaces as reconnect, never as an empty result.
- `last_used_at` timestamptz, null. Written in the same transaction as the unwrap.
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added (chapter 61 had it, chapter 15 did not).
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added (rotation and refresh change the row).

Checks:
- `custody = 'cell'` and `revoked_at is null` implies `ciphertext`, `nonce`, `dek_wrapped`, `key_version_id` all not null; `custody = 'agent'` implies all four null.
- `length(nonce) = 12`; `char_length(last_four) <= 4`.
- `(connection_id is null) = (purpose in ('oauth_client_secret','oauth_registration_token'))`.
- On revocation the sealed columns (`ciphertext`, `nonce`, `dek_wrapped`) are set to null in the same statement that sets `revoked_at`. This crypto-shreds the secret while the row stays for audit. Added.

AAD and rotation: the GCM AAD for `ciphertext` is `(id, organisation_id, connection_id, field_name, purpose)`. The key version is bound to the wrapped DEK through the KMS encryption context, not to `ciphertext`. Reason: chapter 15 requires rotation to re-wrap the DEK without decrypting `ciphertext`, which is impossible if the key version is in the ciphertext's AAD. Rotation updates `dek_wrapped` and `key_version_id` only, one transaction per credential.

Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.

References: `(organisation_id, connection_id) → connect.connections`; `key_version_id → iam.kms_key_versions (id)` (global registry, plain).

Indexes:
- Unique `(organisation_id, connection_id, field_name)` where `revoked_at is null and connection_id is not null`: credential lookup for a connection on every query, and one live secret per field.
- `(organisation_id, expires_at)` where `revoked_at is null and expires_at is not null`: proactive refresh sweep.
- `(organisation_id, key_version_id)` where `revoked_at is null and custody = 'cell'`: rotation job finds rows still on an old key version; foreign key index.

Security: RLS standard. Encrypted columns: `ciphertext`, `nonce`, `dek_wrapped`; no plaintext column exists. Only the credential service opens a row. The "single mediator" rule is enforced in the database: column-level `select` on `ciphertext`, `nonce`, `dek_wrapped` is revoked from `silo_app` and granted to a new role `silo_credential`, used only by the credential service. This closes the CI-enforcement open decision of 15.7 and needs `silo_credential` added to the conventions role list. Every other service reads the row through view `connect.connection_credentials_safe`, which omits those three columns. Refresh serialisation: `select ... for update` on the row (or a transaction advisory lock on the id) held for the refresh; the rotated refresh token is sealed in the same transaction that releases it. Every unwrap also inserts into `iam.credential_unwraps` (append-only ledger) with a reason from the closed set `connect, query, mutation, read_back, refresh, probe, rotation, change_stream, idp, mfa_verify, sso_assert` (Changed (decision 2026-10-29): the last two open MFA factors and identity provider secrets, never a connection credential). Logs are redacted by key name. Written only by the credential service. No hard delete.

---

### `connect.oauth_pending_flows`

Purpose: server-side record of an OAuth authorisation in flight, keyed by the hash of the state parameter. Spec chapter 15.3, 15.5. New in spec, no id column.

Columns:
- `state_hash` bytea, not null. SHA-256 of the state parameter, never the state itself.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `connection_id` uuid, not null. Pending connection (status `draft`).
- `connector_id` uuid, not null. Must equal the connection's connector (composite reference).
- `membership_id` uuid, not null. Initiating membership.
- `session_id` uuid, not null. Binding to the initiating session.
- `pkce_verifier_sealed` bytea, null. Sealed under the credential scheme (AES-256-GCM, wrapped DEK held in the same sealed envelope format, written by the credential service).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `expires_at` timestamptz, not null. Created plus 15 minutes (target). Check `expires_at > created_at`.
- `consumed_at` timestamptz, null. Single use.
- `expired_at` timestamptz, null. Set by the sweep. Added; removal is a status change.

Keys: primary key `(state_hash)`; `unique (organisation_id, state_hash)`. Changed: no `id` column; the hash is the identity, so the standard `unique (organisation_id, id)` is replaced by this one. Nothing references the table.

References: `(organisation_id, connection_id, connector_id) → connect.connections (organisation_id, id, connector_id)`; `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, session_id) → iam.sessions (organisation_id, id)`. Changed (review 2026-10-28): composite; `iam.sessions` has a nullable `organisation_id` and `unique (organisation_id, id)`.

Indexes:
- Primary key on `state_hash`: the callback lookup through `connect.resolve_oauth_flow`.
- `(organisation_id, expires_at)` where `consumed_at is null and expired_at is null`: expiry sweep.
- `(organisation_id, connection_id)`: foreign key index; abandon pending flows when a connection is revoked.
- `(organisation_id, membership_id)`: foreign key index.
- `(organisation_id, session_id)`: foreign key index. Added (review 2026-10-28).

Security: RLS standard, except the callback lookup, which uses `connect.resolve_oauth_flow(state_hash)`: it atomically sets `consumed_at` where `consumed_at is null and expired_at is null and expires_at > now()` and returns `organisation_id`, `connection_id` and `session_id`, or nothing. Single use is therefore a single statement. The callback then verifies the session matches. Encrypted: `pkce_verifier_sealed`. Written by the `oauth` service. Rows older than 30 days are physically purged by the receipted Silo purge job (proposed).

---

### `connect.oauth_clients`

Purpose: the OAuth client (registered application) used to authenticate to a provider: Silo-registered, dynamically registered, or customer-supplied. Spec chapter 15.4, 15.5.

Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null. The cell's system organisation (`iam.organisations.is_system`) for `silo_registered` clients; the customer organisation otherwise. Changed (review 2026-10-28): names the system organisation. This table is not mixed: it carries secrets, so it is never read through a null-organisation policy.
- `connector_id` uuid, not null.
- `origin` text, not null. `silo_registered`, `dynamic_registration`, `bring_your_own`.
- `client_id` text, not null. Public identifier.
- `client_secret_credential_id` uuid, null. Null for public clients.
- `metadata_url` text, null.
- `registration_access_token_credential_id` uuid, null. RFC 7592 management token, sealed.
- `redirect_uri` text, not null. The cell callback URI.
- `created_by` uuid, null. Membership; null for `silo_registered`. Changed from not null to allow Silo-owned rows.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.

Checks: `origin <> 'silo_registered'` implies `created_by` not null.

Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.

References: `connector_id → connect.connectors (id)` (catalogue reference rule: the connector is global or belongs to the same organisation); `(organisation_id, client_secret_credential_id) → connect.connection_credentials`; `(organisation_id, registration_access_token_credential_id) → connect.connection_credentials`; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.

Indexes:
- Unique `(organisation_id, connector_id, client_id)` where `revoked_at is null`.
- `(organisation_id, connector_id)` where `revoked_at is null`: resolve the client to use when a flow starts (own client first, catalogue client second); foreign key index.
- `(organisation_id, client_secret_credential_id)`, `(organisation_id, registration_access_token_credential_id)` where not null: foreign key indexes.

Security: RLS standard. To start a flow with a Silo-registered client, the `oauth` service runs a separate read-only transaction with `app.org_id` set to the system organisation (Changed (review 2026-10-28): was "catalogue organisation"); this capability belongs to that service only. Secrets live in `connect.connection_credentials` (purposes `oauth_client_secret`, `oauth_registration_token`), under the same organisation as the client. Written by the `oauth` service; `oauth_client.manage` permission for customer rows.

---

### `connect.probe_runs`

Purpose: one stage of the sandbox probe and build pipeline for a connection; structure only. Spec chapter 17.1, 17.4.

Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `connection_id` uuid, not null.
- `manifest_id` uuid, not null. Draft or version probed.
- `stage` text, not null. `parse`, `probe`, `reconcile`, `conform`, `propose_mapping`, `confirm`, `verify`, `recheck`.
- `status` text, not null, default `running`. `running`, `completed`, `failed`.
- `findings` jsonb, null. Structure only: objects, fields, types, counts, documented versus observed disagreements. Never values.
- `errors` jsonb, null. Classified errors, redacted.
- `started_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `completed_at` timestamptz, null.
