- `ontology_version_id` uuid, not null.
- `link_type_id`, `interface_id`, `shared_property_id`, `function_id`, `field_authority_id` uuid, null. Exclusive arc. Check `num_nonnulls(link_type_id, interface_id, shared_property_id, function_id, field_authority_id) = 1`.
- `element_ref` uuid, generated always as `coalesce(link_type_id, interface_id, shared_property_id, function_id, field_authority_id)` stored.
- `revision` integer, not null. Monotonic per element.
- `operation` text, not null. Check in (`create`, `change`, `deprecate`, `retire`, `revoke`).
- `change_class` text, not null. Check in (`additive`, `compatible`, `breaking`).
- `snapshot` jsonb, not null. Metadata of the element after the change (names, types, ids, routes, bindings). Never record values.
- `content_hash` bytea, not null. SHA-256 of the canonical snapshot; the version `manifest_hash` is computed from these and from `object_type_versions`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, element_ref, revision)`.
References: `(organisation_id, ontology_version_id) → ontology.ontology_versions`; one composite FK per arc column to `ontology.link_types`, `ontology.interfaces`, `ontology.shared_properties`, `ontology.functions`, `ontology.field_authorities`.
Indexes: the unique key serves element history and diff. `(organisation_id, ontology_version_id)` serves manifest building, review diff and rollback. Arc FK indexes are satisfied by `element_ref` through the unique key (the arc column equals `element_ref` whenever it is set, and purge is the only delete).
Security: RLS standard. Insert-only; trigger rejects update and delete. Written by `ontology-service` in the transaction that creates the ontology version.

---

## Profiles and templates

### `ontology.field_profiles`
Purpose: counts describing one source column, used by derivation and shown at confirmation. Spec chapter 22 (22.3).
Columns:
- `id`, `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `connection_id` uuid, not null.
- `source_object`, `field_path` text, not null.
- `row_count` bigint, not null; `distinct_count` bigint, null (exact only, null when the source cannot push COUNT(DISTINCT); never estimated from a sample); `null_count` bigint, not null; `empty_count` bigint, not null; `min_length`, `max_length` integer, null (lengths, not values); `type_conformance_count` bigint, not null.
- `profiled_at` timestamptz, not null; `connector_version` text, not null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
Check: all counts `>= 0`; `null_count + empty_count <= row_count`; `distinct_count <= row_count`; `type_conformance_count <= row_count`; `min_length <= max_length`. The table has no column that can hold a value: no minimum, maximum or frequent value, by design.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, connection_id, source_object, field_path, profiled_at)`.
References: `(organisation_id, connection_id) → connect.connections`.
Indexes: the unique key serves "latest profile of a column" (descending scan on `profiled_at`) used by derivation and by the confirmation page.
Security: RLS standard. Insert-only (a re-profile adds a row; history is kept for the confirmation record). Written by `derivation-service`. Retention: rows older than the 12 most recent per column are removed by the retention job as `silo_migrate`.

### `ontology.description_embeddings`
Purpose: the names and descriptions of the elements on main (object types, properties, link types), embedded so compile can narrow a large vocabulary to the types a question is about (decision 2026-11-15; spec 7.4: metadata embeddings in pgvector). Added (D103).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`object_type`, `property`, `link_type`).
- `element_id` uuid, not null. The object type id, the property identity id, or the link type id. No foreign key: a cache of main, rebuilt from it.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null. The type it belongs to; for an object type, itself (check); for a link type, its from type.
- `other_object_type_id` uuid, null. A link type's to type; set exactly for link types (check).
- `text_hash` text, not null. SHA-256 (hex) of the text embedded: a different hash means the description changed and it is embedded again.
- `embedding` vector(1536), not null. Names and descriptions only, never a record value. The dimension is the embedding route's, fixed per cell.
- `model` text, not null; `embedded_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, kind, element_id)`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, object_type_id)`; `(organisation_id, other_object_type_id)` where set. Similarity is computed over one organisation's rows for the reader's types (hundreds), so no vector index.
Security: RLS standard. Written and read by `ontology` (silo_app: select, insert, update, delete). Embedded through the model gateway (zero-retention route), screened like any prompt.

### `ontology.concept_templates`
Purpose: Silo-authored names and field names that make a first proposal arrive with a recognisable name. Spec chapter 22 (22.7). Global per cell: no `organisation_id`.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `name` text, not null. For example Invoice.
- `field_names` text[], not null. Names only, no types, no values. Check `cardinality(field_names) between 1 and 200`.
- `authored_by` uuid, not null. Silo staff identity. No foreign key: staff identities are held in the global `directory` database, which a cell cannot join to. Fleet validates it when it distributes the template.
- `reviewed_by` uuid, null; `reviewed_at` timestamptz, null. Same note on `reviewed_by`. Check `status <> 'reviewed' or (reviewed_by is not null and reviewed_at is not null and reviewed_by <> authored_by)`.
- `status` text, not null, default `'draft'`. Check in (`draft`, `reviewed`, `withdrawn`).
- `revision` integer, not null, default 1. Added: Fleet distributes only templates whose revision changed.
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; unique index `(lower(name))` where `status in ('draft','reviewed')`. No `organisation_id`, so the tenant `unique (organisation_id, id)` rule does not apply here.
References: none. `ontology.object_types.template_id` references `id`.
Indexes: the unique index serves `nameFor` (match by field names is done in memory over the reviewed set, which is small: tens to low hundreds of rows). `(status)` is not indexed.
Security: this is the only cross-tenant table in Silo and it is protected in four ways.
1. Content: it holds names and field names only. The column set has no place for a type, a value or anything derived from a tenant; a tenant statement can never be written because no tenant code path writes it.
2. Grants: `silo_app` and `silo_report` have `select` only. No `insert`, `update`, `delete` or `truncate` for any tenant-facing role. Writes are made only by Fleet as `silo_migrate` when it distributes reviewed data to the cell (sovereign cell included, same set).
3. Row level security: `enable` and `force` with a single `for select` policy `using (status = 'reviewed')`. A tenant request sees only reviewed rows, never drafts or withdrawn ones. `silo_migrate` bypasses RLS to write. There is no `with check` policy for `silo_app` because it has no write grant.
4. Triggers: reject a change of `status` from `reviewed` to `draft`, reject edit of `name` or `field_names` on a `reviewed` row (a change is a new `revision` with a fresh review, so Fleet sees it), and reject delete.
Template use is never automatic: derivation reads templates only to name a proposal; a person confirms (section 22.7).

---

## Entity resolution

### `ontology.resolution_proposals`
Purpose: a proposed normalisation rule, pair list or split for unresolved or wrongly merged pairs, confirmed by a person. Spec chapter 23 (23.2).
Columns:
- `id`, `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`normalisation_rule`, `pair_list`, `split`).
- `proposal` jsonb, not null. Rule expression or references to match key ids. Never record values; key shapes only.
- `affected_count` integer, not null. Check `>= 0`.
- `proposed_by_membership_id` uuid, null; `proposed_by_service_principal_id` uuid, null. Changed: spec `proposed_by` ("membership or service principal") becomes an exclusive arc. Check `num_nonnulls(...) = 1`.
- `status` text, not null, default `'open'`. Check in (`open`, `confirmed`, `rejected`).
- `decided_by` uuid, null; `decided_at` timestamptz, null. Membership only. Check `(status = 'open') = (decided_by is null and decided_at is null)`.
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; proposer arc FKs to `iam.memberships` and `iam.service_principals`; `(organisation_id, decided_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, created_at desc)` where `status = 'open'`. The review queue.
- `(organisation_id, object_type_id, created_at desc)`. History per type.
- FK indexes: proposer arc indexes where not null, `(organisation_id, decided_by)` where not null.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `resolution-engine` (open) and `ontology-service` (decision, after `ontology.confirm` check). Never deleted.

### `ontology.match_keys`
Purpose: the entity graph: which keyed-hashed source identifiers belong to which Silo object. Holds no property value and no clear identifier. Spec chapter 23 (23.3), chapter 24 (24.7, 24.8).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null; `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_object_id` uuid, not null. UUIDv5 as defined in the domain rules. Not a foreign key (the object is virtual).
- `connection_id` uuid, not null; `source_object` text, not null.
- `source_identifier_hash` bytea, not null. HMAC-SHA-256 of the source identifier under the organisation HMAC key. Check `octet_length = 32`. The clear identifier is never stored.
- `match_key_hash` bytea, not null. HMAC-SHA-256 of the normalised match key under the same key. Check `octet_length = 32`.
- `hmac_key_version_id` uuid, not null. Added: names the organisation HMAC key version used (`iam.organisation_keys`, purpose `hmac`), so a key rotation can re-hash in batches and the engine knows which key to apply to a lookup. Changed (review 2026-10-28): was a reference to `iam.kms_key_versions`, which holds cell KEK versions, not organisation HMAC keys.
- `hmac_key_purpose` text, not null, default `hmac`. Check `hmac_key_purpose = 'hmac'`. Added (review 2026-10-28): exists only so the composite foreign key can prove the key's purpose (same pattern as `silo_kind`).
- `origin` text, not null. Check in (`exact`, `confirmed_mapping`).
- `resolution_proposal_id` uuid, null. Check `(origin = 'confirmed_mapping') = (resolution_proposal_id is not null)`.
- `first_seen_at`, `last_seen_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `superseded_at` timestamptz, null. Set on remapping.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
Keys: partitioned by hash on `organisation_id` into 64 partitions. Primary key `(organisation_id, id)`, which satisfies `unique (organisation_id, id)` and includes the partition key. Unique partial index `(organisation_id, object_type_id, connection_id, source_object, source_identifier_hash)` where `superseded_at is null` (one live entry per source record).
References: `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, connection_id) → connect.connections`; `(organisation_id, resolution_proposal_id) → ontology.resolution_proposals`; `(organisation_id, hmac_key_version_id, hmac_key_purpose) → iam.organisation_keys (organisation_id, id, purpose)` (Changed (review 2026-10-28): was `(organisation_id, hmac_key_version_id) → iam.kms_key_versions`; now pins purpose `hmac`). Nothing references `match_keys`.
Indexes:
- Merge lookup: `(organisation_id, object_type_id, match_key_hash)` where `superseded_at is null`, including `silo_object_id`, `connection_id`, `source_object`, `source_identifier_hash`. One equality probe per match key returns the object and its sources without touching the heap (index-only scan).
- Object view and read-by-identity: `(organisation_id, silo_object_id)` where `superseded_at is null`, including `connection_id`, `source_object`, `source_identifier_hash`. Gives the source identifiers per contributing object for one Silo object.
- The live unique index above serves the insert-or-touch path when a query returns records and remapping (detect an old entry for the same source record).
- FK indexes: `(organisation_id, connection_id)` where `superseded_at is null` (connection retirement and purge); `(organisation_id, resolution_proposal_id)` where not null; `(organisation_id, hmac_key_version_id)` (rotation batches).
- No index on `last_seen_at`; no query selects by it.
Security: RLS standard. The hash columns are never logged and never returned to a client (the API exposes the Silo object id only). Written by `resolution-engine` on the answering path and by `ontology-service` when a person confirms a mapping. `last_seen_at` is updated by a batched write at most once per hour per row to keep write load down; `superseded_at` is set only by remapping. Superseded rows are retained for lineage and for roll-forward (section 25.8); entries whose elements no longer exist become inactive by a join on the type status, not by deletion. Purge of an organisation removes the partitions' rows as `silo_migrate` with a receipt.

### `ontology.object_redirects`
Purpose: records that one Silo object id was merged into another by a source-system merge, so references to the old id resolve to the target and say they were redirected. Spec chapter 24 (24.8). Added table (the spec states the behaviour but no storage).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null; `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `from_silo_object_id` uuid, not null; `to_silo_object_id` uuid, not null. Check `from_silo_object_id <> to_silo_object_id`.
- `resolution_proposal_id` uuid, null. Set when a person confirmed the merge.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `undone_at` timestamptz, null. Set by a confirmed `split`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; unique partial index `(organisation_id, from_silo_object_id)` where `undone_at is null` (an id redirects to one target at a time).
References: `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, resolution_proposal_id) → ontology.resolution_proposals`.
Indexes: the unique partial index serves redirect resolution on every read by identity. `(organisation_id, to_silo_object_id)` where `undone_at is null` serves collecting all ids merged into a target. FK indexes: `(organisation_id, object_type_id)`, `(organisation_id, resolution_proposal_id)` where not null.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `resolution-engine`. The engine follows redirect chains to a depth of 8 and a cycle is rejected at insert by checking the target's own redirect.

### `ontology.field_authorities`
Purpose: a person's declaration of which system wins for a property, optionally under a condition. Spec chapter 23 (23.4).
Columns:
- `id`, `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `property_identity_id` uuid, not null. Changed: spec `property_id`; points at the stable identity so a declaration survives type versions.
- `winning_connection_id` uuid, not null.
- `condition` text, null. CEL predicate.
- `declared_by` uuid, not null; `declared_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Membership holding `authority.declare`.
- `reason` text, not null. Check `length(btrim(reason)) > 0`.
- `revoked_by` uuid, null; `revoked_at` timestamptz, null. Check `(revoked_by is null) = (revoked_at is null)`.
- `ontology_version_id` uuid, not null. Added: version that introduced the declaration (a new authority is a compatible change, section 25.5).
- `origin_branch_id` uuid, null. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, object_type_id, property_identity_id) → ontology.property_identities (organisation_id, object_type_id, id)`; `(organisation_id, winning_connection_id) → connect.connections`; `(organisation_id, declared_by) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, revoked_by) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, ontology_version_id) → ontology.ontology_versions`; `(organisation_id, origin_branch_id) → ontology.ontology_branches`. Constraint trigger: the winning connection has a mapping for the property in the type's current version.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, object_type_id, property_identity_id)` where `revoked_at is null and origin_branch_id is null`. Merge: load live authorities for the properties of a type (hot path).
- FK indexes: `(organisation_id, winning_connection_id)` where `revoked_at is null`; `(organisation_id, declared_by)`; `(organisation_id, revoked_by)` where not null; `(organisation_id, ontology_version_id)`; `(organisation_id, origin_branch_id)` where not null.
Security: RLS standard. Declaration and revocation are status changes, never deletes; rollback leaves them inactive where the element no longer exists (section 25.8). Changes recorded in `element_revisions`. Written by `ontology-service`.

---

## Object sets

### `ontology.object_sets`
Purpose: a saved, named definition of a set of objects (filter, traversal, explicit or composite); the definition is stored, never the members, except identifiers for explicit sets. Spec chapter 24 (24.4).
Columns:
- `id`, `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `name` text, not null; `description` text, null. Name unique per owner among live sets.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`filter`, `traversal`, `explicit`, `composite`).
- `base_type_id` uuid, null; `base_interface_id` uuid, null. Exclusive arc: check `num_nonnulls(base_type_id, base_interface_id) = 1`.
- `definition` jsonb, not null. Predicates, traversal path (link type ids and routes), set operations. Period expressions stored unresolved. Dependencies it names are mirrored in `ontology_dependencies`. A GIN index is not created; no query filters inside it.
- `explicit_ids` uuid[], null. Silo object ids, explicit sets only. Check `(kind = 'explicit') = (explicit_ids is not null)` and `cardinality(explicit_ids) <= 10000`.
- `ontology_version_id` uuid, not null. Version the definition was validated against.
- `owner_membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `visibility` text, not null, default `'private'`. Check in (`private`, `shared`).
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `archived_at` timestamptz, null. Added: removal is a status change (event `object_set_deleted`).
- `row_version` integer, not null, default 1. Added: optimistic locking.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; unique partial index `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id, lower(name))` where `archived_at is null`.
References: `(organisation_id, base_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, base_interface_id) → ontology.interfaces`; `(organisation_id, ontology_version_id) → ontology.ontology_versions`; `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id, created_at desc)` where `archived_at is null`. "My sets" list screen.
- `(organisation_id, created_at desc)` where `visibility = 'shared' and archived_at is null`. Shared sets list; each opener's permissions are re-checked at evaluation.
- FK indexes: `(organisation_id, base_type_id)` where not null; `(organisation_id, base_interface_id)` where not null; `(organisation_id, ontology_version_id)`.
Security: RLS standard. Markings of an object set derive from the types it touches (via `iam.object_type_markings`); this table stores none. Written by `ontology-service` (`object_set.save`). Shared sets are re-checked under the opener's permissions at evaluation, not at read of this row.

---

## Versions, branches, proposals, dependencies

### `ontology.ontology_versions`
Purpose: an immutable snapshot of the organisation's ontology on a branch; the unit that plans, apps, Crons and Actions record. Spec chapter 25 (25.1).
Columns:
- `id`, `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `branch_id` uuid, not null.
- `sequence` bigint, not null. Monotonic per branch, assigned by `ontology-service` under a row lock on the branch.
- `parent_version_id` uuid, null. Null only for the first version of main.
- `merged_from_proposal_id` uuid, null. Set when `kind = 'merge'`.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`change`, `merge`, `rollback`, `migration`).
- `rolled_back_to_version_id` uuid, null. Added: the version a rollback restores (section 25.8). Check `(kind = 'rollback') = (rolled_back_to_version_id is not null)`.
- `manifest_hash` bytea, not null. SHA-256 over the canonical serialisation of every element in the version (type versions in `object_type_versions`, other elements in `element_revisions`). Check `octet_length = 32`.
- `created_by_membership_id` uuid, null; `created_by_service_principal_id` uuid, null. Changed: exclusive arc, as derivation writes versions on its own branch.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, branch_id, sequence)`.
References: `(organisation_id, branch_id) → ontology.ontology_branches`, deferrable initially deferred (branch head points back); `(organisation_id, parent_version_id) → ontology.ontology_versions`; `(organisation_id, merged_from_proposal_id) → ontology.ontology_proposals`; `(organisation_id, rolled_back_to_version_id) → ontology.ontology_versions`; creator arc FKs.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, branch_id, sequence desc)` is the unique key read backwards. Latest version of a branch and history list.
- FK indexes: `(organisation_id, parent_version_id)`, `(organisation_id, merged_from_proposal_id)` where not null, `(organisation_id, rolled_back_to_version_id)` where not null, creator arc indexes where not null.
Security: RLS standard. Insert-only; trigger rejects update and delete. Written by `ontology-service` only. Referenced by lineage, receipts and Action commits, so never altered.

### `ontology.ontology_branches`
Purpose: a named line of change from a base version of main. Spec chapter 25 (25.3).
Columns:
- `id`, `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `name` text, not null. `main` is reserved and exists for every organisation.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`main`, `working`, `derivation`, `scenario`). Check `(kind = 'main') = (name = 'main')`.
- `base_version_id` uuid, null. Null only for `main`.
- `head_version_id` uuid, null. Null until the first version exists.
- `scenario_id` uuid, null. Check `(kind = 'scenario') = (scenario_id is not null)`.
- `owner_membership_id` uuid, null. Null for `main`.
- `status` text, not null, default `'open'`. Check in (`open`, `merged`, `abandoned`).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(); `closed_at` timestamptz, null. Check `(status = 'open') = (closed_at is null)`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(); `row_version` integer, not null, default 1. Added: `head_version_id` moves on every commit, concurrent writers use `row_version`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; unique partial index `(organisation_id)` where `kind = 'main'` (exactly one main per organisation); unique partial index `(organisation_id, lower(name))` where `status = 'open'`.
References: `(organisation_id, base_version_id) → ontology.ontology_versions`, deferrable; `(organisation_id, head_version_id) → ontology.ontology_versions`, deferrable; `(organisation_id, scenario_id) → simulation.scenarios`; `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes:
- The main-branch partial unique index finds the main head in one probe: the entry point for every compile and for vocabulary resolution.
- `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id, created_at desc)` where `status = 'open'`. "My branches" list.
- FK indexes: `(organisation_id, base_version_id)` where not null, `(organisation_id, head_version_id)` where not null, `(organisation_id, scenario_id)` where not null.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `ontology-service` (`ontology.branch`). The `main` row is created with the organisation. Never deleted; abandonment is a status.

### `ontology.ontology_proposals`
Purpose: a reviewable set of changes on one branch, with impact analysis, approved and merged by people. Spec chapter 25 (25.4, 25.6).
Columns:
- `id`, `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `branch_id` uuid, not null.
- `title` text, not null; `description` text, null.
- `origin` text, not null. Check in (`person`, `derivation`, `ai_fde`, `rollback`).
- `changes` jsonb, not null. Element references and change class per change. No values.
- `highest_change_class` text, not null. Check in (`additive`, `compatible`, `breaking`).
- `impact` jsonb, null. Dependant references and counts at last analysis; dependants a reviewer cannot see are counts only.
- `impact_computed_at` timestamptz, null.
- `status` text, not null, default `'draft'`. Check in (`draft`, `in_review`, `approved`, `merged`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`).
- `author_membership_id` uuid, null; `author_service_principal_id` uuid, null. Changed: spec `author_id` ("membership or service principal") becomes an exclusive arc. Check `num_nonnulls(...) = 1`.
- `approvals` jsonb. Changed: removed, replaced by `ontology.proposal_approvals`.
- `merged_by` uuid, null; `merged_at` timestamptz, null. Membership only. Check `(merged_by is null) = (merged_at is null)` and `(status = 'merged') = (merged_at is not null)`.
- `submitted_at` timestamptz, null; `decided_at` timestamptz, null. Added: status timestamps.
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz, not null; `row_version` integer, not null, default 1. Added: reviewers and authors edit concurrently.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, branch_id) → ontology.ontology_branches`; author arc FKs to `iam.memberships` and `iam.service_principals`; `(organisation_id, merged_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, submitted_at desc)` where `status in ('in_review','approved')`. Review queue.
- `(organisation_id, branch_id, created_at desc)`. Proposals of a branch.
- FK indexes: author arc indexes where not null; `(organisation_id, merged_by)` where not null.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `ontology-service`. A service principal can author, never approve or merge (merged_by is a membership FK and `proposal_approvals` takes memberships only). At merge, the impact analysis is rerun; if it differs from `impact`, merge is refused (event `ontology_merge_refused_impact_changed`).

### `ontology.proposal_approvals`
Purpose: one person's approval of a proposal, with the permission used. Spec chapter 25 (25.4). Added table, replaces `ontology_proposals.approvals` jsonb so the rules can be enforced.
Columns:
- `id`, `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `proposal_id` uuid, not null.
- `membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `permission` text, not null. Check in (`ontology.confirm`, `ontology.manage`, `ontology.mark`).
- `marking_id` uuid, null. Required when `permission = 'ontology.mark'`: the marking the approver holds. FK to `gov.markings`.
- `approved_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, proposal_id, membership_id, permission)`.
References: `(organisation_id, proposal_id) → ontology.ontology_proposals`; `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, marking_id) → gov.markings`.
Constraint trigger: `membership_id` is not the proposal's `author_membership_id`.
Indexes: the unique key serves loading approvals of a proposal. FK index `(organisation_id, membership_id)`; `(organisation_id, marking_id)` where not null.
Security: RLS standard. Insert-only. Written by `ontology-service`. Merge requires: at least one `ontology.confirm`; plus an `ontology.manage` row when the proposal's `highest_change_class` is `breaking`; plus an `ontology.mark` row per added or removed marking.

### `ontology.ontology_dependencies`
Purpose: the dependency index: which dependants (apps, views, sets, Crons, action types, scenarios, functions, Siloes, detectors, lenses, interface implementations) rely on which ontology elements, written by every compile, save and publish. Spec chapter 25 (25.6).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Added: surrogate key (the spec table had none and the arcs make a composite key impractical).
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- Element arc, exclusive (changed from `element_kind`, `element_id`): `object_type_id` (→ `ontology.object_types`), `property_identity_id` (→ `ontology.property_identities`), `link_type_id` (→ `ontology.link_types`), `interface_id` (→ `ontology.interfaces`), `shared_property_id` (→ `ontology.shared_properties`), `function_id` (→ `ontology.functions`), `action_type_id` (→ `action.action_types`), all uuid, null. Check `num_nonnulls(object_type_id, property_identity_id, link_type_id, interface_id, shared_property_id, function_id, action_type_id) = 1`.
- Dependant arc, exclusive (changed from `dependant_kind`, `dependant_id`): `app_id` (→ `workspace.apps`), `saved_view_id` (→ `workspace.saved_views`, covers dashboards), `object_set_id` (→ `ontology.object_sets`), `automation_id` (→ `automation.automations`), `dependant_action_type_id` (→ `action.action_types`), `scenario_id` (→ `simulation.scenarios`), `dependant_function_id` (→ `ontology.functions`), `silo_object_type_id` (→ `siloes.silo_object_types`, the nomination record), `detector_threshold_id` (→ `recognition.detector_thresholds`), `lens_id` (→ `recognition.lenses`), `interface_implementation_id` (→ `ontology.interface_implementations`), all uuid, null. Check `num_nonnulls(app_id, saved_view_id, object_set_id, automation_id, dependant_action_type_id, scenario_id, dependant_function_id, silo_object_type_id, detector_threshold_id, lens_id, interface_implementation_id) = 1`.
- `element_ref` uuid, generated always as `coalesce(` the seven element columns `)` stored. Added.
- `dependant_ref` uuid, generated always as `coalesce(` the eleven dependant columns `)` stored. Added.
- `ontology_version_id` uuid, not null. Version the dependant last compiled against.
- `recorded_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Time of last record.
- `removed_at` timestamptz, null. Added: a recompile that no longer uses the element marks the row removed (no hard delete).
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; unique partial index `(organisation_id, element_ref, dependant_ref)` where `removed_at is null` (compile upserts: update `ontology_version_id` and `recorded_at`).
References: one composite FK per arc column, each `(organisation_id, col) → target`; `(organisation_id, ontology_version_id) → ontology.ontology_versions`. Within this schema's own tables the targets are `ontology.*`; others are named above.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, element_ref)` where `removed_at is null`, including `dependant_ref`, `ontology_version_id`. Impact analysis: all dependants of each changed element, rerun at merge.
- `(organisation_id, dependant_ref)` where `removed_at is null`. A dependant recompiling finds its previous rows to mark removed, and the vocabulary stage reads a function's inputs (rows where `dependant_function_id` is the function).
- `(organisation_id, ontology_version_id)`. Finding dependants still compiled against an older version (deprecation notices, retirement failure sweep).
- Changed (review 2026-10-28): one partial index per element column, `(organisation_id, x_id) where x_id is not null` for `object_type_id`, `property_identity_id`, `link_type_id`, `interface_id`, `shared_property_id`, `function_id`, `action_type_id`: "what depends on this element", the impact analysis every proposal runs. The dependant columns remain a stated departure from indexing rule 1: a dependant column equals `dependant_ref` whenever it is set, so the `dependant_ref` index serves every lookup by a dependant, and rows are only soft-removed.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `compile-service` and the publish and save paths of the owning services, through one function `ontology.record_dependencies` they call. Lens dependants are reported to reviewers as counts only; the owners are notified and never named. Dependants the reviewer cannot see are counted, not named: the impact query returns counts grouped by dependant kind and joins to names only for rows the caller can see. Reference tables for each dependant kind are owned by their domains; their files must keep `unique (organisation_id, id)`.

---

## Hot paths

1. **Vocabulary resolution for a membership (section 26.3).** Runs on a session cache miss, keyed by ontology version and policy version. Sequence of five indexed reads, then an intersection in memory with the reader's grants from `iam.connection_grants`, `gov.clearances`, `iam.field_policies`:
   - main head: `ontology_branches (organisation_id) where kind = 'main'` (one probe);
   - types: `object_types (organisation_id, status, api_name) where status in ('active','deprecated')` giving `current_version_id`;
   - connections each type needs: `contributing_objects (organisation_id, object_type_version_id, connection_id)`; a type is dropped whole unless every connection and every marking on the type is held (anti-join against the held connection set);
   - properties and their mapping connections: `properties (organisation_id, object_type_version_id) where status <> 'retired'` and `property_mappings (organisation_id, object_type_version_id, property_id)`;
   - links and functions: `link_types (organisation_id, from_type_id)` and `(organisation_id, to_type_id)` with `link_type_routes (organisation_id, connection_id) where removed_at is null` (a link is offered only through routes the reader can see; no visible route means the link is absent), and `ontology_dependencies (organisation_id, dependant_ref)` for function inputs.
   The main ontology read is identical for every member, so the service may cache it per ontology version and apply the per-member filter in memory; the indexes above serve the cache fill and the per-branch compile.
2. **Match key lookup during merge (sections 23.3, 24.7).** For each returned record, probe `match_keys (organisation_id, object_type_id, match_key_hash) where superseded_at is null`, an index-only scan returning `silo_object_id` and the source identifiers. A miss inserts a row, guarded by the live unique index on `(organisation_id, object_type_id, connection_id, source_object, source_identifier_hash)`. Redirects are then resolved with `object_redirects (organisation_id, from_silo_object_id) where undone_at is null`.
3. **Sources of one object (read by identity).** `match_keys (organisation_id, silo_object_id) where superseded_at is null` returns the source identifiers per contributing object for an object view.
4. **Field authority at merge (section 23.4).** `field_authorities (organisation_id, object_type_id, property_identity_id) where revoked_at is null and origin_branch_id is null`, loaded once per type per plan.
5. **Impact analysis (section 25.6).** `ontology_dependencies (organisation_id, element_ref) where removed_at is null` for each changed element, at review and again at merge.
6. **Compile dependency write.** Upsert on `ontology_dependencies (organisation_id, element_ref, dependant_ref) where removed_at is null`, plus `(organisation_id, dependant_ref)` to mark stale rows removed.
# Clones and workspace: schemas `clone` and `workspace`

Spec chapters 28 to 37 (part-05.html, part-06a.html). Global rules are in 00_conventions.md and apply to every table below; this file only states exceptions and additions. All tables are tenant tables with `organisation_id uuid not null`, `unique (organisation_id, id)` and RLS standard unless stated. No table holds a record value except `workspace.ask_turns.question`, which is encrypted. Every `uuid[]` column holds references only and cannot carry a foreign key; the owning service validates members on write, and where an ontology change must find rows that use an element, a GIN index is named.

## Relationships

- `clone.clone_layouts.object_type_id → ontology.object_types`; property columns → `ontology.properties`; `containment_link_type_id → ontology.link_types`
- `clone.state_rules.object_type_id → ontology.object_types`; `clone.staleness_thresholds.connection_id → connect.connections`
- `clone.canvas_views.object_set_ref → ontology.object_sets`; `.plan_id → clone.spatial_plans`; `.asset_model_id → clone.asset_models`; `.scenario_id → simulation.scenarios`
- `clone.spatial_plans.silo_id → siloes.siloes`; `.(silo_id, silo_file_id) → siloes.silo_files` (Changed (review 2026-10-28): one composite reference; was `.file_id → files.files`); same for `clone.asset_models`
- `clone.spatial_anchors.plan_id / asset_model_id → clone.spatial_plans / clone.asset_models` (exclusive arc)
- `clone.live_subscriptions.cron_id → automation.automations`; `.object_set_ref → ontology.object_sets`
- `clone.estate_snapshots.discovery_run_id → connect.discovery_runs`
- `workspace.saved_views.owner_membership_id → iam.memberships`; `.thread_id → workspace.ask_threads`; `.object_set_id → ontology.object_sets`
- `workspace.view_shares.saved_view_id / canvas_view_id / scenario_id → workspace.saved_views / clone.canvas_views / simulation.scenarios` (Changed (review 2026-10-28): `scenario_id` added); grantee arc → `iam.memberships` / `iam.scopes`
- `workspace.dashboard_tiles.saved_view_id / canvas_view_id / scenario_id → workspace.saved_views / clone.canvas_views / simulation.scenarios`
- `workspace.favourites` object / app / scenario arc → `ontology.object_types` plus object reference / `workspace.apps` / `simulation.scenarios`
- `workspace.apps.current_version_id → workspace.app_versions`; `workspace.app_versions.app_id → workspace.apps`
- `workspace.app_references` element arc → `ontology.object_types`, `ontology.properties`, `ontology.link_types`, `action.action_types`, `ontology.functions`
- `workspace.app_publications.scope_id → iam.scopes`; `workspace.scope_sharing_policies.scope_id → iam.scopes`
- `workspace.ask_turns.thread_id → workspace.ask_threads`; `workspace.ask_threads.saved_view_id → workspace.saved_views`
- `workspace.notifications.recipient_membership_id → iam.memberships`; source arc → `automation.automation_run_actions` (Changed (review 2026-10-28): was `automation.automation_runs`), `action.approval_chains`, `recognition.findings`, `simulation.simulation_runs`
- `workspace.recent_items.membership_id → iam.memberships`; item arc → object type plus reference, `workspace.saved_views`, `clone.canvas_views`, `workspace.apps`, `simulation.scenarios`
- `workspace.terminology_skins` target arc → `ontology.object_types`, `ontology.link_types`, `action.action_types`

## Decisions that apply to the whole file

1. **`workspace.organisations` is not created.** Spec 37.4 lists `view_sharing_policy`, `org_wide_sharing_permitted` and `external_sharing_permitted` as "organisations (sharing columns)". The identical three columns already exist on `iam.organisations`. Merged into `iam.organisations`; the sharing services read them there. This avoids two copies of one setting.
2. **Compiled manifests.** Changed (review 2026-10-28): the owning table now exists. `manifest_id` on `workspace.saved_views`, `workspace.ask_turns` and `workspace.analysis_steps` is a composite foreign key `(organisation_id, manifest_id) → ontology.compiled_manifests` (defined in the cross-domain section).
3. **Ad hoc object sets.** `object_set_ref` on `clone.canvas_views` and `clone.live_subscriptions`, and `object_set_id` on `workspace.saved_views`, reference `ontology.object_sets`. An Explorer result or Ask "find objects" result must be persisted by the ontology service as a private `object_sets` row before it is saved, canvassed or subscribed. No definition is stored inline here.
4. **Optimistic locking.** Tables with concurrent edits carry `lock_version integer not null default 1`, incremented on every update; the writer updates `where lock_version = :expected` and treats zero rows as a conflict. Added on `apps`, `app_versions`, `saved_views`, `canvas_views`, `state_rules`.
5. **Retention deletes.** The convention allows physical deletes only as partition drops and Silo purges. Two tables here need cache sweeps: `clone.live_subscriptions` (spec: ended rows swept after 7 days) and `clone.layout_precomputations` (expired rows). Both are swept by a scheduled job running as `silo_migrate`, which writes a count receipt. Flag for the conventions owner: confirm this as a third permitted physical delete.
6. **Roles that write.** `studio service` writes apps, versions, references, publications. `view service` writes saved views, shares, tiles, transfer flags, favourites, recent items. `clone service` writes the `clone` schema except `estate_snapshots`, written by the `estate service`. `ask service` writes threads and turns. `notification service` writes `notifications` and sets `read_at` and `acknowledged_at` on behalf of the recipient. All use `silo_app`.

---

# Schema `clone`

### `clone.clone_layouts`
Purpose: per object type, which properties drive the geographic, containment, schematic, timeline and label layouts, versioned by supersession. Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. UUIDv7.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null. The object type the layout is for.
- `geo_property_id` uuid, null. The Located property.
- `crs` text, null. EPSG code, for example `EPSG:4326`. Check: not null if and only if `geo_property_id` is not null; matches `^EPSG:[0-9]+$`.
- `containment_link_type_id` uuid, null.
- `stage_property_id` uuid, null. Schematic stage.
- `time_property_id` uuid, null. Timeline time.
- `lane_property_id` uuid, null. Timeline lane.
- `label_property_id` uuid, not null. Node label.
- `ontology_version` bigint, not null. Ontology version the layout was validated against. Version counter, no foreign key.
- `created_by` uuid, not null. Membership.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `superseded_at` timestamptz, null. Added behaviour: a layout is never updated in place; a new row supersedes it.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; partial unique `(organisation_id, object_type_id) where superseded_at is null`, so one live layout per type.
References: `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, geo_property_id)`, `(organisation_id, stage_property_id)`, `(organisation_id, time_property_id)`, `(organisation_id, lane_property_id)`, `(organisation_id, label_property_id) → ontology.properties`; `(organisation_id, containment_link_type_id) → ontology.link_types`; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the partial unique above serves "live layout for this type" on every canvas open. FK indexes `(organisation_id, geo_property_id)`, `(organisation_id, stage_property_id)`, `(organisation_id, time_property_id)`, `(organisation_id, lane_property_id)`, `(organisation_id, label_property_id)`, `(organisation_id, containment_link_type_id)`, `(organisation_id, created_by)`, each partial `where <col> is not null`, serving the ontology delete-restrict checks and "which layouts use this property" on ontology change. The type FK is covered by the partial unique.
Security: RLS standard. Written by clone service, permission `canvas.save` or ontology owner. Update restricted by trigger to `superseded_at` only.

### `clone.state_rules`
Purpose: versioned, ordered CEL rules that derive a clone's display state from declared input properties, unusable until confirmed. Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `version` integer, not null. Starts at 1 per type. Immutable once used.
- `input_property_ids` uuid[], not null. Declared inputs.
- `rules` jsonb, not null. Ordered `{state, CEL, reason}`.
- `compiled_hash` text, not null. Shared by state plane and client.
- `freshness_window_seconds` integer, not null, default 900. Check: greater than 0.
- `marking_ids` uuid[], not null, default empty. Computed from inputs by the service, never supplied by the caller.
- `proposed_by` text. Changed: replaced by an exclusive arc `proposed_by_membership_id` uuid null and `proposed_by_service_principal_id` uuid null; check `num_nonnulls(proposed_by_membership_id, proposed_by_service_principal_id) = 1`. Changed (review 2026-10-28): `proposed_by_fde_principal_id → fde.fde_principals` renamed to `proposed_by_service_principal_id → iam.service_principals`, as every other AI FDE proposer column does.
- `confirmed_by` uuid, null. Membership. Check: `confirmed_by` and `confirmed_at` both null or both not null; `confirmed_by` is a membership, never the AI FDE principal.
- `confirmed_at` timestamptz, null. Unusable until set.
- `retired_at` timestamptz, null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
- `lock_version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, object_type_id, version)`; partial unique `(organisation_id, object_type_id) where confirmed_at is not null and retired_at is null`, one active rule set per type.
References: `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, proposed_by_membership_id)`, `(organisation_id, confirmed_by) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, proposed_by_service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals` (Changed (review 2026-10-28): was `proposed_by_fde_principal_id → fde.fde_principals`).
Indexes: the unique and partial unique above serve "active rule set for type" and "next version". GIN `(input_property_ids)` on the table, serving "which rules use this property" when an ontology change retires or alters a property (the query filters inside the array, so the GIN is justified; organisation isolation comes from RLS). `(organisation_id, proposed_by_service_principal_id)` partial where not null (Changed (review 2026-10-28): renamed), `(organisation_id, confirmed_by)` partial where not null, `(organisation_id, proposed_by_membership_id)` partial where not null, FK indexes. Proposal queue: `(organisation_id, created_at desc) where confirmed_at is null and retired_at is null`.
Security: RLS standard. Written by clone service, permission `state_rule.manage`. Trigger: once `confirmed_at` is set, `rules`, `input_property_ids`, `compiled_hash` and `version` are immutable; only `retired_at` may change.

### `clone.staleness_thresholds`
Purpose: the maximum age before a source's clones are declared stale, per connection and optionally per object type. Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `connection_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, null. Null means all types on the connection.
- `threshold_seconds` integer, not null. Check: greater than 0.
- `manifest_cadence_seconds` integer, not null. Declared by the connector manifest. Check: greater than 0.
- `set_by` uuid, not null. Membership.
- `set_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added. The audit event `staleness_threshold_changed` carries old and new values.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; partial unique `(organisation_id, connection_id) where object_type_id is null`; partial unique `(organisation_id, connection_id, object_type_id) where object_type_id is not null`.
References: `(organisation_id, connection_id) → connect.connections`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, set_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the two partial uniques serve the per-source stale check (connection first, then type override). `(organisation_id, object_type_id)` partial where not null for the type FK; `(organisation_id, set_by)`.
Security: RLS standard. Written by clone service, permission `state_rule.manage`.

### `clone.canvas_views`
Purpose: a saved Clone Canvas configuration (layout, camera, layers, filters, pins, overlay) owned by one membership. Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `owner_membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `name` text, not null.
- `canvas_scope` text, not null. Changed: renamed from `scope` to avoid confusion with `iam.scopes`. Values `object`, `set`, `estate_ontology`, `estate_map`.
- `object_set_ref` uuid, null. Set definition including filters. Check: not null when `canvas_scope` in (`object`, `set`); null when `estate_ontology` or `estate_map`.
- `layout_kind` text, not null. Values `schematic`, `graph_force`, `graph_layered`, `spatial_map`, `spatial_3d`, `hierarchy`, `timeline`, `list`. Changed: spec says "Layout or list"; values taken from chapter 29.2, confirm against the final layout catalogue.
- `plan_id` uuid, null. Check: only when `layout_kind = 'spatial_map'`.
- `asset_model_id` uuid, null. Check: only when `layout_kind = 'spatial_3d'`.
- `camera` jsonb, not null, default `{}`. Centre, zoom, bearing, pitch; 3D position and target.
- `layers` jsonb, not null, default `{}`. Toggles.
- `focus` jsonb, not null, default `{}`. Depth and focal references. Changed: spec lists `layers, focus` as one row; two columns.
- `state_filter` text[], not null, default empty.
- `pinned_object_refs` uuid[], not null, default empty. Check: `cardinality <= 200`.
- `scenario_id` uuid, null. Overlay.
- `favourited` boolean, not null, default false. Promotes to dashboard; kept in step with `workspace.dashboard_tiles` in one transaction.
- `ontology_version` bigint, not null. At save.
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `deleted_at` timestamptz, null.
- `archived_at` timestamptz, null. Added, for the transfer rule.
- `transferred_from_membership_id` uuid, null. Added, to match `workspace.saved_views` (spec 37.7 transfers "every view").
- `transferred_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
- `visibility` text, not null, default `private`. Added. Values `private`, `shared`, `org_visible`. Canvas shares use the view share tables (chapter 57, resolved here as `workspace.view_shares`).
- `lock_version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id)`, `(organisation_id, transferred_from_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, object_set_ref) → ontology.object_sets`; `(organisation_id, plan_id) → clone.spatial_plans`; `(organisation_id, asset_model_id) → clone.asset_models`; `(organisation_id, scenario_id) → simulation.scenarios`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id, updated_at desc) where deleted_at is null and archived_at is null`, "my canvas views" list and Clones page; `(organisation_id, object_set_ref) where object_set_ref is not null`; `(organisation_id, plan_id) where plan_id is not null` and `(organisation_id, asset_model_id) where asset_model_id is not null`, used when a plan or model is purged and its views fall back; `(organisation_id, scenario_id) where scenario_id is not null`; `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id) where favourited and deleted_at is null` for Home favourites.
Security: RLS standard. Written by clone service, permission `canvas.save`; sharing `canvas.share`. Open with permission re-check follows the same rule as saved views (37.5).

### `clone.spatial_plans`
Purpose: an uploaded floor plan or site plan held in a Silo, rasterised for the canvas. Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null. Holding Silo.
- `silo_file_id` uuid, not null. The uploaded file. Changed (review 2026-10-28): was `file_id → files.files`; the stored object is `siloes.silo_files`.
- `raster_tileset_ref` text, not null. Storage key inside the Silo.
- `name` text, not null.
- `width_px`, `height_px` integer, not null. Check: greater than 0.
- `control_points` jsonb, null. Georeferencing pairs.
- `marking_ids` uuid[], not null. At least the Silo's; the service enforces the superset.
- `uploaded_by` uuid, not null. Membership.
- `uploaded_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `purged_at` timestamptz, null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id) → siloes.siloes`; `(organisation_id, silo_id, silo_file_id) → siloes.silo_files (organisation_id, silo_id, id)` (Changed (review 2026-10-28): one composite reference, so the Silo and the file cannot disagree; was `(organisation_id, file_id) → files.files`); `(organisation_id, uploaded_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, silo_id) where purged_at is null`, plans in a Silo and Silo purge; `(organisation_id, silo_file_id)` (Changed (review 2026-10-28): was `(organisation_id, file_id)`); `(organisation_id, uploaded_by)`; picker `(organisation_id, uploaded_at desc) where purged_at is null`.
Security: RLS standard. Written by clone service, permission `asset.upload`. Purge sets `purged_at`; row kept for audit; the tileset is deleted inside the Silo by the Silo purge receipt.

### `clone.asset_models`
Purpose: an uploaded glTF 2.0 binary 3D model held in a Silo. Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_file_id` uuid, not null. The `.glb`. Changed (review 2026-10-28): was `file_id → files.files`; the stored object is `siloes.silo_files`.
- `name` text, not null.
- `format` text, not null, default `gltf2_glb`. Check: in (`gltf2_glb`).
- `bytes` bigint, not null. Check: greater than 0.
- `lod_refs` text[], not null, default empty. Level-of-detail storage keys inside the Silo.
- `validation_report` jsonb, not null. Validator result, stripped extensions; no geometry.
- `node_names` text[], not null, default empty. For anchoring.
- `marking_ids` uuid[], not null.
- `uploaded_by` uuid, not null.
- `uploaded_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `purged_at` timestamptz, null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id) → siloes.siloes`; `(organisation_id, silo_id, silo_file_id) → siloes.silo_files (organisation_id, silo_id, id)` (Changed (review 2026-10-28): one composite reference, so the Silo and the file cannot disagree; was `(organisation_id, file_id) → files.files`); `(organisation_id, uploaded_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: as `clone.spatial_plans`: `(organisation_id, silo_id) where purged_at is null`; `(organisation_id, silo_file_id)` (Changed (review 2026-10-28): was `(organisation_id, file_id)`); `(organisation_id, uploaded_by)`.
Security: RLS standard. Written by clone service, permission `asset.upload`. A rejected model (audit `asset_model_rejected`) is never inserted.

### `clone.spatial_anchors`
Purpose: places one object, or all objects matching a rule, on a plan (pixel position) or a model node. Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `plan_id` uuid, null; `asset_model_id` uuid, null. Changed: `target_kind` removed and replaced by this exclusive arc; check `num_nonnulls(plan_id, asset_model_id) = 1`.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_ref` uuid, null; `match_rule` text, null. Check: `num_nonnulls(object_ref, match_rule) = 1`. `match_rule` is a CEL predicate a person wrote, configuration not a record value.
- `plan_x`, `plan_y` numeric, null. Plan pixels. Check: both null or both not null; only when `plan_id` is not null.
- `model_node_name` text, null. Check: only when `asset_model_id` is not null; exactly one of (`plan_x`, `model_node_name`) is not null.
- `created_by` uuid, not null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `removed_at` timestamptz, null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, plan_id) → clone.spatial_plans`; `(organisation_id, asset_model_id) → clone.asset_models`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, plan_id) where removed_at is null and plan_id is not null`, load anchors when drawing a plan; `(organisation_id, asset_model_id) where removed_at is null and asset_model_id is not null`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id, object_ref) where removed_at is null and object_ref is not null`, find where an object is anchored; `(organisation_id, created_by)`.
Security: RLS standard. Written by clone service, permission `asset.upload` plus clearance on every anchored type.

### `clone.live_subscriptions`
Purpose: metadata for a live subscription so a lost state-plane node can be rebuilt and bounds counted; values stay in Redis (`redis-state`). Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `holder_kind` text, not null. Values `session`, `cron`. Check ties it to the arc below.
- `membership_id` uuid, null; `session_id` uuid, null; `cron_id` uuid, null. Exclusive arc on holder: check `num_nonnulls(session_id, cron_id) = 1`; when `holder_kind = 'session'`, `session_id` and `membership_id` are not null and `cron_id` is null; when `'cron'`, `cron_id` is not null and `session_id` is null.
- `object_set_ref` uuid, not null.
- `property_ids` uuid[], not null. Watched properties and inputs.
- `projection_hash` text, not null. Effective field projection (a hash, no values).
- `object_count` integer, not null. For bounds. Check: not negative.
- `connection_ids` uuid[], not null. Sources serving the set.
- `state_plane_node` text, not null. Owning node.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `last_heartbeat_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `ended_at` timestamptz, null.
- `end_reason` text, null. Values `closed`, `expired`, `revoked`, `bound`. Check: not null if and only if `ended_at` is not null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, cron_id) → automation.automations`; `(organisation_id, object_set_ref) → ontology.object_sets`; `(organisation_id, session_id) → iam.sessions (organisation_id, id)`. Changed (review 2026-10-28): composite; `iam.sessions` has a nullable `organisation_id` and `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, state_plane_node) where ended_at is null`: rebuild a lost node's subscriptions.
- `(organisation_id, membership_id) include (object_count) where ended_at is null`: per-person bound count when opening a subscription.
- `(organisation_id) include (object_count) where ended_at is null`: organisation-wide bound (`live.bounds.manage`).
- `(organisation_id, cron_id) where cron_id is not null and ended_at is null`: cron subscription lookup.
- `(organisation_id, object_set_ref) where ended_at is null`: share an existing subscription for the same set.
- `(organisation_id, session_id) where session_id is not null`: FK. Added (review 2026-10-28).
- GIN `(connection_ids) where ended_at is null`: end subscriptions when a connection is revoked (filters inside the array).
- `(last_heartbeat_at) where ended_at is null`: cross-tenant expiry sweep run by `silo_migrate`; deliberately has no `organisation_id` lead.
- `(ended_at) where ended_at is not null`: cross-tenant 7-day sweep, same reason.
Security: RLS standard. Written by clone service. Ended rows are swept after 7 days (decision 5). Never stores values.

### `clone.layout_precomputations`
Purpose: records that a layout for an object set was precomputed and where the positions live in the state plane. Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_set_ref` uuid, not null.
- `set_definition_hash` text, not null.
- `ontology_version` bigint, not null.
- `layout_kind` text, not null. Same values as `clone.canvas_views.layout_kind`.
- `parameters` jsonb, not null, default `{}`.
- `node_count` integer, not null.
- `cache_key` text, not null. State plane key; positions are never stored here.
- `computed_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `expires_at` timestamptz, not null. Check: after `computed_at`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, cache_key)`.
References: `(organisation_id, object_set_ref) → ontology.object_sets`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, set_definition_hash, layout_kind, ontology_version)`, the lookup at canvas open; `(organisation_id, object_set_ref)` FK; `(expires_at)` cross-tenant sweep by `silo_migrate`.
Security: RLS standard. Written by clone service. Invalidated by service when membership changes by more than 5 percent or the ontology version changes (chapter 29.8). Expired rows swept (decision 5).

### `clone.render_selections`
Purpose: records which archetype or layout was chosen for a result, what else was offered and whether the person overrode it, to tune selection. Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `result_ref` uuid, not null. Data plane result id, no foreign key, never the result.
- `result_structure` jsonb, not null. Selection signals: counts and booleans only.
- `surface` text, not null. Values `view`, `canvas`.
- `chosen` text, not null. Archetype or layout name.
- `alternatives_offered` text[], not null, default empty.
- `user_override` boolean, not null, default false.
- `overridden_to` text, null. Check: not null if and only if `user_override`.
- `membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `recorded_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
Keys: primary key `(id, recorded_at)`; `unique (organisation_id, id, recorded_at)`. Changed: range-partitioned by month on `recorded_at`, because this is a high-volume insert-only telemetry table and retention must be a partition drop. Propose adding it to the ledger list in 00_conventions.md. No foreign keys into it.
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: BRIN `(recorded_at)`; `(organisation_id, surface, chosen, recorded_at)`, override-rate analysis per archetype. Membership FK index `(organisation_id, membership_id)`.
Security: RLS standard. Insert only, trigger rejects update and delete. Written by clone service. Retention by partition drop.

### `clone.view_preferences`
Purpose: a person's preferred representation for one saved view or canvas view. Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `saved_view_id` uuid, null; `canvas_view_id` uuid, null. Changed: `view_id` polymorphic ("saved view or canvas view") replaced by an exclusive arc; check `num_nonnulls(saved_view_id, canvas_view_id) = 1`.
- `membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `preferred_representation` text, not null. Values `prose`, `view`, `data` for saved views; `canvas`, `list` for canvas views. Check couples value set to the arm.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; partial unique `(organisation_id, membership_id, saved_view_id) where saved_view_id is not null`; partial unique `(organisation_id, membership_id, canvas_view_id) where canvas_view_id is not null`.
References: `(organisation_id, saved_view_id) → workspace.saved_views`; `(organisation_id, canvas_view_id) → clone.canvas_views`; `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the two partial uniques serve the read at view open. FK indexes `(organisation_id, saved_view_id) where saved_view_id is not null`, `(organisation_id, canvas_view_id) where canvas_view_id is not null`.
Security: RLS standard. Written by view service, only for the person's own membership.

### `clone.estate_snapshots`
Purpose: daily and post-discovery counts and id references of the Estate map, for comparing two times without Capture. Spec chapter 32.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `taken_at` timestamptz, not null. Daily and after each discovery run.
- `node_counts` jsonb, not null. Per kind and health state.
- `edge_counts` jsonb, not null.
- `node_refs` jsonb, not null. Ids present; no values.
- `discovery_run_id` uuid, null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; unique `(organisation_id, discovery_run_id) where discovery_run_id is not null`, one snapshot per run.
References: `(organisation_id, discovery_run_id) → connect.discovery_runs`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, taken_at desc)`, the "compare two times" picker and latest snapshot.
Security: RLS standard. Insert only (trigger rejects update and delete). Written by estate service. Retention: not specified in the spec; proposal, keep daily snapshots 13 months, run as a receipted delete by `silo_migrate`, flagged for chapter 70.

---

# Schema `workspace`

### `workspace.terminology_skins`
Purpose: per-organisation display labels for object types, link types, Action types and declared state values. Spec chapter 33.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, null; `link_type_id` uuid, null; `action_type_id` uuid, null. Changed: `target_kind` and `target_id` replaced by an exclusive arc; check `num_nonnulls(object_type_id, link_type_id, action_type_id) = 1`. The former kind `state_value` is an object type arm with `state_value` not null.
- `state_value` text, null. Declared enumeration value, not a record value. Check: only when `object_type_id` is not null.
- `label_singular` text, not null.
- `label_plural` text, null.
- `set_by` uuid, not null. Membership.
- `set_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `superseded_at` timestamptz, null. Never updated in place; a new row supersedes.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; three partial uniques where `superseded_at is null`: `(organisation_id, object_type_id, coalesce(state_value, ''))`, `(organisation_id, link_type_id)`, `(organisation_id, action_type_id)`, each with its own `is not null` predicate.
References: `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, link_type_id) → ontology.link_types`; `(organisation_id, action_type_id) → action.action_types`; `(organisation_id, set_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the partial uniques serve label resolution at every render, cached per policy version; `(organisation_id, set_by)`. The label set for an organisation is loaded whole: `(organisation_id) where superseded_at is null` for the bulk load.
Security: RLS standard. Written by workspace service, permission `org.terminology.manage`. Update restricted to `superseded_at`. Audit `terminology_skin_set`, `terminology_skin_superseded`.

### `workspace.workspace_preferences`
Purpose: per-person shell state and the "since last visit" marker for Home. Spec chapter 33.
Columns:
- `membership_id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `rail_collapsed` boolean, not null, default false.
- `ask_panel_open` boolean, not null, default false.
- `last_home_seen_at` timestamptz, null.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
Keys: primary key `(membership_id)`; `unique (organisation_id, membership_id)` (this is the tenant unique, since `id` is the membership id). Changed: no separate `id` column.
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the primary key serves the lookup on sign-in.
Security: RLS standard. Written by workspace service for the person's own row. Home advances `last_home_seen_at` only when the briefing is rendered, so the next briefing starts after what was shown.

### `workspace.favourites`
Purpose: a person's favourited objects, apps and scenarios, ordered for Home. Spec chapter 33.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, null; `object_ref` uuid, null; `app_id` uuid, null; `scenario_id` uuid, null. Changed: `resource_type` and `resource_id` (text) replaced by an exclusive arc. The object arm is the pair (`object_type_id`, `object_ref`); objects live in source systems so `object_ref` has no foreign key. Checks: `num_nonnulls(object_ref, app_id, scenario_id) = 1`; `object_type_id` is not null if and only if `object_ref` is not null. A favourited saved view or canvas view is not here; it uses `favourited` on its own table and a tile (33.6).
- `position` integer, not null. Order on Home.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; partial uniques `(organisation_id, membership_id, object_type_id, object_ref) where object_ref is not null`, `(organisation_id, membership_id, app_id) where app_id is not null`, `(organisation_id, membership_id, scenario_id) where scenario_id is not null`.
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, app_id) → workspace.apps`; `(organisation_id, scenario_id) → simulation.scenarios`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, membership_id, position)`, Home favourites in order; FK indexes `(organisation_id, app_id) where app_id is not null`, `(organisation_id, scenario_id) where scenario_id is not null`, `(organisation_id, object_type_id) where object_type_id is not null`. Inserts stamp `position` as max plus one inside the transaction.
Security: RLS standard. Written by view service for the person's own membership. An unfavourite is a physical delete here: Added exception because a favourite is a preference, not a record anything references; the audit event `view_unfavourited` or equivalent carries the history. Confirm with the conventions owner, or add `removed_at` and make the uniques partial on it.

### `workspace.object_view_layouts`
Purpose: the layout of an object view per object type, generated default or custom from a Studio app version. Spec chapter 34.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `ontology_version` bigint, not null. Type version validated against.
- `generated` boolean, not null. True for the generated default. Check: if `generated` then `app_version_id` is null, else not null.
- `app_version_id` uuid, null. Studio app version holding the custom definition.
- `status` text, not null. Values `active`, `superseded`, `invalid`.
- `created_by` uuid, null. Membership; null for generated.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added, for status changes.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; partial unique `(organisation_id, object_type_id) where status = 'active'`.
References: `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, app_version_id) → workspace.app_versions`; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the partial unique serves opening any object view; `(organisation_id, app_version_id) where app_version_id is not null`, invalidating layouts when an app version is superseded; `(organisation_id, created_by) where created_by is not null`.
Security: RLS standard. Written by studio service. Audit `layout_published`, `object_view_layout_invalidated`.

### `workspace.apps`
Purpose: a Studio app or object view layout definition container, with owner, visibility and current published version. Spec chapter 35.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `owner_membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `name` text, not null.
- `description` text, null. The tooltip (33.9). Changed: nullable.
- `kind` text, not null. Values `app`, `object_view_layout`.
- `visibility` text, not null, default `private`. Values `private`, `shared`, `published`.
- `current_version_id` uuid, null. Latest published version; deferrable initially deferred foreign key (circular with `app_versions`). Check in service: the version belongs to this app and is `published`.
- `generated_by` text, null. Values `ai_fde`. Check: in (`ai_fde`).
- `require_full_clearance` boolean, not null, default false.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
- `archived_at` timestamptz, null.
- `transferred_from_membership_id` uuid, null; `transferred_at` timestamptz, null. Both set together.
- `lock_version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id)`, `(organisation_id, transferred_from_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, current_version_id) → workspace.app_versions`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id, updated_at desc) where archived_at is null`, "my apps"; `(organisation_id, created_at desc) where archived_at is null and visibility = 'published'`, directory fallback; `(organisation_id, current_version_id) where current_version_id is not null`; `(organisation_id, transferred_from_membership_id) where transferred_from_membership_id is not null`; name search `gin (name gin_trgm_ops)` for the app picker and Cmd-K.
Security: RLS standard. Written by studio service. Archive is `archived_at`.

### `workspace.app_versions`
Purpose: an immutable-once-out-of-draft definition of an app, with validation, markings and review state. Spec chapter 35.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `app_id` uuid, not null.
- `version` integer, not null.
- `state` text, not null. Values `draft`, `review`, `published`, `returned`, `superseded`.
- `definition` jsonb, not null. Immutable once `state` is not `draft`.
- `schema_version` text, not null.
- `ontology_version` bigint, not null. Validated against.
- `markings` uuid[], not null, default empty. Union of markings on referenced elements, computed from `workspace.app_references`.
- `invalidated_at_ontology_version` bigint, null. The ontology version at which an open last found widgets of this version invalid; app_invalidated_by_ontology_change is raised once per version and ontology version (D165).
- `validation_findings` jsonb, not null, default `[]`. Empty for a publishable version.
- `rolled_back_from_version` integer, null.
- `authored_by` uuid, not null.
- `reviewed_by` uuid, null. Check: differs from `authored_by`; not null when `state` is `published` unless the version is a rollback republish approved by the same publish permission (service rule).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `reviewed_at` timestamptz, null; `published_at` timestamptz, null.
- `lock_version` integer, not null, default 1. Added, for draft co-editing.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, app_id, version)`.
References: `(organisation_id, app_id) → workspace.apps`; `(organisation_id, authored_by)`, `(organisation_id, reviewed_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique serves version history and next-version allocation. Review queue `(organisation_id, created_at) where state = 'review'`. `(organisation_id, authored_by)`, `(organisation_id, reviewed_by) where reviewed_by is not null`.
Security: RLS standard. Written by studio service. Trigger: once `state` leaves `draft`, `definition`, `schema_version`, `ontology_version`, `markings` are immutable; state changes follow the lifecycle only.

### `workspace.app_references`
Purpose: which ontology elements an app version references, with the widgets that use each, for impact analysis and marking union. Spec chapter 35.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Added; the spec's composite key cannot span an arc.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `app_version_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, null; `property_id` uuid, null; `link_type_id` uuid, null; `action_type_id` uuid, null; `function_id` uuid, null. Changed: `element_kind` and `element_id` replaced by an exclusive arc; check `num_nonnulls(object_type_id, property_id, link_type_id, action_type_id, function_id) = 1`.
- `widget_ids` text[], not null. Widgets in the definition that reference the element.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; five partial uniques `(organisation_id, app_version_id, <arm column>) where <arm column> is not null`, restoring the spec's uniqueness per version and element.
References: `(organisation_id, app_version_id) → workspace.app_versions`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, property_id) → ontology.properties`; `(organisation_id, link_type_id) → ontology.link_types`; `(organisation_id, action_type_id) → action.action_types`; `(organisation_id, function_id) → ontology.functions`.
Indexes: the partial uniques cover per-version lookups. For "which apps use this element" on ontology change, one index per arm `(organisation_id, <arm column>) where <arm column> is not null`, five in total.
Security: RLS standard. Written by studio service in the same transaction as the version. Rows of a version past draft are immutable (trigger).

### `workspace.app_shares`
Purpose: a share of an app with a membership, a scope or the whole organisation at an access level. Spec chapter 35, model of 37.4.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `app_id` uuid, not null.
- `membership_id` uuid, null; `scope_id` uuid, null; `organisation_wide` boolean, null. Changed: `shared_with_type` and `shared_with_id` replaced by an exclusive arc; check `num_nonnulls(membership_id, scope_id, organisation_wide) = 1` and `organisation_wide` is true when not null.
- `access` text, not null. Values `view`, `run`, `copy`, `edit`.
- `shared_by` uuid, not null. Must be the current owner (service rule, re-checked at resolution).
- `shared_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `expires_at`, `revoked_at`, `suspended_at` timestamptz, null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; partial uniques `(organisation_id, app_id, membership_id) where membership_id is not null`, `(organisation_id, app_id, scope_id) where scope_id is not null`, `(organisation_id, app_id) where organisation_wide`. Re-sharing updates the row and clears `revoked_at`.
References: `(organisation_id, app_id) → workspace.apps`; `(organisation_id, membership_id)`, `(organisation_id, shared_by) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, scope_id) → iam.scopes`.
Indexes: "apps shared with me" `(organisation_id, membership_id) where membership_id is not null and revoked_at is null and suspended_at is null`; `(organisation_id, scope_id) where scope_id is not null and revoked_at is null and suspended_at is null`; the organisation-wide partial unique serves the third arm; `(organisation_id, shared_by)`; expiry sweep `(expires_at) where revoked_at is null and expires_at is not null`, run cross-tenant.
Security: RLS standard. Written by studio service. No deletes; revocation sets `revoked_at`.

### `workspace.app_publications`
Purpose: publishes an app version to a scope subtree and makes it eligible for mobile. Spec chapter 35.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `app_id` uuid, not null.
- `app_version_id` uuid, not null. Advanced on each publish.
- `scope_id` uuid, not null. Scope subtree root.
- `mobile_enabled` boolean, not null, default false.
- `published_by` uuid, not null. Holder of `app.publish` at `scope_id`.
- `published_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `withdrawn_at` timestamptz, null.
