# Schema `recognition` (chapter 38)

### `recognition.detectors`
Purpose: registry of the ten detectors, global and authored by Silo; findings, runs, thresholds and Cron conditions refer to it instead of a name string. Spec chapter 38 (38.2); added to close the stress-test finding on the missing detectors registry.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Primary key. Seeded with fixed UUIDs so every cell holds the same ids.
- `key` text, not null. Stable machine name, lower snake case, for example `disagreement`. Referenced by code and by seeds, never renamed.
- `name` text, not null. Display name.
- `description` text, not null. One sentence stating the fact the detector computes (never a judgement).
- `execution_mode` text, not null. `federated` or `history`. Check. Seven rows are `federated`, three are `history` (timing deviation, drift, recurrence).
- `requires_property` boolean, not null. True when the customer must name the property to examine. Seven of the ten rows are true (38.2).
- `requires_time_field` boolean, not null. True when a time field must be named. All three `history` rows are true unless the built code says otherwise.
- `minimum_baseline` jsonb, null. Declared minimum history as `{"amount": n, "unit": "days"|"transitions"}`. Check: not null exactly when `execution_mode = 'history'`. Used to produce the `accumulating_baseline` run state with "have and need".
- `current_version` text, not null. Version string stamped on every run (`detector_runs.detector_version`). Changes only with a release of the recognition service.
- `status` text, not null, default `active`. `active` or `retired`. Check.
- `retired_at` timestamptz, null. Set with `status = 'retired'`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added. Set by trigger.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (key)`; `unique (name)`.
References: none.
Indexes: none beyond the keys. The table holds ten rows.
Security: global table, no `organisation_id`, so no RLS and no tenant FKs. `silo_app` has `select` only. Rows are written by `silo_migrate` (Fleet migration seeds). Not tenant data, so not purged with an organisation.
Seed rule: the seed for `disagreement`, `timing_deviation`, `drift` and `recurrence` is known from the spec. The other six federated detectors are not named anywhere in the source set (checked: chapter 38, spec 04 v2, spec 06). Their `key`, `name`, `description`, `requires_property` and `current_version` must be copied from the v1 recognition specification or from the built recognition service before the seed is written. The migration must fail if fewer than ten active rows exist after seeding, so the gap cannot be shipped silently.

### `recognition.detector_runs`
Purpose: one execution of one detector over one object type, recording what the detector did even when it produced nothing. Spec chapter 38 (38.2, 38.12).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. The run marker (38.3): a finding raised again in a later run is a different finding under a different run.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `detector_id` uuid, not null. Added. Changed: replaces `detector` text ("name and version"); version moves to `detector_version`.
- `detector_version` text, not null. Added. Version of the detector code that ran.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `properties` text[], not null, default empty. Configured property names (names only, not an FK array; they are property names of the object type). Empty when the detector requires none.
- `state` text, not null. `ran`, `not_configured`, `accumulating_baseline`, `history_unavailable`, `source_unreachable`, `bounded`. Check.
- `state_detail` jsonb, null. Added. For `source_unreachable` the connection ids named; for `bounded` the bound and the population size seen. Identifiers and counts only.
- `population_count` bigint, null. Changed: nullable. Check: not null when `state = 'ran'`.
- `baseline` jsonb, null. `{"have": ..., "need": ...}`. Check: not null when `state = 'accumulating_baseline'`, null otherwise.
- `findings_count` integer, not null, default 0. Check: `findings_count = 0` unless `state = 'ran'`.
- `run_by_membership_id` uuid, null. Added. The member who ran it on demand (`recognition.run`); null for scheduled runs. Findings are visible by marking, so who ran it is evidence.
- `started_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `completed_at` timestamptz, null. Null while running.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id, detector_id)` and `unique (organisation_id, id, detector_id, object_type_id)` (targets for the findings FK).
References:
- `(detector_id) → recognition.detectors (id)` (global, not composite).
- `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`.
- `(organisation_id, run_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, object_type_id, detector_id, started_at desc)`: latest run per detector on an object type (run response, threshold reuse, "has this detector run").
- `(organisation_id, started_at desc)`: run history list screen.
- `(organisation_id, detector_id, started_at desc)`: runs of one detector; FK index. Added (review 2026-10-28).
Security: RLS standard. Written by `recognition`. No retention stated; rows are small.

### `recognition.findings`
Purpose: a stated fact about named objects, produced by one detector in one run, holding references and counts and never record values. Spec chapter 38 (38.3, 38.12).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `detector_run_id` uuid, not null.
- `detector_id` uuid, not null. Added. Denormalised from the run and held consistent by the composite FK; lets tuning and Cron finding conditions filter without a join.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_refs` jsonb, not null. Identifiers only, as in the spec; kept as the full reference for display. The queryable copy is `recognition.finding_objects`.
- `properties` text[], not null. Property names only.
- `computation` jsonb, not null. Statistic, threshold crossed, population, sample size. Never record values.
- `coverage` jsonb, not null. Counts of decided, disputed, empty, unchecked.
- `org_disposition` text, null. Organisation disposition under `finding.disposition`. `confirmed`, `dismissed` or `deferred`. Check. Values are not stated in the spec for the organisation disposition; they mirror the Lens set (38.9).
- `org_disposition_by` uuid, null. Added. Membership that recorded it. Check: set together with `org_disposition_at` and `org_disposition`.
- `org_disposition_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
- `superseded_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Set when a later run of the same detector on the same object type no longer raises, or re-raises, this finding. A finding is current when this is null (38.10 "every current finding").
- `raised_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added. Optimistic lock for disposition writes.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Changed: `connection_ids uuid[]` and `marking_ids uuid[]` are replaced by `recognition.finding_connections` and `recognition.finding_markings`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id, detector_id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id, object_type_id)`.
References:
- `(organisation_id, detector_run_id, detector_id, object_type_id) → recognition.detector_runs (organisation_id, id, detector_id, object_type_id)`.
- `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`.
- `(organisation_id, org_disposition_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, detector_run_id)`: FK, and "findings of a run".
- `(organisation_id, object_type_id, raised_at desc) where superseded_at is null`: current findings list per object type.
- `(organisation_id, detector_id, object_type_id, org_disposition_at) where org_disposition is not null`: the five-decision floor and the dismissed/confirmed ratio for tuning (38.5).
- `(organisation_id, detector_id, raised_at desc)`: findings of one detector. Added (review 2026-10-28).
Security: RLS standard. Visibility additionally requires the viewer to hold every marking in `finding_markings` (checked by the service and by the query joined to the viewer's clearances). Written by `recognition`. After creation only `org_disposition*`, `superseded_at`, `version`, `updated_at` change. A Siloes purge never deletes a finding (38.3).
Open decision carried: a second reviewer for dispositions on marked object types (38.14). If adopted, add `org_disposition_status` and `second_reviewer_id`; not added now.

### `recognition.finding_objects`
Purpose: queryable list of the objects a finding names, so "findings on this object" is an index lookup instead of a jsonb scan. Added; spec chapter 38 (38.10, requirement for object views and clones).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `finding_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null. Denormalised from the finding, held consistent by the composite FK.
- `object_key` text, not null. The resolved-object identifier that object views and clones are keyed by (chapters 29 and 34). An identifier, not a record value.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, finding_id, object_key)`.
References:
- `(organisation_id, finding_id, object_type_id) → recognition.findings (organisation_id, id, object_type_id)`.
- `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`.
Indexes:
- `unique (organisation_id, object_type_id, object_key, finding_id)`: findings panel on an object view, clone icon lookup, "finding recurred" Cron condition.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `recognition` in the same transaction as the finding. Insert only. The author of the ontology domain must confirm that `object_key` is the identity key used by Explorer and object views; if it is a composite of connection and source key, replace the column with that pair.

### `recognition.finding_connections`
Purpose: the connections that contributed to a finding. Added; replaces `findings.connection_ids uuid[]`. Spec chapter 38.
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `finding_id` uuid, not null.
- `connection_id` uuid, not null.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, finding_id, connection_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, finding_id) → recognition.findings`; `(organisation_id, connection_id) → connect.connections`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, connection_id)`: findings that depend on a halted or removed connection (FK index).
Security: RLS standard. Insert only; written by `recognition`.

### `recognition.finding_markings`
Purpose: the markings propagated onto a finding; a viewer must hold all of them. Added; replaces `findings.marking_ids uuid[]`. Spec chapter 38 (38.3, 38.11).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `finding_id` uuid, not null.
- `marking_id` uuid, not null.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, finding_id, marking_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, finding_id) → recognition.findings`; `(organisation_id, marking_id) → gov.markings`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, marking_id)`: FK, and marking declassification fan-out.
Security: RLS standard. Insert only; written by `recognition`.

### `recognition.finding_scores`
Purpose: how much a finding is worth looking at, within its own detector. Spec chapter 38 (38.3).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `finding_id` uuid, not null.
- `detector_id` uuid, not null. Added. Scores are not comparable across detectors, so every list sorts within one detector.
- `score` numeric, not null.
- `computed_at` timestamptz, not null.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, finding_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, finding_id, detector_id) → recognition.findings (organisation_id, id, detector_id)`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, detector_id, score desc)`: findings list ordered by score within a detector. The FK is covered by the primary key.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `recognition`; one row per finding, replaced when the score is recomputed.

### `recognition.finding_links`
Purpose: links between findings about the same records. Spec chapter 38 (38.3, 38.10).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `finding_id` uuid, not null.
- `linked_finding_id` uuid, not null.
- `shared_refs_count` integer, not null. Check `> 0`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, finding_id, linked_finding_id)`. Check `finding_id <> linked_finding_id`. Each link is stored in both directions (two rows, one transaction) so a lookup by `finding_id` is complete.
References: `(organisation_id, finding_id) → recognition.findings`; `(organisation_id, linked_finding_id) → recognition.findings`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, linked_finding_id)`: FK index.
Security: RLS standard. Insert only; written by `recognition`.

### `recognition.detector_thresholds`
Purpose: the persisted threshold per detector, object type and optional property, derived from the population and tuned only by organisation dispositions. Spec chapter 38 (38.5).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `detector_id` uuid, not null. Changed: replaces `detector` text.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `property` text, null. Property name; null when the threshold is not per property.
- `value` numeric, not null. A statistic.
- `origin` text, not null. `derived` or `tuned`. Check.
- `tuned` boolean, not null, default false. Check: `tuned = (origin = 'tuned')`. Only an actual adjustment sets it.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added. Optimistic lock for concurrent tuning.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique nulls not distinct (organisation_id, detector_id, object_type_id, property)`.
References: `(detector_id) → recognition.detectors (id)`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`.
Indexes: the unique key serves the per-run lookup. `(organisation_id, object_type_id)`: FK.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `recognition`. Every movement is audited as `threshold_tuned` with its evidence; the table keeps only the current value. No cross-tenant read.

### `recognition.association_computations`
Purpose: one association analysis run, so "an earlier set existed" is a real reference. Added; replaces the bare `computation_id` and `supersedes_computation_id` columns. Spec chapter 38 (38.6).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. This is the `computation_id` of the spec.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `supersedes_computation_id` uuid, null. Changed: moved here from `associations`. The computation this one replaced.
- `computed_by_membership_id` uuid, null. Null when scheduled.
- `computed_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, supersedes_computation_id) → recognition.association_computations`; `(organisation_id, computed_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, computed_at desc)`: latest computation; `(organisation_id, supersedes_computation_id) where supersedes_computation_id is not null`: FK.
Security: RLS standard. Insert only; written by `recognition`. Outcome designation, an open point here before, has its own table: `recognition.outcome_designations` (D151).

### `recognition.associations`
Purpose: a co-occurrence between two populations with sample size always stated, in fixed language. Spec chapter 38 (38.6).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `computation_id` uuid, not null.
- `left_object_type_id` uuid, not null. Changed: `left_ref jsonb` becomes a typed side.
- `left_property` text, null. Property name on the left object type.
- `left_detector_id` uuid, null. Finding kind on the left object type.
- `right_object_type_id` uuid, not null. Changed: as above.
- `right_property` text, null.
- `right_detector_id` uuid, null.
- `link_type_id` uuid, null. Added (D151). Set when the two populations are on types a link type joins ("is linked through"); no reference, as with the object type columns.
- `link_direction` text, null. Added (D151). `forward` or `reverse`: which way the link type was read. Set exactly when `link_type_id` is; a same-type association has no link.
- `co_occurrence_count` bigint, not null. Check `>= 0`.
- `sample_size` bigint, not null. Check `> 0` and `co_occurrence_count <= sample_size`.
- `temporal_order` jsonb, null. Counts for "precedes in N of M instances". Counts only.
- `statement` text, not null. Fixed language. Check: does not match `\m(cause|causes|caused|drive|drives|driven)\M` (case-insensitive), which enforces the rule in 38.6 at the database.
- `computed_at` timestamptz, not null.
Each side is an exclusive arc: `num_nonnulls(left_property, left_detector_id) = 1`, and the same for the right side.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, computation_id) → recognition.association_computations`; `(organisation_id, left_object_type_id)` and `(organisation_id, right_object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(left_detector_id)` and `(right_detector_id) → recognition.detectors (id)`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, computation_id)`: the set of one computation (also the FK index); `(organisation_id, left_object_type_id)` and `(organisation_id, right_object_type_id)`: FK indexes, and "what co-occurs with this object type" in Investigation.
Security: RLS standard. Insert only after computation; written by `recognition`. If the built code stores value-bucket populations in the refs, keep a `*_qualifier jsonb` of names only; no record values.

### `recognition.outcome_designations`
Purpose: an outcome of interest for association analysis: a yes/no property of a type, or a finding kind (a detector) on it. Designation never changes what a detector raises. Added (D151). Spec chapter 38 (38.6).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `property` text, null. A boolean property's API name: a name, never a value.
- `detector_id` uuid, null. The finding kind.
- `designated_by` uuid, not null. The membership holding `outcome.designate`.
- `designated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `revoked_by` uuid, null; `revoked_at` timestamptz, null. Revoked, never deleted; both or neither.
Exclusive arc: `num_nonnulls(property, detector_id) = 1`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; one live designation of an outcome: unique `(organisation_id, object_type_id, coalesce(property, ''), coalesce(detector_id::text, '')) where revoked_at is null`.
References: `(detector_id) → recognition.detectors (id)`; `(organisation_id, designated_by)` and `(organisation_id, revoked_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, object_type_id) where revoked_at is null`: the live outcomes of a type; the membership FKs.
Security: RLS standard. Insert, and update to revoke; written by `recognition`. `outcome_designated` is audited on both, with the change.

### `recognition.lenses`
Purpose: a person's private working layer over the shared ontology, owned by a membership. Spec chapter 38 (38.9).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `membership_id` uuid, not null. Owner. A person in two organisations has separate Lenses.
- `name` text, not null.
- `working_sets` jsonb, not null, default `[]`. Set definitions and reference lists. References, counts and definitions only; no record values (binding rule 38.9).
- `counts` jsonb, null. Added. Counts at last evaluation.
- `evaluated_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
- `archived_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Removal is a status change.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added. Optimistic lock.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, membership_id, name) where archived_at is null`.
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the name unique index serves the workspace header Lens selector (a member's live Lenses). No GIN on `working_sets`: nothing filters inside it.
Security: RLS standard plus an owner rule in the service: private by default, readable by others only through a live `lens_shares` row. Written by `recognition`.

### `recognition.lens_dispositions`
Purpose: a person's disposition on a finding within a Lens; personal, never counts toward thresholds. Spec chapter 38 (38.9).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `lens_id` uuid, not null.
- `finding_id` uuid, not null.
- `disposition` text, not null. `confirmed`, `dismissed`, `deferred`. Check.
- `recorded_at` timestamptz, not null. Updated when the disposition changes.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, lens_id, finding_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, lens_id) → recognition.lenses`; `(organisation_id, finding_id) → recognition.findings`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, finding_id)`: FK. The primary key serves "dispositions of this finding in the active Lens" and "all dispositions in a Lens".
Security: RLS standard. Written by `recognition`. Cron finding conditions ignore this table by design (a finding silenced in a Lens still satisfies a condition).

### `recognition.lens_links`
Purpose: reinforced links, written when a question genuinely relates two object types through a join. Spec chapter 38 (38.9).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `lens_id` uuid, not null.
- `link_type_id` uuid, not null. Route the question took.
- `reinforcement_count` integer, not null, default 1. Check `> 0`.
- `last_reinforced_at` timestamptz, not null.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, lens_id, link_type_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, lens_id) → recognition.lenses`; `(organisation_id, link_type_id) → ontology.link_types`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, link_type_id)`: FK.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `recognition` (and the planner through it).

### `recognition.lens_shares`
Purpose: a share of a Lens with a membership, a scope or the whole organisation. Spec chapter 38 (38.9).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `lens_id` uuid, not null.
- `grantee_membership_id` uuid, null. Changed: exclusive arc replaces `grantee_type` and `grantee_id`.
- `grantee_scope_id` uuid, null.
- `grantee_whole_organisation` boolean, null. Holds true or null (check `grantee_whole_organisation is true or null`); true means the whole organisation.
- `access` text, not null. `view`, `use`, `copy`. Check.
- `coverage_at_share` numeric, not null. Proportion the recipient can see, 0 to 1. Check. Recorded because "they can see 12% of it" decides whether a share was meaningful.
- `shared_by` uuid, not null.
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
- `revoked_by` uuid, null. Added.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Arc check: `num_nonnulls(grantee_membership_id, grantee_scope_id, grantee_whole_organisation) = 1`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`. Live uniqueness, one per grantee: `unique (organisation_id, lens_id, grantee_membership_id) where revoked_at is null and grantee_membership_id is not null`; the same on `grantee_scope_id`; `unique (organisation_id, lens_id) where revoked_at is null and grantee_whole_organisation`.
References: `(organisation_id, lens_id) → recognition.lenses`; `(organisation_id, grantee_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, grantee_scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, shared_by)` and `revoked_by → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the three partial unique indexes above serve the share dialogue and the FK on `lens_id`. `(organisation_id, grantee_membership_id) where revoked_at is null and grantee_membership_id is not null` and `(organisation_id, grantee_scope_id) where revoked_at is null and grantee_scope_id is not null`: "Lenses shared with me".
Security: RLS standard. Written by `recognition`. Permission is re-checked on every open (38.9); the share grants visibility, never authorisation.

---

# Schema `simulation` (chapter 39)

### `simulation.graph_state`
Purpose: the organisation's current graph version, incremented on every edge confirmation, revision or retirement. Added; spec chapter 39 (39.3) requires the counter but defines no table.
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `graph_version` bigint, not null, default 0.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id)` is the tenant key; no other FK.
Indexes: none.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `simulation`. The service updates this row first (row lock), uses the new value for the edge change and the `edge_revisions` row in the same transaction, which serialises graph changes per organisation.

### `simulation.dependency_edges`
Purpose: a directed dependency between two object types, evaluated over a link type, which is live only after a person confirms it. Spec chapter 39 (39.2, 39.3, 39.11).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `from_object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `to_object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `via_link_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `kind` text, not null. `hard`, `soft`, `resource`. Check.
- `lead_time` jsonb, null. `{"value": n, "unit": "..."}`. Changed: nullable while proposed; check not null when confirmed, and `jsonb_typeof = 'object'` with keys `value` and `unit`.
- `buffer` jsonb, null. Same shape.
- `source` text, not null. `structure`, `history`, `stated`. Check. Check: a confirmed edge never has source `structure` (39.3: structure is proposals only).
- `evidence_ref` jsonb, null. Changed: nullable. Reference to the evidence (observation window, sample count). References only.
- `status` text, not null, default `proposed`. Added. `proposed`, `confirmed`, `retired`. Checks: `proposed` has null `confirmed_at` and `retired_at`; `confirmed` has `confirmed_by` and `confirmed_at` set and null `retired_at`; `retired` has `retired_at` set.
- `proposed_by_membership_id` uuid, null. Added. Person who ran derivation (`graph.propose`).
- `proposed_by_service_principal_id` uuid, null. Added. The AI FDE principal that proposed it. Arc: `num_nonnulls(proposed_by_membership_id, proposed_by_service_principal_id) = 1`.
- `confirmed_by` uuid, null. A membership only, so a principal can never confirm (invariant 9).
- `confirmed_at` timestamptz, null.
- `retired_at` timestamptz, null.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Optimistic lock; incremented on each revision.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, from_object_type_id, to_object_type_id, via_link_type_id, kind) where status <> 'retired'`.
References: `(organisation_id, from_object_type_id)` and `(organisation_id, to_object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, via_link_type_id) → ontology.link_types`; `(organisation_id, confirmed_by)` and `(organisation_id, proposed_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, proposed_by_service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, from_object_type_id) where status = 'confirmed'`: propagation walk, edges leaving a node, per hop.
- `(organisation_id, to_object_type_id)`: FK and reverse traversal.
- `(organisation_id, via_link_type_id)`: FK.
- `(organisation_id, created_at desc) where status = 'proposed'`: confirmation queue.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `simulation`. Rows are never deleted; retirement is `status = 'retired'`. Every change to `status`, `kind`, `lead_time`, `buffer` also writes an `edge_revisions` row.

### `simulation.edge_observations`
Purpose: observed lead-time statistics for an edge from Silo history, never values. Spec chapter 39 (39.3, 39.5).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Added.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `edge_id` uuid, not null.
- `sample_count` integer, not null. Check `>= 0`.
- `distribution` jsonb, not null. Statistics only.
- `observed_from` timestamptz, not null.
- `observed_to` timestamptz, not null. Check `observed_to >= observed_from`.
- `computed_at` timestamptz, not null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, edge_id, computed_at)`.
References: `(organisation_id, edge_id) → simulation.dependency_edges`.
Indexes: the unique key, read as `(organisation_id, edge_id, computed_at desc)`: latest observation per edge when a probabilistic run starts (also the FK index).
Security: RLS standard. Insert only; written by `simulation`. A history edge with no row here cannot be sampled and is computed deterministically (39.5).

### `simulation.edge_revisions`
Purpose: append-only record of every confirmation, revision and retirement of an edge. Spec chapter 39 (39.3).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Added.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `edge_id` uuid, not null.
- `change_kind` text, not null. Added. `confirmed`, `revised`, `retired`. Check.
- `previous_state` jsonb, null. Null on first confirmation.
- `new_state` jsonb, not null.
- `reason` text, not null.
- `revised_by` uuid, not null. Membership.
- `graph_version` bigint, not null. Added. The version this change produced.
- `revised_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, graph_version)`.
References: `(organisation_id, edge_id) → simulation.dependency_edges`; `(organisation_id, revised_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, edge_id, revised_at desc)`: edge history and "was this edge confirmed differently since the run" (FK index).
Security: RLS standard. Append-only: trigger rejects update and delete, grants `insert, select`. Not partitioned; volume is human-paced. Written by `simulation`.

### `simulation.scenarios`
Purpose: a saved failure or branch scenario, rerunnable on current data and graph. Spec chapter 39 (39.7, 39.11).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `owner_membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `name` text, not null.
- `kind` text, not null. `failure` or `branch`. Check.
- `stated_failure` jsonb, null. Failure form and the named objects (identifiers only). Check: not null when `kind = 'failure'`, null when `kind = 'branch'`.
- `mode` text, not null. `deterministic`, `probabilistic`. Check.
- `bounds` jsonb, not null. Hops, fan-out, iterations.
- `graph_version` bigint, not null. Version at save.
- `archived_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id, created_at desc) where archived_at is null`: Scenarios list in the left rail.
Security: RLS standard. Private by default. Sharing uses the view share model (chapter 37): `workspace.view_shares` carries `simulation.scenarios` as the `scenario_id` arm of its exclusive arc (Changed (review 2026-10-28): done); this file does not add a second share table. Written by `simulation`.

### `simulation.scenario_branches`
Purpose: a branch of clone state in which Actions are staged and never executed. Spec chapter 39 (39.8). New in this version.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `scenario_id` uuid, not null. The scenario must have `kind = 'branch'` (enforced by the service).
- `name` text, not null.
- `created_by` uuid, not null.
- `status` text, not null, default `open`. `open`, `promoted`, `partially_promoted`, `closed`. Check.
- `retention` interval, not null. No default (default for closed branches is an open decision); bases purge at its end.
- `closed_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
- `bases_purge_at` timestamptz, null. Added. `closed_at + retention`, set at close.
- `bases_purged_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Set by the purge sweep.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, scenario_id, name)`.
References: `(organisation_id, scenario_id) → simulation.scenarios`; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique key serves branches of a scenario (FK). `(bases_purge_at) where bases_purge_at is not null and bases_purged_at is null`: retention sweep across organisations, run by `silo_migrate`; the one index in this domain without a leading `organisation_id`, because the sweep is cross-tenant.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `simulation`. Nothing in a branch writes to a source: no foreign key, trigger or service call from this schema reaches `action` execution tables other than the proposal entry (39.8 binding rule).

### `simulation.simulation_runs`
Purpose: one execution of a scenario or branch against current data and the current graph. Spec chapter 39 (39.7, 39.9, 39.11).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `scenario_id` uuid, not null.
- `branch_id` uuid, null. Set for branch runs.
- `run_by_membership_id` uuid, not null. Added. Runs execute under the opener's permissions.
- `mode` text, not null. `deterministic`, `probabilistic`. Check.
- `iterations` integer, null. Check: not null and `> 0` when `mode = 'probabilistic'`, null otherwise.
- `graph_version` bigint, not null.
- `status` text, not null, default `running`. Added. `running`, `completed`, `failed`. Check.
- `started_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `completed_at` timestamptz, null.
- `bounded_at_hop` integer, null.
- `metering_transaction_id` uuid, not null. Token or simulation-allowance transaction. No foreign key: `billing.token_transactions` is a partitioned append-only ledger and takes no inbound keys.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, scenario_id) → simulation.scenarios`; `(organisation_id, branch_id) → simulation.scenario_branches`; `(organisation_id, run_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, scenario_id, started_at desc)`: run history and comparison of runs of one scenario (FK). `(organisation_id, branch_id, started_at desc) where branch_id is not null`: branch runs (FK).
Security: RLS standard. Written by `simulation`. There is no scenario-wide headline probability column by design (39.5).

### `simulation.simulation_results`
Purpose: one affected object, or one stopping point, reached by a run, with its delay and probability; references only. Spec chapter 39 (39.4, 39.5, 39.6, 39.11).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Added.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `run_id` uuid, not null.
- `result_kind` text, not null. Added. `reached` or `stopped`. Check. A stopped path is stored as incomplete with its reason (39.3 binding rule, 39.6).
- `affected_object_type_id` uuid, null. Changed: `affected_object_ref jsonb` becomes a typed reference. Not null when `reached`.
- `affected_object_key` text, null. Resolved-object identifier. Not null when `reached`. Same identity key as `recognition.finding_objects.object_key`.
- `via_soft_edge` boolean, not null, default false. Added. Soft paths are reported apart from hard-only paths (39.4).
- `path_mode` text, not null. Added. `deterministic` or `probabilistic`, per path (39.5).
- `accumulated_delay` interval, null. In probabilistic paths, the median delay.
- `delay_spread` jsonb, null. Added. Spread for probabilistic paths, for example percentiles. Null when deterministic.
- `probability` numeric, null. Check between 0 and 1; null when `path_mode = 'deterministic'`.
- `stop_reason` text, null. Added. `unconfirmed_edge`, `bounded_hop`, `uncleared_object_type`. Not null exactly when `result_kind = 'stopped'`.
- `stop_edge_id` uuid, null. Added. Exclusive arc for the stopping point: the unconfirmed edge.
- `stop_object_type_id` uuid, null. Added. The object type the runner lacks clearance for.
- `stop_hop` integer, null. Added. The hop at which a bound stopped the walk.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Changed: `path uuid[]` and `edge_sources_on_path jsonb` are replaced by `simulation.simulation_result_edges`.
Arc check: when `result_kind = 'reached'`, `num_nonnulls(stop_edge_id, stop_object_type_id, stop_hop) = 0`; when `stopped`, it equals 1, and `stop_reason` agrees with the column set (`unconfirmed_edge` with `stop_edge_id`, `uncleared_object_type` with `stop_object_type_id`, `bounded_hop` with `stop_hop`).
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, run_id) → simulation.simulation_runs`; `(organisation_id, affected_object_type_id)` and `(organisation_id, stop_object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, stop_edge_id) → simulation.dependency_edges`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, run_id, affected_object_type_id, affected_object_key)`: results of a run, the table of affected objects, and comparison of two runs (objects entering or leaving); FK index on `run_id`.
- `(organisation_id, affected_object_type_id, affected_object_key, run_id)`: scenario run results by entity (object view "what scenarios reach this object").
- `(organisation_id, stop_edge_id) where stop_edge_id is not null`: FK, and the rate of `simulation_crossed_unconfirmed_edge`.
- `(organisation_id, stop_object_type_id) where stop_object_type_id is not null`: FK.
Security: RLS standard. Insert only; written by `simulation`. Results are references, delays and probabilities, never record values. Retention follows the owning scenario; results of an archived scenario are kept because runs are the record of what was concluded.

### `simulation.simulation_result_edges`
Purpose: the ordered edges on the path to one result, with the evidence behind each. Added; replaces `path uuid[]` and `edge_sources_on_path`. Spec chapter 39 (39.3: the source travels with every result).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `result_id` uuid, not null.
- `position` integer, not null. 1 is the edge leaving the origin. Check `>= 1`.
- `edge_id` uuid, not null.
- `edge_kind` text, not null. Kind of the edge at run time (`hard`, `soft`, `resource`). Check.
- `edge_source` text, not null. `structure`, `history`, `stated`. Check. The source at run time.
- `sample_size` integer, null. Null for stated edges.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, result_id, position)`.
References: `(organisation_id, result_id) → simulation.simulation_results`; `(organisation_id, edge_id) → simulation.dependency_edges`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, edge_id)`: FK, and "which results rest on this edge" when an edge is revised and runs stop being comparable.
Security: RLS standard. Insert only; written by `simulation` with the result row. Bulk-written by `copy`.

### `simulation.staged_actions`
Purpose: an Action staged in a branch, with its manifest, staleness and promotion state. Spec chapter 39 (39.8). New in this version.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `branch_id` uuid, not null.
- `sequence` integer, not null. Check `>= 1`.
- `action_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `manifest` jsonb, not null. Retention and purge as mutation manifests. Holds action type, targets as identifiers, parameter names and structure. Changed (rule): it must hold no record values; staged values are in `staged_action_bases.staged_value`.
- `staleness` text, not null, default `clean`. `clean`, `conflicted`, `already_applied`, `orphaned`. Check.
- `conflicts` jsonb, null. Per property: property name, who changed it where knowable, resolution (`keep_staged`, `take_current`, `re_stage`). Names and choices only, no values.
- `staged_by` uuid, not null.
- `promoted_action_id` uuid, null. The real Action created at promotion.
- `promoted_by` uuid, null.
- `promoted_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Check: `promoted_action_id`, `promoted_by`, `promoted_at` are all null or all set.
- `staleness_checked_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Last three-way check.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added. Optimistic lock for per-property conflict resolution.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, branch_id, sequence)`.
References: `(organisation_id, branch_id) → simulation.scenario_branches`; `(organisation_id, action_type_id) → action.action_types`; `(organisation_id, promoted_action_id) → action.mutations`; `(organisation_id, staged_by)` and `promoted_by → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique key serves a branch's staged Actions in order and the staleness count at the top of the branch (FK). `(organisation_id, action_type_id)`: FK. `(organisation_id, promoted_action_id) where promoted_action_id is not null`: receipt to staged Action back-reference.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `simulation`. No execution path exists from this table (39.8). The action domain's origin field on a promoted mutation should reference `staged_actions` through its own arc; named here so the action author adds it.

### `simulation.staged_action_bases`
Purpose: the prior value of every touched property on every target, read when staging, for the three-way staleness check. Spec chapter 39 (39.8). New in this version.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Added.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `staged_action_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null. Changed: `object_ref jsonb` becomes `object_type_id` plus `object_key`.
- `object_key` text, not null. Resolved-object identifier.
- `connection_id` uuid, not null.
- `property` text, not null. Property name; touched properties only, never the whole record.
- `base_value` bytea, null. Encrypted per the conventions (AES-256-GCM under the per-organisation data key). Changed from jsonb. Never indexed or logged. Null only when `purged_at` is set.
- `staged_value` bytea, null. Added. The value the staged Action would write, encrypted the same way. The spec's three-way check needs it and gives it no column; it is on the conventions list of encrypted columns (Changed (review 2026-10-28)). Null only when `purged_at` is set.
- `read_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `purged_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Set when the branch retention ends; `base_value` and `staged_value` are set to null in the same update (removal as status plus timestamp). Check: values are null if and only if `purged_at` is not null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, staged_action_id, connection_id, object_type_id, object_key, property)`.
References: `(organisation_id, staged_action_id) → simulation.staged_actions`; `(organisation_id, connection_id) → connect.connections`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`.
Indexes: the unique key serves the bases of one staged Action (staleness check on open and before promotion; FK). `(organisation_id, connection_id)`: FK. `(organisation_id, staged_action_id) where purged_at is null`: purge sweep of one branch.
Security: RLS standard. Encrypted columns: `base_value`, `staged_value`. Written by `simulation`. The branch base is never used as prior state at promotion (39.8). Purged with the branch by the sweep in `scenario_branches`; also on `silo.purge` where the target connection is purged.

---

# Schema `automation` (chapter 40)

### `automation.automations`
Purpose: a Cron, with its subject, trigger, owner and execution identity. Spec chapter 40 (40.1, 40.2, 40.7, 40.8, 40.10).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `owner_membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `service_principal_id` uuid, not null. Principal of kind `automation`, scoped to this Cron. Executes, never authorises.
- `name` text, not null.
- `saved_view_id` uuid, null. The saved question.
- `object_set_id` uuid, null. The watched object set.
- `schedule` text, null. Five-field expression.
- `watch` jsonb, null. Properties, change kinds, coalescing window.
- `timezone` text, not null. The organisation's time zone as an IANA name, validated by the service against `pg_timezone_names`.
- `status` text, not null, default `active`. `active`, `paused`, `stopped`. Check.
- `paused_reason` text, null. Added. `manual`, `repeated_failure`, `connection_halted`, `owner_removed`, `billing_suspended`, `authorisation_expired`. Check; set with `paused_at`.
- `failure_policy` jsonb, not null. Mode (`notify_continue`, `pause_after_failures`) and the failure count limit.
- `next_run_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Next due time computed in the organisation's time zone; null for change-triggered Crons and for non-active Crons.
- `lease_expires_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Set when the scheduler claims a due Cron, so two scheduler instances never take the same run.
- `last_run_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
- `paused_at` timestamptz, null. Check: not null when `status = 'paused'`.
- `deleted_at` timestamptz, null. Added. `automation_deleted` is a status change.
- `version` integer, not null, default 1. Added.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Checks: subject arc `num_nonnulls(saved_view_id, object_set_id) = 1`; trigger arc `num_nonnulls(schedule, watch) = 1`; `watch is null or object_set_id is not null`; `next_run_at` is null unless `schedule` is not null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, service_principal_id)`; `unique (organisation_id, owner_membership_id, name) where deleted_at is null`.
References: `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, service_principal_id) → iam.service_principals`; `(organisation_id, saved_view_id) → workspace.saved_views`; `(organisation_id, object_set_id) → ontology.object_sets`.
Indexes:
- `(next_run_at, id) where status = 'active' and next_run_at is not null and deleted_at is null`: the scheduler's due sweep across organisations. Exception to the leading `organisation_id` rule because the sweep is cross-tenant (see Security).
- `(organisation_id, saved_view_id) where saved_view_id is not null` and `(organisation_id, object_set_id) where object_set_id is not null`: FK; "Crons built on this view or set".
- `(organisation_id, owner_membership_id) where deleted_at is null`: Governance list, owner removal pausing Crons (the unique name key covers this).
Security: RLS standard for all tenant reads and writes. The cross-tenant due sweep cannot run under a single `app.org_id`. Requirement for the conventions: a `security definer` function `automation.claim_due_automations(batch_size, now)`, owned by the migrate role, that returns only `(organisation_id, id, next_run_at)` of due rows and sets `lease_expires_at` in the same statement (skip locked). The scheduler then sets `app.org_id` per returned row and works under RLS. Written by `scheduler` and by members through the API. A Cron never exceeds its owner (40.6): that is enforced in the policy service, not in this table.

### `automation.automation_connections`
Purpose: the connections a Cron depends on, so a halted connection pauses every Cron that depends on it. Added; spec chapter 40 (40.8 binding rule).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `automation_id` uuid, not null.
- `connection_id` uuid, not null.
- `recorded_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, automation_id, connection_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, automation_id) → automation.automations`; `(organisation_id, connection_id) → connect.connections`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, connection_id)`: on a connection halt, find and pause dependent Crons (FK).
Security: RLS standard. Written by `scheduler`; the set is replaced when the Cron is saved and after each run (the resolved plan lists the connections).

### `automation.automation_conditions`
Purpose: the condition tree of a Cron: result, finding, value and composite conditions. Spec chapter 40 (40.3, 40.10).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `automation_id` uuid, not null.
- `parent_condition_id` uuid, null. Added. Null for the root; a composite condition is the parent of its operands. Depth is at most three levels (40.3), enforced by trigger.
- `kind` text, not null. `result`, `finding`, `value`, `composite`. Check.
- `detector_id` uuid, null. Added. Changed: the detector named by a finding condition is a typed reference. Not null when `kind = 'finding'`, null otherwise.
- `object_type_id` uuid, null. Added. Same rule as `detector_id`.
- `target` jsonb, null. Changed: nullable. Result and value conditions: the figure or result being examined. Null for composite.
- `operator` text, null. Changed: nullable; null for composite. Values by kind: result `returned_rows`, `returned_none`, `count_crossed`, `differs_from_previous`; finding `raised`, `score_above`, `recurred`; value `above`, `below`, `changed_by_proportion`, `unchanged_for`. Derived from 40.3; extended by migration.
- `value` jsonb, null. Owner-stated threshold.
- `combinator` text, null. `AND` or `OR`. Changed: nullable; not null exactly when `kind = 'composite'`.
- `sequence` integer, not null. Order among siblings.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique nulls not distinct (organisation_id, automation_id, parent_condition_id, sequence)`; one root per Cron: `unique (organisation_id, automation_id) where parent_condition_id is null`.
References: `(organisation_id, automation_id) → automation.automations`; `(organisation_id, parent_condition_id) → automation.automation_conditions`; `(detector_id) → recognition.detectors (id)`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id) → ontology.object_types`.
Indexes: the unique keys serve loading a Cron's tree (FK). `(organisation_id, parent_condition_id) where parent_condition_id is not null`: FK. `(organisation_id, detector_id, object_type_id) where kind = 'finding'`: Crons affected when a detector is retired or an object type is retired.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `scheduler`. No condition means a schedule that always fires: a Cron with zero rows here is valid.

### `automation.automation_actions`
Purpose: the ordered actions a Cron takes when its condition holds. Spec chapter 40 (40.4, 40.5, 40.10).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `automation_id` uuid, not null.
- `kind` text, not null. `notify`, `report`, `mutate`, `escalate`. Check.
- `configuration` jsonb, not null. Channel and recipient identifiers for notify, report format and folder for report. No record values.
- `action_type_id` uuid, null. Added. Action type for `mutate`; required for `mutate`, null otherwise.
- `authorisation_id` uuid, null. Added. Authorisation for `mutate`; required for `mutate`, null otherwise.
- `escalate_membership_id` uuid, null. Added. Escalation target arc: exactly one of the two for `escalate`, none otherwise: `num_nonnulls(escalate_membership_id, escalate_scope_id) = 1` when `kind = 'escalate'`, else 0.
- `escalate_scope_id` uuid, null. Added.
- `sequence` integer, not null. Check `>= 1`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, automation_id, sequence)`.
References: `(organisation_id, automation_id) → automation.automations`; `(organisation_id, action_type_id) → action.action_types`; `(organisation_id, authorisation_id, automation_id) → automation.automation_authorisations (organisation_id, id, automation_id)`; `(organisation_id, escalate_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, escalate_scope_id) → iam.scopes`.
Indexes: the unique key serves loading actions in order (FK). `(organisation_id, action_type_id) where action_type_id is not null`: FK. `(organisation_id, authorisation_id) where authorisation_id is not null`: FK.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `scheduler`. Trigger: an action with an `execute` authorisation is rejected when its action type is a physical actuation type (40.5 binding rule); the scheduler repeats the refusal at run time.

### `automation.automation_authorisations`
Purpose: the bounds and the named authorising person for a mutate action; set at creation and unchangeable. Spec chapter 40 (40.5, 40.10).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `automation_id` uuid, not null.
- `mode` text, not null. `propose` or `execute`. Check.
- `max_rows` integer, null. Changed: nullable; required for `execute`. Check `> 0` and `< 10000` (ten thousand or more is refused). The fall back to propose above one hundred rows is applied at run time.
- `permitted_fields` text[], null. Changed: nullable; required and non-empty for `execute`. Property names.
- `authorised_by` uuid, not null. Membership whose name goes on the receipt.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, null. Changed: nullable; required for `execute`.
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
- `revoked_by` uuid, null. Added.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Changed: `permitted_connections uuid[]` is replaced by `automation.authorisation_connections`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id, automation_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, automation_id) → automation.automations`; `(organisation_id, authorised_by)` and `revoked_by → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, automation_id) where revoked_at is null`: the live authorisation at run time (FK). `(expires_at) where mode = 'execute' and revoked_at is null`: expiry sweep that returns mutate actions to propose and writes `automation_authorisation_expired`; cross-tenant, run through the same definer pattern as the due sweep.
Security: RLS standard. Immutable: trigger rejects any update except `revoked_at` and `revoked_by`. Written by `scheduler`. The authorisation never transfers on owner change; a new owner needs a new row.

### `automation.authorisation_connections`
Purpose: the connections an execute or propose authorisation may reach. Added; replaces `permitted_connections uuid[]`. Spec chapter 40 (40.5).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `authorisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `connection_id` uuid, not null.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, authorisation_id, connection_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, authorisation_id) → automation.automation_authorisations`; `(organisation_id, connection_id) → connect.connections`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, connection_id)`: FK; authorisations affected when a connection is halted or removed.
Security: RLS standard. Insert only, in the same transaction as the authorisation; trigger rejects update and delete.

### `automation.automation_runs`
Purpose: the record of every run, including runs where the condition did not hold, skipped runs and indeterminate runs. Spec chapter 40 (40.9, 40.10).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `automation_id` uuid, not null.
- `trigger_kind` text, not null. `schedule`, `change`, `manual`. Changed: renamed from `trigger` to avoid the SQL keyword. Check.
- `status` text, not null, default `running`. Added. `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `skipped`. Check.
- `started_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `completed_at` timestamptz, null. Not null unless `status = 'running'`.
- `condition_outcome` text, null. `met`, `not_met`, `indeterminate`. Check. Null for skipped runs and while running.
- `authorised_by_membership_id` uuid, null. Added. For execute runs, the authorising person, recorded on every run (40.5).
- `change_count` bigint, null. Added. Coalesced changes behind a `change` run.
- `error` text, null. Redacted.
- `skipped_reason` text, null. `overlap`, `connection_halted`, `owner_unavailable`, `authorisation_expired`, `billing_suspended`, `stream_gap`. Check; not null exactly when `status = 'skipped'`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Changed: `actions_taken jsonb` is replaced by `automation.automation_run_actions`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; overlap guard `unique (organisation_id, automation_id) where status = 'running'`, so a second concurrent run cannot start (40.7).
References: `(organisation_id, automation_id) → automation.automations`; `(organisation_id, authorised_by_membership_id) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, automation_id, started_at desc)`: run history of one Cron (FK). `(organisation_id, started_at desc) where condition_outcome = 'met'`: Home, Crons that ran and found something.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `scheduler`. After completion the row is immutable by trigger. Not partitioned at launch (run history must stay readable for the life of a Cron); runs are not metered.

### `automation.automation_run_actions`
Purpose: the outcome of each action in a run, the produced artefact, and the acknowledgement state of escalations. Added; replaces `actions_taken` and covers the missing delivery record. Spec chapter 40 (40.4) and the stress-test finding on notifications.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `run_id` uuid, not null.
- `action_id` uuid, not null.
- `action_kind` text, not null. Copy of `automation_actions.kind` at run time. Check against the four kinds.
- `sequence` integer, not null.
- `outcome` text, not null. `succeeded`, `failed`, `skipped`, `proposed`, `executed`, `delivered`. Check. A failed action stops later mutate actions but not later notifications (40.4).
- `result_counts` jsonb, null. Counts only, for example recipients notified or rows proposed.
- `mutation_id` uuid, null. Proposed or executed Action.
- `file_id` uuid, null. Report export. Arc: `num_nonnulls(mutation_id, file_id) <= 1`.
- `escalated_membership_id` uuid, null. Copied target for `escalate`; `num_nonnulls(escalated_membership_id, escalated_scope_id) = 1` when `action_kind = 'escalate'`, else 0.
- `escalated_scope_id` uuid, null.
- `acknowledged_by` uuid, null. Membership. Set only for escalations.
- `acknowledged_at` timestamptz, null. Check: set together with `acknowledged_by`.
- `error` text, null. Redacted.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, run_id, sequence)`.
References: `(organisation_id, run_id) → automation.automation_runs`; `(organisation_id, action_id) → automation.automation_actions`; `(organisation_id, mutation_id) → action.mutations`; `(organisation_id, file_id) → files.files`; `(organisation_id, escalated_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, escalated_scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, acknowledged_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique key serves actions of a run (FK). `(organisation_id, action_id)`: FK. `(organisation_id, escalated_membership_id, created_at desc) where action_kind = 'escalate' and acknowledged_at is null` and the same on `escalated_scope_id`: open escalations on Home and Governance until acknowledged. `(organisation_id, mutation_id) where mutation_id is not null` and `(organisation_id, file_id) where file_id is not null`: FK.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `scheduler`; `acknowledged_*` set by the API on the escalation. Per-recipient delivery rows (email, push, Home item) belong to the notifications table that the workspace domain defines; that table references `automation_run_actions` through its own exclusive arc. Notification content carries the Cron name, condition, counts and a link, never values.

### `automation.automation_run_state`
Purpose: the minimum state kept between runs for "differs from previous", value and change conditions. Spec chapter 40 (40.2, 40.3, 40.10).
Columns:
- `automation_id` uuid, not null. Primary key.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `previous_result_hash` bytea, null. Changed: nullable before the first run. A keyed hash (HMAC under a per-organisation key), so a small result cannot be recovered by guessing. Never the rows.
- `previous_row_count` bigint, null.
- `previous_value` bytea, null. Changed from `numeric`: one derived customer figure is a record value, and the conventions list of columns that may hold values does not include it. Encrypted per the conventions, pending the decision in chapter 62; it is on the conventions list (Changed (review 2026-10-28)). If chapter 62 settles on a keyed hash with direction only, the column becomes a hash and leaves the list.
- `follow_up_pending` boolean, not null, default false. Added. At most one pending follow-up for changes arriving during a run (40.2).
- `consecutive_failures` integer, not null, default 0. Added. Drives `pause_after_failures`.
- `findings_checked_at` timestamptz, null. Added (D101): when the last run read the findings its finding conditions name; a finding raised after it is new to the next run. Null before the first run, which counts from the Cron's creation.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(automation_id)`; `unique (organisation_id, automation_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, automation_id) → automation.automations`.
Indexes: none beyond the keys; one row per Cron.
Security: RLS standard. Encrypted column: `previous_value`. Written by `scheduler`. Purged with the Cron.

---

# Schema `files` (chapter 41)

### `files.folders`
Purpose: an arrangement tree for files; it grants nothing. Spec chapter 41 (41.1, 41.7).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `name` text, not null.
- `parent_id` uuid, null.
- `path` ltree, not null. Labels are the folder ids without hyphens, so a rename never rewrites paths; a move rewrites the subtree in one transaction. Maintained by trigger; a cycle is rejected.
- `created_by` uuid, not null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique nulls not distinct (organisation_id, parent_id, name)`.
References: `(organisation_id, parent_id) → files.folders`; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `gist (path)`: subtree move and descendant listing. `(organisation_id, parent_id)` is covered by the unique key (FK).
Security: RLS standard. No folder-level permission and no file count, ever (a count is a disclosure); the API lists only files the viewer may see. Written by `files`.

### `files.files`
Purpose: an export or an upload, with its storage key, markings and retention. Spec chapter 41 (41.2, 41.4, 41.5, 41.7).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `folder_id` uuid, null.
- `kind` text, not null. `export` or `upload`. Check.
- `name` text, not null.
- `object_store_key` text, null. Key of the encrypted object. Unique per organisation. Changed (review 2026-10-28): nullable; check `(kind = 'export') = (object_store_key is not null)`. An upload's bytes live only at `siloes.silo_files.object_store_key`.
- `content_type` text, null. Detected from the bytes, not the declared header. Changed (review 2026-10-28): nullable; check `(kind = 'export') = (content_type is not null and size is not null)`. For uploads, read from `siloes.silo_files`.
- `size` bigint, null. Check `>= 0`. Changed (review 2026-10-28): nullable, as `content_type`.
- Changed (review 2026-10-28): `silo_id` removed, with its check, reference and index; the Silo comes from `siloes.silo_files.silo_id`.
- `silo_file_id` uuid, null. Check: `(kind = 'upload') = (silo_file_id is not null)`. Added (review 2026-10-28): `files.files` is the Files-page catalogue entry and `siloes.silo_files` holds the stored object, so an upload has one storage record.
- `ingestion_state` text, null. Added. `stored` or `ingested` for uploads; null for exports. Check.
- `status` text, not null, default `available`. Added. `available` or `deleted`. Check.
- `retention` interval, null. Null is indefinite. For uploads, the Silo's window.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, null. Added. `created_at + retention`; recomputed when the Silo window is shortened (requires `silo.purge`). Null when indefinite.
- `deleted_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Check: set exactly when `status = 'deleted'`. The object is removed from the store; the row remains as the anchor for the deletion receipt. Changed (review 2026-10-28): deleting an upload is a Silo purge (41.6): `siloes-import` removes the bytes and `files` sets `status = 'deleted'` and `deleted_at` when the purge completes.
- `created_by` uuid, not null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Changed: `marking_ids uuid[]` is replaced by `files.file_markings`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, object_store_key)` partial where `object_store_key is not null` (Changed (review 2026-10-28): partial).
References: `(organisation_id, folder_id) → files.folders`; `(organisation_id, silo_file_id) → siloes.silo_files` (Added (review 2026-10-28)); Changed (review 2026-10-28): `(organisation_id, silo_id) → siloes.siloes` removed; `(organisation_id, created_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, folder_id, created_at desc) where status = 'available'`: folder contents list (FK).
- `(organisation_id, silo_file_id) where silo_file_id is not null`: uploads of a Silo (through `siloes.silo_files.silo_id`), delete-with-extractions, Silo retention change (FK). Changed (review 2026-10-28): replaces `(organisation_id, silo_id) where silo_id is not null`.
- `(expires_at) where status = 'available' and expires_at is not null`: retention sweep (`file_retention_swept`), cross-tenant, run by `silo_migrate` through the sweep path.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `files`. Changed (review 2026-10-28): `files` writes the catalogue row and `siloes-import` writes the stored object (`siloes.silo_files`). Content-type check, size cap and SVG sanitisation happen before the row exists (41.4). Retention: exports follow the organisation's setting, uploads follow the Silo.

### `files.file_markings`
Purpose: the markings a file carries; a recipient must hold every one. Added; replaces `files.marking_ids uuid[]`. Spec chapter 41 (41.2, 41.3).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `file_id` uuid, not null.
- `marking_id` uuid, not null.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, file_id, marking_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, file_id) → files.files`; `(organisation_id, marking_id) → gov.markings`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, marking_id)`: FK; files affected by a declassification.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `files` at creation (equal to the frozen snapshot) and changed only by the governance declassification path.

### `files.file_permissions`
Purpose: the frozen permissions of the person who made the file, at creation. Spec chapter 41 (41.2).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `file_id` uuid, not null.
- `markings` jsonb, not null. Snapshot.
- `field_policies` jsonb, not null. Snapshot.
- `connection_grants` jsonb, not null. Snapshot.
- `frozen_at` timestamptz, not null.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, file_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, file_id) → files.files`.
Indexes: none beyond the key.
Security: RLS standard. Immutable by trigger (reject update and delete). Snapshots are historic decisions and deliberately carry no foreign keys; the file never tracks its source. Written by `files`.

### `files.file_provenance`
Purpose: which source, which run, when, and by whom a file was produced, kept after the source is removed. Spec chapter 41 (41.2).
Columns:
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `file_id` uuid, not null.
- `source_saved_view_id` uuid, null. Changed: exclusive arc replaces `source_kind` and `source_id`.
- `source_finding_id` uuid, null.
- `source_detector_run_id` uuid, null. A ranking export is sourced to the detector run whose findings were ranked; the spec defines no ranking table.
- `source_receipt_id` uuid, null.
- `source_simulation_run_id` uuid, null. A scenario run or a branch run.
- `source_automation_run_id` uuid, null. A Cron's report action.
- `source_kind` text, not null. Kept: generated always stored from the arc (`view`, `finding`, `ranking`, `receipt`, `scenario_run`, `cron_report`).
- `run_reference` uuid, null. Opaque identifier of the executed query run for view, finding and receipt exports. No foreign key: query runs live in the data plane.
- `produced_at` timestamptz, not null.
Arc check: `num_nonnulls(source_saved_view_id, source_finding_id, source_detector_run_id, source_receipt_id, source_simulation_run_id, source_automation_run_id) = 1`.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, file_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, file_id) → files.files`; `(organisation_id, source_saved_view_id) → workspace.saved_views`; `(organisation_id, source_finding_id) → recognition.findings`; `(organisation_id, source_detector_run_id) → recognition.detector_runs`; `(organisation_id, source_receipt_id) → action.receipts`; `(organisation_id, source_simulation_run_id) → simulation.simulation_runs`; `(organisation_id, source_automation_run_id) → automation.automation_runs`.
Indexes: one partial index per arc column, `(organisation_id, source_x_id) where source_x_id is not null`: each is the FK index and serves "exports made from this view, finding or run" (shown when a source is reviewed).
Security: RLS standard. Insert only; written by `files`. "Kept after source deletion" holds because sources are soft-removed and never hard-deleted; this FK also blocks a hard delete of a source that has exports.

### `files.file_shares`
Purpose: a share of a file with a membership, scope or the organisation. Spec chapter 41 (41.3).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `file_id` uuid, not null.
- `grantee_membership_id` uuid, null. Changed: exclusive arc replaces `grantee_type` and `grantee_id`.
- `grantee_scope_id` uuid, null.
- `grantee_whole_organisation` boolean, null. True or null.
- `access` text, not null. `view` or `download`. Check. Values are not stated in the spec; this is the minimum set.
- `shared_by` uuid, not null.
- `expires_at` timestamptz, null.
- `revoked_at` timestamptz, null.
- `revoked_by` uuid, null. Added.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default `now()`. Added.
Arc check: `num_nonnulls(grantee_membership_id, grantee_scope_id, grantee_whole_organisation) = 1`, with `grantee_whole_organisation is true or null`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; live uniqueness: `unique (organisation_id, file_id, grantee_membership_id) where revoked_at is null and grantee_membership_id is not null`, the same on `grantee_scope_id`, and `unique (organisation_id, file_id) where revoked_at is null and grantee_whole_organisation`.
References: `(organisation_id, file_id) → files.files`; `(organisation_id, grantee_membership_id) → iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, grantee_scope_id) → iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, shared_by)` and `revoked_by → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the three unique indexes serve the share dialogue (FK on `file_id`). `(organisation_id, grantee_membership_id) where revoked_at is null and grantee_membership_id is not null` and `(organisation_id, grantee_scope_id) where revoked_at is null and grantee_scope_id is not null`: "Shared with me".
Security: RLS standard. Written by `files`. Marking and Silo access are checked at share time and on every open; a share never grants either (41.3). A refused open writes `file_download_refused`.

### `files.file_deletions`
Purpose: the deletion receipt: what was removed, by whom, and what stopped working. Spec chapter 41 (41.5).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Added.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `file_id` uuid, not null.
- `scope_of_removal` jsonb, not null. The file, its extractions and derived data, and the detectors that lose input (names and identifiers).
- `counts` jsonb, not null.
- `purge_receipt_id` uuid, null. Added. For an ingested upload, the Silo purge receipt (the deletion is a purge, 41.6).
- `requested_by` uuid, not null.
- `completed_at` timestamptz, not null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, file_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, file_id) → files.files`; `(organisation_id, purge_receipt_id) → siloes.purge_receipts`; `(organisation_id, requested_by) → iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique key serves the receipt of a file (FK). `(organisation_id, purge_receipt_id) where purge_receipt_id is not null`: FK.
Security: RLS standard. Append-only: trigger rejects update and delete, grants `insert, select`. Not partitioned. Written by `files`.
