## Schema `siloes`

Relationships:
- `siloes.source_connection_id → connect.connections` (Import, Object Index and Warehouse answer as sources)
- `silo_object_types.silo_id → siloes`, `object_type_id → ontology.object_types`
- `transitions.(silo_id) → siloes`, `connection_id → connect.connections`
- `silo_baselines.(silo_id) → siloes`
- `silo_sources.silo_id → siloes`, `definition_id → silo_definitions`
- `silo_definitions.silo_id → siloes`
- `silo_files.(silo_id, source_id) → silo_sources`
- `silo_extractions.file_id → silo_files`
- `extraction_confirmations.extraction_id → silo_extractions`
- `index_definitions.(silo_id, silo_kind) → siloes`, `object_type_id → ontology.object_types`
- `index_refreshes.index_definition_id → index_definitions`
- `warehouse_projects.(silo_id, silo_kind) → siloes`
- `warehouse_tables.warehouse_project_id → warehouse_projects`, `object_type_id → ontology.object_types`, `link_type_id → ontology.link_types`, `ontology_version_id → ontology.ontology_versions`
- `warehouse_sync_runs.warehouse_table_id → warehouse_tables`
- `warehouse_sql_grants.warehouse_project_id → warehouse_projects`
- `purge_requests.silo_id → siloes`, `object_type_id → ontology.object_types`, `silo_file_id → silo_files`, `approval_chain_id → action.approval_chains` (Added (review 2026-10-28))
- `purge_receipts.silo_id → siloes`, `silo_file_id → silo_files`, `purge_request_id → purge_requests` (Changed (review 2026-10-28): `purge_request_id` added; `approval_chain_id` removed)
- `clone.asset_models`, `clone.spatial_plans` and `files` references point at `silo_files`

### `siloes.siloes`
Purpose: one opt-in Silo of one of the four types, created for a stated purpose with a retention window. Spec chapter 66.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`capture`, `import`, `object_index`, `warehouse`). Immutable.
- `name` text, not null. Unique per organisation among live Siloes. Check non-empty.
- `purpose` text, not null. Stated purpose, shown in the disclosure. Check non-empty.
- `retention_days` integer, not null, no default. Check `> 0`. Shortening needs `silo.purge`, lengthening `silo.manage`; both write `retention_changed` with the old and new values.
- `location` text, not null. Residency location of the backing store (a GCP region such as `europe-west2`, or the Postgres cell location for Capture). Set at creation from the cell's permitted locations; immutable (trigger rejects change).
- `status` text, not null, default `active`. Added. Check in (`active`, `purging`, `disabled`). `purging` stops new captures and imports while the queue drains (70.3).
- `store_ref` text, null. Added. The backing store: BigQuery dataset id for Import, Object Index and Warehouse; `pg-capture` for Capture. Names derive deterministically from ids (see BigQuery section) and are stored so purge receipts and audit name exactly what was removed.
- `source_connection_id` uuid, null. Added. The `connect.connections` row through which an Import Silo, Object Index or Warehouse is queried as a source (66.5). Null for Capture. Check: not null when `kind <> 'capture'` once `status = 'active'`.
- `carveout_acknowledged_by` uuid, null; `carveout_acknowledged_at` timestamptz, null. Added. The recorded acceptance of the document-extraction prompt carve-out (68.7, 70.7). Both set together. Without it, document extraction is unreachable for this Silo (checked in `siloes-import` before any definition with `requires_model` is published). Only meaningful for `kind = 'import'`; check: null for other kinds.
- `action_ledger_enabled_at` timestamptz, null; `action_ledger_include_values` boolean, null. Added. Set when the Action ledger copy is directed into this Silo (66.4, chapter 48.2). Both set together. Check: only for `kind in ('capture','import','warehouse')` (capture since D205, where the cell has no Warehouse); one live Silo per organisation holds it (`siloes_one_ledger`). `include_values` records the "values option" the enabling person chose.
- `created_by` uuid, not null. Membership.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added.
- `disabled_at` timestamptz, null. Set by disable and purge. Check: not null when `status = 'disabled'`.
- `version` bigint, not null, default 1. Added. Retention and nomination edits race.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id, kind)` (pins the kind for index and warehouse tables); `unique (organisation_id, name)` where `disabled_at is null`; `unique (organisation_id)` where `kind = 'warehouse' and disabled_at is null` (one Warehouse per organisation, 69.21).
References: `(organisation_id, created_by)`, `(organisation_id, carveout_acknowledged_by)` → `iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, source_connection_id)` → `connect.connections`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, created_at desc)` where `disabled_at is null`: Siloes page list.
- `(organisation_id, kind)` where `status = 'active'`: "is any Capture Silo active" checks and per-type routing.
- `(organisation_id, source_connection_id)` where `source_connection_id is not null`: foreign key index; source-to-Silo resolution by the federated engine.
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `siloes-capture` (kind capture) and `siloes-import` (all other kinds). Creation is refused when the organisation switch `silo.enable` is off, and no row of this schema is reachable while it is off (checked in the service before any query; the RLS policy is not changed). Rows are never deleted; disable and purge sets `status` and `disabled_at`.

### `siloes.silo_object_types`
Purpose: the object types a Silo holds and, per type, the properties nominated. Spec chapter 66 (replaces `silo_concepts`).
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `nominated_properties` text[], not null. Property API names held. Nothing outside this list is stored. Check: `cardinality >= 1`, no null element. The names stay text so history survives a later property rename or removal in the ontology (transitions and index columns are keyed by the name at the time). Marking clearance is checked in the service at add time (66.10).
- `added_by` uuid, not null; `added_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `removed_at` timestamptz, null.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added. Property list changes write `silo_fields_changed`.
- `version` bigint, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, silo_id, object_type_id)` where `removed_at is null`.
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id)` → `siloes.siloes`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id)` → `ontology.object_types`.
Indexes:
- The partial unique serves "what is in this Silo" (Siloes page node selection).
- `(organisation_id, object_type_id, silo_id)` where `removed_at is null`: capture lookup "is this object type held in a Capture Silo" on every query result and change stream event, and the purge-concept scope.
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `siloes-capture` and `siloes-import` per Silo kind. Nothing cascades: adding a type never adds related types (66.6).

### `siloes.transitions`
Purpose: append-only record that a nominated property of an object changed from one value to another, as observed. Spec chapter 67.
Columns:
- `id` bigint, not null, `generated always as identity`.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_ref` text, not null. Resolved object reference.
- `property` text, not null. Must be in the nominated list of the live `silo_object_types` row (checked by the writer, not by the database).
- `previous_value` bytea, not null. Changed: was `jsonb`. Encrypted envelope of the JSON value (a JSON `null` is encrypted too). Associated data `(organisation_id, silo_id, object_type_id, object_ref, property, observed_at)`.
- `new_value` bytea, not null. Changed: was `jsonb`. Same envelope and associated data.
- `observed_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `connection_id` uuid, not null. Connection the row came from.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, id, observed_at)`. Changed from the generic ledger key `(id, occurred_at)`: the partition key columns of both levels must be in the key.
Partitioning: list on `organisation_id`, then range by month on `observed_at`, so a retention window or a Silo purge is a partition drop (67.5). A list partition for an organisation is created by `silo_migrate` (`siloes.create_capture_partitions`) when its first Capture Silo is created. Changed (review 2026-10-28): it has a default sub-partition and is registered in `platform.partition_plan`, so the daily job keeps its months ahead like every other ledger, and no observation is refused for its date. A purge that drops the list partition deletes its plan row in the same transaction. (Superseded text: no default partition; an insert with no partition fails and is counted as a capture gap.) Where an organisation has Capture Siloes with different windows, the sweep drops sub-partitions older than the longest window and deletes the older rows of the shorter-window Silo in batches of 10,000 as `silo_migrate`, receipted. Partition count (organisations with Capture times retained months) is a planning limit: untested above about 5,000 per cell.
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id)` → `siloes.siloes`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id)` → `ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, connection_id)` → `connect.connections`. Nothing references this table.
Indexes (created on the partitioned parent):
- `(organisation_id, silo_id, object_type_id, object_ref, property, observed_at desc)`: state at time T for one object and field (Clone Canvas scrubbing), purge entity, entity history.
- `(organisation_id, silo_id, object_type_id, property, observed_at)`: lead time derivation and the three history detectors, which scan one property across objects in time order.
- BRIN `(observed_at)`: retention sweeps and baseline-depth counts ("how much history exists" for the building baseline state).
- `(organisation_id, object_type_id)`: transitions of an object type across Siloes; FK index. Added (review 2026-10-28).
- No index on `connection_id`: no query filters by it, and the referenced rows are never deleted.
Security: RLS standard. Append-only: a before update or delete trigger rejects the statement unless `current_user = 'silo_migrate'`; `silo_app` holds `insert, select` only. Deletes by `silo_migrate` are retention sweeps, entity purges and Silo purges, each receipted in `siloes.purge_receipts`. Writes by `siloes-capture` in batches from the queue in `redis-data`. Encrypted columns: `previous_value`, `new_value`. No row is written on first sighting (67.2).

### `siloes.silo_baselines`
Purpose: the last observed value of each nominated property, so the next observation can be compared. Spec chapter 67.
Columns:
- `silo_id` uuid, not null; `object_type_id` uuid, not null; `object_ref` text, not null; `property` text, not null.
- `last_observed_value` bytea, not null. Changed: was `jsonb`. Encrypted envelope; associated data is the primary key columns.
- `last_seen_at` timestamptz, not null.
Keys: primary key `(organisation_id, silo_id, object_type_id, object_ref, property)` (the spec key, with the tenant column first). Exception: no `id` column and no `unique (organisation_id, id)`, because nothing references a baseline and a surrogate key would add a second index to the busiest update path in this schema.
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id)` → `siloes.siloes`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id)` → `ontology.object_types`.
Indexes: the primary key only. It serves the compare on every observed row, entity purge (prefix on object reference) and concept purge (prefix on object type). Set `fillfactor = 70` and index no updated column, so `last_seen_at` updates are heap-only. A baseline is written only when the value changes or `last_seen_at` is more than 10 minutes old (writer rule, to bound write volume; the building-baseline state counts transitions, not sightings).
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `siloes-capture`. Encrypted column: `last_observed_value`. Purged with its owning object, type or Silo. Hash-partitioning by organisation is not applied at first; revisit when a cell exceeds about 500 million rows (untested).

### `siloes.silo_definitions`
Purpose: a published, versioned structuring definition for an Import Silo. Spec chapter 68.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null. Added. The spec row had no owner; a definition belongs to one Import Silo.
- `version` integer, not null. Check `>= 1`. Next version = highest for the Silo plus one.
- `route` text, not null. Check in (`ai`, `builder`, `prebuilt`).
- `document` jsonb, not null. Validated definition, mirrors `connect.connector_manifests`. Structure only, no secrets, no values. Check object.
- `requires_model` boolean, not null. Added. True when any field is extracted by a structured-document or prose method (68.2). Drives the carve-out acknowledgement and the disclosure variant (70.6).
- `published_by` uuid, not null; `published_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `retired_at` timestamptz, null. Added. The only mutable column.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, silo_id, version)`; `unique (organisation_id, silo_id, id)` (target for sources).
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id)` → `siloes.siloes`; `(organisation_id, published_by)` → `iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique `(organisation_id, silo_id, version)` serves "latest definition" (read descending). `jsonb` is not indexed: no query filters inside it.
Security: RLS standard. A row exists only once published, so it is immutable: a trigger rejects update of every column except `retired_at`, and rejects delete (spec: "immutable once used"). Writes by `siloes-import`. Publishing a row with `requires_model` is refused unless `siloes.carveout_acknowledged_at` is set.

### `siloes.silo_sources`
Purpose: an upload folder or watched location feeding an Import Silo, bound to a definition. Spec chapter 68.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`upload`, `watched`).
- `location` text, not null. For `upload`, the GCS prefix inside the organisation bucket; for `watched`, the watched location reference. No credentials: credentials for a watched location are a `connect.connection_credentials` row reached through `source_connection_id`.
- `definition_id` uuid, null. Changed (review 2026-10-28): nullable. Required for sources whose files are structured (`tabular`, `structured`, `prose`); an `upload` source that receives only asset models and site plans has none. Check: `kind = 'watched'` implies `definition_id is not null`.
- `poll_interval_minutes` integer, null. Added. Required for `watched` (the spec says files are picked up "on a schedule" and gives no column); null for `upload`. Check `> 0`.
- `last_polled_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
- `created_by` uuid, not null; `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added.
- `disabled_at` timestamptz, null. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, silo_id, id)` (target for files).
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id)` → `siloes.siloes`; `(organisation_id, silo_id, definition_id)` → `siloes.silo_definitions (organisation_id, silo_id, id)`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, silo_id)` where `disabled_at is null`: sources of a Silo; `(organisation_id, definition_id)`: foreign key index; `(organisation_id, last_polled_at)` where `kind = 'watched' and disabled_at is null`: watched location scheduler picks the oldest due source.
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `siloes-import`. Added (review 2026-10-28): every Silo that accepts uploads gets one `upload` source, created with the Silo; Files-page uploads and Clone Canvas plan and model uploads go through it.

### `siloes.silo_files`
Purpose: one file received into an Import Silo, its class and processing state. Spec chapter 68.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null. Added, so the retention sweep, metering and purge by Silo need no join.
- `source_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_store_key` text, not null. GCS object key inside the organisation bucket (layout in the object storage section). Not the filename.
- `filename` text, not null. As received. Shown to users, never used in a storage key or a path.
- `size_bytes` bigint, not null. Check `>= 0`.
- `content_type` text, not null. Sniffed server-side, never from the client header.
- `content_class` text, not null. Check in (`tabular`, `structured`, `prose`, `asset_model`, `site_plan`).
- `received_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `processed_at` timestamptz, null. Check: not null when `status = 'processed'`.
- `status` text, not null, default `received`. Check in (`received`, `processed`, `failed`, `purged`).
- `error_stage` text, null. Added. Names the failing stage, never a value. Check: not null when `status = 'failed'`.
- `purged_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Check: not null when `status = 'purged'`.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, object_store_key)`; `unique (organisation_id, silo_id, id)` (Added (review 2026-10-28): target for the clone plan and model references).
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id, source_id)` → `siloes.silo_sources (organisation_id, silo_id, id)`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, silo_id, received_at desc)`: files list and the retention sweep by received date.
- `(organisation_id, source_id, received_at desc)`: foreign key index; watched location "files since last poll".
- `(organisation_id, silo_id, status)` where `status in ('received','failed')`: processing queue and failed list.
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `siloes-import`. A purge sets `status = 'purged'` after the GCS object (all generations) and the BigQuery rows are deleted; the row stays so receipts and `clone` references keep integrity. `asset_model` and `site_plan` rows are never sent to a model and have no extraction rows. Markings attach through `gov` (cross-domain requirement 7). Retention: removed from GCS by the Silo window; the metadata row is kept.

### `siloes.silo_extractions`
Purpose: a value extracted by a method less certain than a column read, with its source location and confirmation, held for flag display. Spec chapter 68.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `file_id` uuid, not null.
- `object` text, not null. Definition object name.
- `row_ref` text, not null. Key of the row in BigQuery.
- `field` text, not null.
- `value` bytea, not null. Changed: was `jsonb`. Encrypted envelope; associated data `(organisation_id, file_id, object, row_ref, field)`.
- `method` text, not null. Check in (`certain`, `near`, `inferred`).
- `confidence` numeric(4,3), null. Model score. Check between 0 and 1; null when the value was `certain` from the start.
- `raw_text_ref` text, not null. Location of the source text: page, cell or offset. Not the text.
- `confirmed_by` uuid, null; `confirmed_at` timestamptz, null. Check: both null or both not null; when set, `method = 'certain'`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
Reading of the spec: rows exist for `near` and `inferred` values (the ones that carry a flag), and a confirmed value is the same row with `method` set to `certain`. A value read from a tabular column is `certain` from the start and lives in BigQuery only, because the table holds values "for flag display". If the product wants a row per tabular value, this table needs partitioning and the volume must be re-estimated.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, file_id, object, row_ref, field)`.
References: `(organisation_id, file_id)` → `siloes.silo_files`; `(organisation_id, confirmed_by)` → `iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique serves flag lookup for a BigQuery row; `(organisation_id, file_id)`: purge file and foreign key index; `(organisation_id, object, created_at desc)` where `confirmed_at is null`: the review queue of unconfirmed values for an object.
Security: RLS standard. Encrypted column: `value`. The only update allowed is the confirmation (`method`, `confirmed_by`, `confirmed_at`, `confidence` unchanged), rejected by trigger once `confirmed_at` is set. Writes by `siloes-import`; the confirming person's permission is checked by the service (68.9). Purged with its file.

### `siloes.extraction_confirmations`
Purpose: append-only record of each confirmation, with the method before it. Spec chapter 68.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `extraction_id` uuid, not null.
- `membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `previous_method` text, not null. Check in (`near`, `inferred`).
- `confirmed_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, extraction_id)` (a value is confirmed once, permanently).
References: `(organisation_id, extraction_id)` → `siloes.silo_extractions`; `(organisation_id, membership_id)` → `iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique `(organisation_id, extraction_id)` is the foreign key index and the lookup. `(organisation_id, membership_id, confirmed_at desc)`: "values I confirmed" in the audit trail view.
Security: RLS standard; append-only (trigger rejects update and delete, `silo_app` holds `insert, select`). Written in the same transaction as the `silo_extractions` update by `siloes-import`. Deleted only by a file or Silo purge run as `silo_migrate`.

### `siloes.index_definitions`
Purpose: an object type nominated into an Object Index, with its properties and refresh schedule. Spec chapter 69.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null; `silo_kind` text, not null, default `object_index`. Added; check `= 'object_index'`. Pins the Silo kind through the composite key.
- `object_type_id` uuid, not null.
- `nominated_properties` text[], not null. Same rules as `silo_object_types.nominated_properties`.
- `refresh_schedule` text, not null. Cron expression in the organisation's time zone.
- `uses_change_stream` boolean, not null.
- `added_by` uuid, not null; `added_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `removed_at` timestamptz, null.
- `next_refresh_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Next scheduled bounded query; null for removed definitions.
- `last_refreshed_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Freshness stated on every result served from the index (69.3).
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added. `version` bigint, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, silo_id, object_type_id)` where `removed_at is null`.
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id, silo_kind)` → `siloes.siloes (organisation_id, id, kind)`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id)` → `ontology.object_types`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, next_refresh_at)` where `removed_at is null`: refresh scheduler picks due definitions; `(organisation_id, object_type_id)` where `removed_at is null`: search routing "is every object type in scope indexed for the searched properties" and the foreign key index.
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `siloes-import`. Silo purge or index purge sets `removed_at`.

### `siloes.index_refreshes`
Purpose: one refresh run of an index definition, with counts and outcome. Spec chapter 69.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `index_definition_id` uuid, not null.
- `trigger` text, not null. Check in (`schedule`, `change_stream`, `rebuild`).
- `objects_written` bigint, not null, default 0; `objects_removed` bigint, not null, default 0. Counts only. Check `>= 0`.
- `started_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(); `completed_at` timestamptz, null.
- `status` text, not null, default `running`. Check in (`running`, `completed`, `failed`, `refused`). Check: `completed_at` not null unless `running`.
- `error_stage` text, null. Added. Names the failing stage, never a value. Check: not null when `status in ('failed','refused')`.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, index_definition_id)` where `status = 'running'` (one refresh at a time per definition).
References: `(organisation_id, index_definition_id)` → `siloes.index_definitions`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, index_definition_id, started_at desc)`: refresh history on the Silo page and the foreign key index.
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `siloes-import`. Change stream refreshes are rolled up by the writer into one row per definition per 15 minutes, to bound volume (writer rule). Rows older than the Silo's retention window are removed by the retention sweep.

### `siloes.warehouse_projects`
Purpose: the dedicated Google Cloud project and dataset of an organisation's Warehouse, with provisioning state. Spec chapter 69.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null; `silo_kind` text, not null, default `warehouse`. Added; check `= 'warehouse'`.
- `gcp_project_id` text, not null. Dedicated project. Unique across all rows in the cell.
- `dataset` text, not null. BigQuery dataset name.
- `location` text, not null. Fixed at creation (trigger rejects change). Must equal `siloes.location`.
- `kms_key_ref` text, not null. Cloud KMS key resource name (a reference, never key material).
- `provisioning_step` text, not null. Last completed step. Check in (`none`, `project_created`, `dataset_created`, `key_bound`, `access_granted`, `tables_created`, `backfill_started`). Provisioning is idempotent and recorded step by step (69.13).
- `status` text, not null, default `provisioning`. Check in (`provisioning`, `backfilling`, `active`, `failed`, `handed_over`, `purged`).
- `failed_step` text, null. Added. The step that failed, never a value. Check: not null when `status = 'failed'`.
- `handed_over_at` timestamptz, null; `purged_at` timestamptz, null. Added; each not null for its status.
- `created_by` uuid, not null; `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added. `version` bigint, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id)` (one Warehouse per organisation, as the spec states); `unique (gcp_project_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id, silo_kind)` → `siloes.siloes (organisation_id, id, kind)`.
Indexes: the unique `(organisation_id)` serves every Warehouse lookup; `(organisation_id, silo_id)`: foreign key index; `(organisation_id, status)` where `status in ('provisioning','backfilling','failed')`: provisioning retry sweep.
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `siloes-import`. Not available in the sovereign cell (69.18): the table exists but stays empty and the service refuses creation.

### `siloes.warehouse_tables`
Purpose: each BigQuery table in a Warehouse, the ontology version it reflects and its freshness. Spec chapter 69.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `warehouse_project_id` uuid, not null.
- `object_type_id` uuid, null. Null for link and ledger tables.
- `link_type_id` uuid, null. Added. The spec has a link table per link type and no column to say which. Check: `kind in ('current','history')` requires `object_type_id` not null and `link_type_id` null; `kind = 'link'` requires `link_type_id` not null and `object_type_id` null; `kind = 'ledger'` requires both null.
- `table_name` text, not null. BigQuery table name.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`current`, `history`, `link`, `ledger`).
- `ontology_version_id` uuid, not null. Version the schema reflects.
- `last_synced_at` timestamptz, null. Freshness shown to users. Null until the first sync.
- `row_count` bigint, not null, default 0. Count only.
- `dropped_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Set when the object type leaves the Warehouse and its table is dropped after the retention window.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added. `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, warehouse_project_id, table_name)`.
References: `(organisation_id, warehouse_project_id)` → `siloes.warehouse_projects`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id)` → `ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, link_type_id)` → `ontology.link_types`; `(organisation_id, ontology_version_id)` → `ontology.ontology_versions`.
Indexes: the unique serves the table list of the Warehouse page; `(organisation_id, object_type_id, kind)` where `dropped_at is null`: query routing "is this object type in the Warehouse and how fresh"; `(organisation_id, link_type_id)` where `link_type_id is not null`, `(organisation_id, ontology_version_id)`: foreign key indexes.
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `siloes-import`.

### `siloes.warehouse_sync_runs`
Purpose: one backfill, stream roll-up, scheduled sync or reconciliation of one Warehouse table. Spec chapter 69.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `warehouse_table_id` uuid, not null.
- `mode` text, not null. Check in (`backfill`, `stream`, `scheduled`, `reconcile`).
- `rows_written` bigint, not null, default 0; `bytes_scanned` bigint, not null, default 0. Counts. Check `>= 0`. `bytes_scanned` feeds `billing.storage_measurements`.
- `status` text, not null, default `running`. Check in (`running`, `completed`, `failed`). The spec lists the column without values.
- `error` text, null. Names the stage, never a value. Check: not null when `status = 'failed'`.
- `started_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(); `completed_at` timestamptz, null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, warehouse_table_id)` → `siloes.warehouse_tables`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, warehouse_table_id, started_at desc)`: sync history and freshness drill-down, and the foreign key index; `(organisation_id, started_at desc)` where `status = 'failed'`: failed sync list.
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `siloes-import`. Stream mode is rolled up to one row per table per hour (writer rule). Removed by the retention sweep after the Silo window.

### `siloes.warehouse_sql_grants`
Purpose: a super admin's grant of read-only direct SQL access to a named Google identity. Spec chapter 69.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `warehouse_project_id` uuid, not null.
- `google_identity` text, not null. Email of the Google identity. Check contains `@`, stored lower case.
- `granted_by` uuid, not null; `granted_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Super admin membership (`warehouse.sql_access`).
- `revoked_by` uuid, null; `revoked_at` timestamptz, null. Check: both null or both not null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, warehouse_project_id, google_identity)` where `revoked_at is null`.
References: `(organisation_id, warehouse_project_id)` → `siloes.warehouse_projects`.
Indexes: the partial unique serves the active grants list; the foreign key index is its prefix.
Security: RLS standard. Rows are never deleted. Writes by `siloes-import`, which also applies or removes the IAM binding on the dataset in the same operation. The service refuses a grant when any table of the Warehouse holds a marked property (69.16).

### `siloes.purge_requests`
Purpose: a request to purge Silo data, which an approval chain can approve before the wipe runs; the receipt is written only when the wipe completes. Spec chapter 70. Added (review 2026-10-28): an approval chain needs a row to point at before the wipe, and the receipt exists only after it.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null.
- `scope` text, not null. Check in (`entity`, `file`, `object`, `index`, `concept`, `silo`), the same values as `siloes.purge_receipts`.
- `object_type_id` uuid, null; `silo_file_id` uuid, null; `object_ref` text, null. The same per-scope column checks as `siloes.purge_receipts`: `entity` requires `object_type_id` and `object_ref`; `file` requires `silo_file_id` only; `object` requires `object_ref` only; `index` allows `object_type_id` (one type) or none (whole index); `concept` requires `object_type_id`; `silo` requires none.
- `requested_by` uuid, not null. Membership.
- `requested_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `status` text, not null, default `awaiting_approval`. Check in (`awaiting_approval`, `approved`, `rejected`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`).
- `approval_chain_id` uuid, null. The `action.approval_chains` row where the organisation configured a chain (70.3). Added (review 2026-10-28): approvers are the decided steps of this chain (`action.approval_steps`); where the organisation configured no chain, the requester holding `silo.purge` is the approver of record on the request.
- `decided_at` timestamptz, null.
- `completed_at` timestamptz, null. Check: not null exactly when `status = 'completed'`.
- `failure_stage` text, null. Names the failing stage, never a value.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). `updated_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `version` bigint, not null, default 1.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id)` → `siloes.siloes`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id)` → `ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, silo_file_id)` → `siloes.silo_files`; `(organisation_id, requested_by)` → `iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, approval_chain_id)` → `action.approval_chains`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, silo_id, requested_at desc)`: purge requests on the Silo page and the foreign key index; `(organisation_id, status)` where `status in ('awaiting_approval','approved','running')`: open requests and the wipe worker; `(organisation_id, silo_file_id)` where `silo_file_id is not null`, `(organisation_id, object_type_id)` where `object_type_id is not null` and `(organisation_id, approval_chain_id)` where `approval_chain_id is not null`: foreign key indexes.
Security: RLS standard. Written by the Silo's service (`siloes-capture` or `siloes-import`).

### `siloes.purge_receipts`
Purpose: append-only proof of what a wipe removed, from which stores, with the detector impact. Spec chapter 70.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `purge_request_id` uuid, not null. Added (review 2026-10-28): the request this receipt completes. The receipt stays append-only and is inserted only at completion.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null.
- `scope` text, not null. Check in (`entity`, `file`, `object`, `index`, `concept`, `silo`).
- Changed: `target_ref text` (reference to an object, file or object type, untyped) is replaced by three typed columns: `object_type_id` uuid, null; `silo_file_id` uuid, null; `object_ref` text, null (a resolved object reference for `entity`, a definition object name for `object`). Checks by scope: `entity` requires `object_type_id` and `object_ref`; `file` requires `silo_file_id` only; `object` requires `object_ref` only; `index` allows `object_type_id` (one type) or none (whole index); `concept` requires `object_type_id`; `silo` requires none.
- `removed` jsonb, not null. What was removed, as references and counts per store. Never values. Check object.
- `counts` jsonb, not null. Rows, files, bytes. Check object.
- `impact` jsonb, not null. Detectors, timelines, lead times and search routes that stop working.
- Changed: `approved_by uuid[]` removed. Changed (review 2026-10-28): `siloes.purge_receipt_approvers` is dropped; approvers are the decided steps of the request's approval chain (`purge_requests.approval_chain_id → action.approval_steps`), or the requester where no chain is configured.
- Changed (review 2026-10-28): `requested_by`, `approval_chain_id` and `requested_at` removed; they are reached through `purge_request_id`. The scope and target columns stay, because the receipt is the self-contained proof of what was removed.
- `completed_at` timestamptz, not null. Written at completion; the receipt is inserted once the wipe is done.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, purge_request_id)` (Added (review 2026-10-28): one receipt per request).
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id)` → `siloes.siloes`; `(organisation_id, object_type_id)` → `ontology.object_types`; `(organisation_id, silo_file_id)` → `siloes.silo_files`; `(organisation_id, purge_request_id)` → `siloes.purge_requests` (Added (review 2026-10-28)). Changed (review 2026-10-28): the `requested_by` and `approval_chain_id` references removed with their columns.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, silo_id, completed_at desc)`: receipts on the Silo page; `(organisation_id, completed_at desc)`: organisation purge ledger replayed before a restore opens to traffic (8.2); `(organisation_id, silo_file_id)` where `silo_file_id is not null` and `(organisation_id, object_type_id)` where `object_type_id is not null`: foreign key indexes.
Security: RLS standard; append-only (trigger rejects update and delete; `silo_app` holds `insert, select`). Written by the Silo's service (`siloes-capture` or `siloes-import`). Retention: indefinite, because "prove you deleted it" is the next question. Not purged by a Silo purge.

### Hot paths (siloes)

1. Capture lookup on every query result and change stream event ("is this object type held in a live Capture Silo"): `(organisation_id, object_type_id, silo_id) where removed_at is null` on `silo_object_types`, held in memory by `siloes-capture` and refreshed on policy version change.
2. Baseline compare per observed row: primary key of `silo_baselines`.
3. State of one object's property at time T (scrubbing): `(organisation_id, silo_id, object_type_id, object_ref, property, observed_at desc)` on `transitions`, pruned to one organisation partition and the months at or before T.
4. History detector scan of one property across objects: `(organisation_id, silo_id, object_type_id, property, observed_at)` on `transitions`.
5. Source resolution for the federated engine: `(organisation_id, source_connection_id) where source_connection_id is not null` on `siloes`, then `(organisation_id, object_type_id, kind) where dropped_at is null` on `warehouse_tables` for freshness.
6. Retention and purge: BRIN `(observed_at)` on `transitions`, `(organisation_id, silo_id, received_at desc)` on `silo_files`.

---

## Schema `billing`

The `billing` service is compiled out of the sovereign cell (chapter 7): the tables exist there and stay empty, and `entitlements` is filled by a staff path. Nothing in the product reads Stripe; every reader reads `entitlements` (71.4). Every Stripe object is created with `organisation_id` in its metadata, so a webhook handler learns the tenant from the verified event and then runs `set local app.org_id`, and no cross-tenant lookup is ever needed.

Relationships:
- `entitlements.subscription_id → subscriptions`, `contract_id → contracts`
- `seats.subscription_id → subscriptions`, `contract_id → contracts`, `membership_id → iam.memberships`, `allocated_scope_id → iam.scopes`
- `seat_allocations.scope_id → iam.scopes`
- `token_allowances.membership_id → iam.memberships`
- `token_balances.membership_id → iam.memberships`
- `token_transactions.membership_id → iam.memberships`, `engagement_id → fde.fde_engagements`
- `simulation_allowances.membership_id → iam.memberships`
- `purchases.purchased_by → iam.memberships`
- `storage_measurements.silo_id → siloes.siloes`
- `invoices.contract_id → contracts`
- `marketplace_payouts.connector_id → connect.connectors`

### `billing.subscriptions`
Purpose: a self-serve Stripe subscription (Standard or Business) for an organisation. Spec chapter 71.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `plan` text, not null. Check in (`standard`, `business`).
- `seat_count` integer, not null. Check `>= 1`.
- `term` text, not null. Check in (`monthly`, `annual`).
- `discount_tier` text, not null. Seat discount tier applied (72.1). Check in (`list`, `tier_25_99`, `tier_100_249`, `tier_250_499`, `quoted`).
- `stripe_customer_id` text, not null. Added. Needed to raise further Stripe objects for the organisation.
- `stripe_subscription_id` text, not null. Unique.
- `current_period_start` timestamptz, not null; `current_period_end` timestamptz, not null. Check `current_period_end > current_period_start`.
- `status` text, not null. Mirrors the organisation billing status. Check in (`active`, `past_due`, `suspended`, `cancelled`). Written only by the Stripe webhook handler or a staff path, in the same transaction that writes `iam.organisations.billing_status` (75.3).
- `cancelled_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Check: not null when `status = 'cancelled'`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added. `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (stripe_subscription_id)`; `unique (organisation_id)` where `status <> 'cancelled'` (one live subscription per organisation).
References: none beyond the organisation.
Indexes: the live-subscription unique serves the billing page; `(organisation_id, created_at desc)`: subscription history. The Stripe id unique serves nothing at read time (webhooks carry the organisation in metadata); it prevents duplicate mirroring.
Security: RLS standard for reads. Writes by `billing` only, from the verified webhook or a staff path. Compiled out of sovereign.

### `billing.contracts`
Purpose: an Enterprise contract held in Silo's database, from which entitlements derive. Spec chapter 74.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `status` text, not null, default `draft`. Added. Check in (`draft`, `awaiting_margin_approval`, `active`, `expired`, `terminated`). Entitlements derive only from `active`.
- `platform_fee` numeric(14,2), not null. Annual. Check `>= 0`.
- `seat_count` integer, not null; `seat_rate` numeric(10,2), not null. Check `>= 0`.
- `token_allocation` bigint, not null; `simulation_allocation` integer, not null; `storage_included_bytes` bigint, not null. Check `>= 0`. The two allocations are per seat per month (D45), as entitlements carry them.
- `storage_rate` numeric(6,4), not null, default 0.1000. Margin over provider cost, as a fraction (0.1000 is 10%). Check `>= 0`.
- `capabilities` text[], not null. Check `<@` (`sso`, `scim`, `custom_roles`, `dedicated`, `sovereign`).
- `sovereign` boolean, not null, default false.
- `fde_onboarding_bundled` boolean, not null, default false. Pending the open decision of 73.5.
- `term_start` date, not null; `term_end` date, not null. Check `term_end > term_start`. Term end is an explicit event (74.3).
- `payment_terms` text, not null. For example `net 30`.
- `purchase_order_ref` text, null.
- `renewal_state` text, not null, default `upcoming`. Check in (`upcoming`, `in_negotiation`, `renewed`, `lapsed`).
- `signed_by` text, null. Customer signatory. Check: not null when `status = 'active'`.
- `countersigned_at` timestamptz, null. Check: not null when `status = 'active'`.
- `quoted_margin` numeric(5,4), null. Added. Margin at quote from the calculator (74.4).
- `margin_approved_by` uuid, null; `margin_approved_at` timestamptz, null. Added. Staff sign-off under `contract.manage` where the margin is below the floor. `margin_approved_by` references `platform.operators`. Check: both set or both null.
- `stripe_customer_id` text, null. Added.
- `created_by` uuid, not null. Added (D45). The member of staff who quoted it; `margin_approved_by` is never the same person.
- `countersigned_by` uuid, null. Added (D45). The member of staff who countersigned for Silo; set exactly with `countersigned_at`.
- `overage_reported_tokens` bigint, not null, default 0. Added (D45). Overage already reported; a report is raised when it grows (74.3).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added. `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added.
- `version` bigint, not null, default 1. Added. Staff and the renewal job edit the same row.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; exclusion constraint `exclude using gist (organisation_id with =, daterange(term_start, term_end, '[]') with &&) where (status = 'active')`: no two active contracts overlap.
References: `margin_approved_by` → `platform.operators (id)` (single column, staff are not tenant data).
Indexes: the exclusion constraint's index serves "contract in force on date D"; `(organisation_id, term_end)` where `status = 'active'`: renewal tracking by term end (upcoming, lapsed).
Security: select under RLS standard (the customer sees its own contract under `billing.view`). Insert and update policy additionally require `current_setting('app.operator_id', true) is not null` (D45; it read `app.operator_session_id`): only a member of staff named by `admin-portal` can write, because `contract.manage` is staff only. Writes by `admin-portal` (through billing) and by billing's sweeps through security definer functions (D45). Exception to the single standard policy, stated because a tenant endpoint must not be able to alter its own contract. Compiled out of sovereign unless the sovereign cell runs the staff path.

### `billing.entitlements`
Purpose: the versioned set of limits and capabilities in force for an organisation; the only billing data the product reads. Spec chapter 71.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `seats` integer, not null. Licensed seat count. Check `>= 0`.
- `tokens_per_seat_period` integer, not null; `simulations_per_seat_period` integer, not null (zero on Standard); `daily_token_limit` integer, not null. Check `>= 0`.
- `storage_included_bytes` bigint, not null. Check `>= 0`.
- `capabilities` text[], not null. Check `<@` (`sso`, `scim`, `custom_roles`, `dedicated`, `sovereign`).
- `source` text, not null. Check in (`subscription`, `contract`).
- Changed: `source_id uuid` (references a subscription or a contract) is replaced by `subscription_id` uuid, null, and `contract_id` uuid, null, with `check ((source = 'subscription' and subscription_id is not null and contract_id is null) or (source = 'contract' and contract_id is not null and subscription_id is null))`.
- `effective_from` timestamptz, not null; `effective_to` timestamptz, null. Check `effective_to > effective_from`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id)` where `effective_to is null` (one open row); exclusion constraint `exclude using gist (organisation_id with =, tstzrange(effective_from, effective_to) with &&)` (no overlap, so the entitlement at any past moment is unambiguous).
References: `(organisation_id, subscription_id)` → `billing.subscriptions`; `(organisation_id, contract_id)` → `billing.contracts`.
Indexes: the open-row unique serves every entitlement read; the exclusion index serves "entitlement in force at T"; `(organisation_id, subscription_id)` where not null and `(organisation_id, contract_id)` where not null: foreign key indexes.
Security: RLS standard. Rows are never updated in place: a trigger allows only one update, setting `effective_to` on the open row, in the same transaction that inserts the successor. Written by `billing`; read by every service, cached keyed by `effective_from`.

### `billing.seats`
Purpose: one purchased seat and its lifecycle, independent of the membership occupying it. Spec chapter 72.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `subscription_id` uuid, null; `contract_id` uuid, null. Changed: the spec says one of the two is set; this is now `check (num_nonnulls(subscription_id, contract_id) = 1)`.
- `membership_id` uuid, null. Set only while `status = 'assigned'` (check both ways). History of who held the seat is in the audit trail, so removing a member never changes the seat (72.4).
- `allocated_scope_id` uuid, null. Scope whose pool the seat sits in while unassigned.
- `allocated_by` uuid, null; `allocated_at` timestamptz, null. Membership. Null for a seat never allocated to a scope. Check: both set or both null.
- `plan_tier` text, not null. Check in (`standard`, `business`, `enterprise`).
- `status` text, not null, default `unassigned`. Check in (`unassigned`, `assigned`, `reclaimed`, `released`).
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
- `released_at` timestamptz, null. Check: not null exactly when `status = 'released'`. A released seat cannot return to another status (trigger).
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added.
- `version` bigint, not null, default 1. Added. Two admins can assign the same seat.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, membership_id)` where `status = 'assigned'` (a membership holds one seat).
References: `(organisation_id, subscription_id)` → `billing.subscriptions`; `(organisation_id, contract_id)` → `billing.contracts`; `(organisation_id, membership_id)` → `iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, allocated_scope_id)` → `iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, allocated_by)` → `iam.memberships`.
Indexes:
- `(organisation_id, status)`: the index the spec names; seat counts by state on the billing page.
- `(organisation_id, allocated_scope_id, plan_tier)` where `status in ('unassigned','reclaimed')`: assignment finds an available seat in the admin's scope.
- `(organisation_id, subscription_id)` and `(organisation_id, contract_id)` where not null: foreign key indexes; the seat count rule counts assigned plus unassigned seats per subscription.
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `auth` (the catalogue gives seats to `auth`). The rule "subscription seat count is at least assigned plus unassigned" is enforced at seat creation by locking the subscription or contract row (`for update`) and counting in the same transaction.

### `billing.seat_allocations`
Purpose: a pool of seats held against a scope, drawn from its parent scope's pool. Spec chapter 72.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `scope_id` uuid, not null.
- `seats_allocated` integer, not null. Check `>= 0`. Bounded by the parent scope's pool and by the seats actually held below it; both checked in the service inside one transaction that locks the parent row, because a check constraint cannot see other rows.
- `plan_tier` text, not null. Same check as `seats.plan_tier`.
- `allocated_by` uuid, not null; `allocated_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added. `version` bigint, not null, default 1. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, scope_id, plan_tier)` (one current pool per scope and tier; changes update the row and write `seat_pool_allocated`).
References: `(organisation_id, scope_id)` → `iam.scopes`; `(organisation_id, allocated_by)` → `iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique serves pool lookup per scope; its prefix is the foreign key index.
Security: RLS standard. Writes by `auth`.

### `billing.token_allowances`
Purpose: a membership's token allowance for one billing period, with consumption and the daily counter. Spec chapter 73.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `period_start` timestamptz, not null; `period_end` timestamptz, not null. Check `period_end > period_start`.
- `tokens_granted` integer, not null. Prorated on mid-period assignment. Check `>= 0`.
- `tokens_consumed` integer, not null, default 0. Check `between 0 and tokens_granted`.
- `daily_limit` integer, not null. Check `>= 0`.
- `daily_consumed` integer, not null, default 0; `daily_consumed_on` date, null. Added. The daily limit checks against allowance consumption only (73.4); keeping the day's count here avoids scanning the ledger on every charge. `daily_consumed_on` is the date in the organisation's time zone; the charge resets the counter when the date differs. Check `between 0 and daily_limit` for `daily_consumed`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, membership_id, period_start)` (the spec rule: allowances do not pool and do not roll over, by constraint).
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id)` → `iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique serves the charge lookup for the current period and the foreign key; no other index. Removed members keep their row (consumed and unusable).
Security: RLS standard. Written by `metering`. The charge is one statement: update with `where tokens_consumed + :w <= tokens_granted and daily_consumed + :w <= daily_limit`, in the same transaction as the ledger insert. Created on seat assignment, never for unassigned seats (72.5).

### `billing.simulation_allowances`
Purpose: a membership's simulation allowance for one billing period. Spec chapter 73.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `period_start` timestamptz, not null; `period_end` timestamptz, not null. Check `period_end > period_start`.
- `simulations_granted` integer, not null. Check `>= 0`.
- `simulations_consumed` numeric(10,4), not null, default 0. Numeric because re-runs charge a fraction. Check `between 0 and simulations_granted`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, membership_id, period_start)`.
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id)` → `iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique only.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `metering`, same atomic charge pattern as tokens.

### `billing.token_balances`
Purpose: a membership's purchased and onboarding balances, which never expire. Spec chapter 73.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. Added. The spec key was `membership_id`; the conventions require `id`.
- `membership_id` uuid, not null.
- `purchased_remaining` integer, not null, default 0. Never expires. Check `>= 0`.
- `onboarding_grant_remaining` integer, not null, default 0. 200 on first activation. Check `between 0 and 200`.
- `simulations_purchased_remaining` numeric(10,4), not null, default 0. Added. The spec has purchases of kind `simulations` and no place to hold them; allowances alone cannot hold a top-up.
- `updated_at` timestamptz, not null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, membership_id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, membership_id)` → `iam.memberships`.
Indexes: the unique on membership only.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `metering`. Consumption order is onboarding grant, then allowance, then purchased balance (73.4), inside the charge transaction. Auto top-up credits this row and inserts a `billing.purchases` row in one transaction.

### `billing.token_transactions`
Purpose: append-only ledger of every charge, traceable to what it bought. Spec chapter 73.
Columns:
- `id` bigint, not null, `generated always as identity`.
- `membership_id` uuid, null. The membership whose balance was debited. Null when the debit was against a contract allocation. Check: `(source = 'contract') = (membership_id is null)`.
- `operation` text, not null. Check in (`compile`, `advanced_compile`, `connector_generation`, `repair_proposal`, `document_extraction`, `simulation`, `simulation_rerun`). Changed: the value `multi_system_compile` is renamed `advanced_compile` and is not accepted.
- `pool` text, not null. Check in (`tokens`, `simulations`). Check: `pool = 'simulations'` exactly when `operation in ('simulation','simulation_rerun')`.
- `weight` numeric(12,4), not null. Units charged. Changed: was `integer`; a simulation re-run charges a reduced fraction (73.7). Check `> 0` (a refusal never writes a charging row) and, when `pool = 'tokens'`, `weight = trunc(weight)`.
- `source` text, not null. Funding source. Check in (`grant`, `allowance`, `purchase`, `contract`). Changed (reading): chapter 52.6 says "source fde" for engagement charges; this file keeps `source` as the funding source (`contract` or `purchase`) and uses `engagement_id` to mark AI FDE work, because 73.6 has both columns and the funding source is what the dispute and the overage report need.
- `correlation_id` uuid, not null. Identity of the charged operation (the query, connector, file or simulation). Not a foreign key.
- Changed: the typed record it paid for is carried by four nullable foreign keys, at most one set: `silo_file_id` → `siloes.silo_files` (document extraction), `simulation_run_id` → `simulation.simulation_runs` (simulation, re-run), `heal_proposal_id` → `connect.heal_proposals` (repair proposal), `connector_manifest_id` → `connect.connector_manifests` (connector generation). Compile and advanced compile set none (the query is not a stored row). Check `num_nonnulls(...) <= 1`, and each operation requires its own column where one exists.
- `engagement_id` uuid, null. AI FDE engagement.
- `occurred_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
Keys: primary key `(id, occurred_at)`. No unique on `(organisation_id, id)`: nothing references a ledger.
Partitioning: range by month on `occurred_at`. Retention by partition drop by `silo_migrate`; minimum seven years (set as cell configuration; the spec gives none, and customers dispute against this table).
References (outgoing only): `(organisation_id, membership_id)` → `iam.memberships`; `(organisation_id, engagement_id)` → `fde.fde_engagements`; `(organisation_id, silo_file_id)` → `siloes.silo_files`; `(organisation_id, simulation_run_id)` → `simulation.simulation_runs`; `(organisation_id, heal_proposal_id)` → `connect.heal_proposals`; `(organisation_id, connector_manifest_id)` → `connect.connector_manifests`.
Indexes (on the partitioned parent):
- `(organisation_id, occurred_at desc)`: the customer's ledger screen and dispute view, and the contract overage report (filter `source = 'contract'` after the range).
- `(organisation_id, membership_id, occurred_at desc)` where `membership_id is not null`: a member's usage history.
- `(organisation_id, engagement_id, occurred_at)` where `engagement_id is not null`: engagement cost report by operation and stage (73.5, 54.1).
- BRIN `(occurred_at)`: partition maintenance and retention scans.
- No unique key for idempotency. A rephrase inside the short window charges once (73.2); that rule and retry safety are enforced in `metering` with an idempotency key in `redis-data` (24 hours), because a unique index on a partitioned table must include `occurred_at` and would not detect a retry across a month boundary.
Security: RLS standard; append-only (trigger rejects update and delete; `silo_app` holds `insert, select`). Written by `metering` only. The non-charging rules of 73.2 are enforced by `metering` not writing a row.

### `billing.purchases`
Purpose: each purchase of tokens, simulations or seats, manual or automatic. Spec chapter 73.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `kind` text, not null. Check in (`tokens`, `simulations`, `seats`).
- `quantity` integer, not null. Check `> 0`.
- `amount` numeric(12,2), not null. Check `>= 0`.
- `currency` char(3), not null, default `GBP`.
- `purchased_by` uuid, not null. Membership. For an auto top-up, the membership whose balance was topped up.
- `beneficiary_membership_id` uuid, null. Added. Whose balance receives tokens or simulations. Check: not null when `kind in ('tokens','simulations')`; null when `kind = 'seats'`.
- `auto_topup` boolean, not null, default false.
- `stripe_invoice_id` text, null. Added. Payment reference for reconciliation.
- `occurred_at` timestamptz, not null, default now().
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`.
References: `(organisation_id, purchased_by)`, `(organisation_id, beneficiary_membership_id)` → `iam.memberships`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, occurred_at desc)`: purchases list (`billing.view`); `(organisation_id, beneficiary_membership_id)` where not null: foreign key index.
Security: RLS standard; insert and select only (a correction is a Stripe refund recorded outside this table; whether refunds need a compensating row is open). Written by `metering` (top-up) and `billing` (purchase).

### `billing.storage_measurements`
Purpose: periodic measurement of bytes held and scanned per Silo per store, with provider cost, for billing at cost plus 10%. Spec chapter 74.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null.
- `store` text, not null. Check in (`postgres`, `gcs`, `bigquery`, `index`).
- `bytes_held` bigint, not null; `bytes_scanned` bigint, not null, default 0. Added: `bytes_egressed` bigint, not null, default 0. Check each `>= 0`.
- `provider_cost` numeric(14,6), not null. At the actual regional rate, for the interval since the previous measurement of the same Silo and store, so the period total is a sum. Added breakdown: `cost_storage`, `cost_compute`, `cost_egress` numeric(14,6), not null, default 0, with `check (provider_cost = cost_storage + cost_compute + cost_egress)`. The breakdown is needed because the invoice shows provider cost per line and the spec has one column (74.1).
- `period` text, not null. Billing period as `YYYY-MM`.
- `measured_at` timestamptz, not null.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, silo_id, store, measured_at)`.
References: `(organisation_id, silo_id)` → `siloes.siloes`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, period, silo_id)`: arrears invoice build per period and Silo; `(organisation_id, silo_id, measured_at desc)`: size trend on the Siloes page and the foreign key index.
Security: RLS standard; insert and select only. Written daily by `metering` from `siloes-capture` and `siloes-import` measurements, from the first day a Silo exists. Volume is Silos times stores times days, so no partitioning.

### `billing.silo_charges`

Purpose: Siloes billed at provider cost plus 10%, in arrears (spec 74.1, 74.2, 74.5). When a month closes, each organisation's `storage_measurements` for it are summed per Silo and store into one line: the provider cost of storage, compute and egress, less what the entitlement's included storage covers, plus 10%. The provider cost and the 10% are kept and shown apart on every line, never a blended rate. Added (D105).

Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null. `organisation_id` uuid, not null.
- `period` text, not null. `YYYY-MM`.
- `silo_id` uuid, not null. `store` text, not null: `postgres`, `gcs`, `bigquery`, `index`.
- `mean_bytes_held` bigint; `bytes_scanned` bigint; `bytes_egressed` bigint, not null. The month's figures, for the customer.
- `cost_storage`, `cost_compute`, `cost_egress` numeric(14,6), not null. Provider cost, summed from the measurements.
- `included_cost` numeric(14,6), not null. The storage cost the included storage covers: all of it where the organisation held, on average over its Silos and stores, no more than is included; else each line's storage cost times included over held. Check: between 0 and `cost_storage`.
- `provider_cost` numeric(14,6), not null. Check: storage less included, plus compute and egress.
- `uplift` numeric(14,6), not null. Check: `round(provider_cost * 0.1, 6)`.
- `amount` numeric(14,2), not null. Provider cost plus uplift, to the penny: the invoice line.
- `invoice_state` text, not null, default `pending`: `pending`, `invoiced`, `not_billed` (nothing due, or no subscription or contract to bill). `invoice_id` uuid, null; set exactly when invoiced.
- `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamptz.

Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, period, silo_id, store)`: a month is charged once. Silo to `siloes.siloes`, invoice to `billing.invoices`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, silo_id)`; `(organisation_id, invoice_id)` where invoiced; `(organisation_id, period)` where pending.
Security: RLS standard. Written by billing's sweep (silo_app: select, insert; update of `invoice_state`, `invoice_id` only); read by billing for `billing.view`; silo_report reads. `billing.silo_charges_due(period, limit)` (security definer) lists the organisations with a closed month to charge or still to invoice.

### `billing.invoices`
Purpose: each invoice mirrored from Stripe, or recorded manually when paid outside Stripe. Spec chapter 74.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `stripe_invoice_id` text, null. Null when manual. Unique where not null.
- `manual` boolean, not null, default false.
- `contract_id` uuid, null. Null for self-serve invoices.
- `period_covered` text, not null. `YYYY-MM`, or `YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM` for an annual invoice.
- `amount` numeric(14,2), not null. Check `> 0`. Added: `currency` char(3), not null, default `GBP`.
- `terms` text, not null.
- `due_date` date, not null.
- `status` text, not null, default `draft`. Check in (`draft`, `open`, `paid`, `overdue`, `void`).
- `paid_at` timestamptz, null. Check: not null when `status = 'paid'`.
- `recorded_by` uuid, null. Staff identity for manual payment, `platform.operators (id)`. Changed: stated as a staff reference, not a membership. Check: `manual` implies `recorded_by` not null and `stripe_invoice_id` null when `status = 'paid'`; not `manual` implies `recorded_by` null.
- `purchase_order` text, null.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). Added. `updated_at` timestamptz, not null. Added.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (stripe_invoice_id)` where not null.
References: `(organisation_id, contract_id)` → `billing.contracts`; `recorded_by` → `platform.operators (id)`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, created_at desc)`: invoices list; `(organisation_id, due_date)` where `status = 'open'`: overdue sweep, run per organisation by `billing`; `(organisation_id, contract_id)` where not null: foreign key index.
Security: RLS standard. Written by `billing` from verified Stripe webhooks, and by `admin-portal` (`payment.record`) for manual payments; the second path emits `payment_recorded_manually`. The status transition `overdue` moves `iam.organisations.billing_status` only through the staff or webhook path (75.3).

### `billing.marketplace_payouts`
Purpose: the 70% revenue share owed to the organisation that authored a community connector, per connector and period, with its payment state. Added table; the stress test found no marketplace tables. Spec chapter 16.5 states the 70% share; nothing else.
Columns:
- `id` uuid, not null.
- `organisation_id` uuid, not null. The author organisation: the tenant that owns the payout and may read it under `billing.view`.
- `connector_id` uuid, not null. The community connector.
- `period_start` date, not null; `period_end` date, not null. Calendar month. Check `period_end > period_start`.
- `gross` numeric(14,2), not null. Marketplace revenue attributed to the connector in the period. The attribution rule (which consuming organisations and charges count) is not in the spec; it is an open decision and must be fixed before the first payout. Check `>= 0`.
- `share_rate` numeric(5,4), not null, default 0.7000. Check `between 0 and 1`.
- `share_amount` numeric(14,2), not null. Check `share_amount = round(gross * share_rate, 2)`.
- `currency` char(3), not null, default `GBP`.
- `usage_summary` jsonb, not null, default `{}`. Counts only (for example number of organisations using the connector). Never an organisation identifier, so the author learns no customer from a payout. Check object.
- `status` text, not null, default `calculated`. Check in (`calculated`, `approved`, `transferring`, `paid`, `failed`, `void`).
- `stripe_connected_account_id` text, null. Added. Destination account at transfer time. Check: not null from `approved` onward.
- `stripe_transfer_id` text, null. Stripe transfer reference. Check: not null when `status = 'paid'`. Unique where not null.
- `approved_by` uuid, null; `approved_at` timestamptz, null. `platform.operators (id)`. Both set from `approved` onward.
- `paid_at` timestamptz, null. Check: not null when `status = 'paid'`.
- `failure_stage` text, null. Names the failing step. Check: not null when `status = 'failed'`.
- `created_at` timestamptz, not null, default now(). `updated_at` timestamptz, not null.
- `version` bigint, not null, default 1.
Keys: primary key `(id)`; `unique (organisation_id, id)`; `unique (organisation_id, connector_id, period_start)` (one payout per connector per month); `unique (stripe_transfer_id)` where not null.
References: `(organisation_id, connector_id)` → `connect.connectors (author_organisation_id, id)` (cross-domain requirement 3); `approved_by` → `platform.operators (id)`.
Indexes: `(organisation_id, period_start desc)`: the author's payout statement list; `(organisation_id, status)` where `status in ('approved','transferring','failed')`: the transfer worker, run per author organisation; the unique on connector and period is the foreign key index.
Security: select under RLS standard, so an author sees only its payouts. Insert and update policy requires `current_setting('app.operator_session_id', true) is not null`: payouts are computed from usage across tenants, which no tenant session can see, so they are written by the staff payout run (`admin-portal`) which sets `app.org_id` to the author organisation for each row. Exception stated for that reason. Audit events: `payout_calculated`, `payout_approved`, `payout_paid`, `payout_failed` (new). Compiled out of sovereign.

### Hot paths (billing)

1. Charge: unique `(organisation_id, membership_id, period_start)` on `token_allowances`, unique `(organisation_id, membership_id)` on `token_balances`, then insert into `token_transactions`. All in one transaction, target a handful of indexed single-row operations.
2. Entitlement in force now: partial unique `(organisation_id) where effective_to is null` on `entitlements`.
3. Seat assignment: `(organisation_id, allocated_scope_id, plan_tier) where status in ('unassigned','reclaimed')` on `seats`, then the partial unique on assigned membership.
4. Engagement cost report: `(organisation_id, engagement_id, occurred_at) where engagement_id is not null` on `token_transactions`.
5. Arrears Silo bill: `(organisation_id, period, silo_id)` on `storage_measurements`.
6. Overdue sweep and invoices list: `(organisation_id, due_date) where status = 'open'` and `(organisation_id, created_at desc)` on `invoices`.
