- D64 (implementation 2026-11-10, outbound webhook side effects):
  - `connect.webhook_endpoints.risk_class` (external or physical, default external): declared for an outbound target; a physical one makes an Action type naming it physical.
  - `connect.connection_credentials.purpose` gains `outbound_webhook_secret` (field `outbound_webhook_<id>`, so a connection holds one per target), and `iam.credential_unwraps.reason` gains `webhook`.
  - `action.webhook_deliveries`: one per Action and target, references only; a physical target's carries the allow-list entry it was queued under (`allowlist_entry_id`, frozen; D195), attempted by notify with backoff until delivered or failed; `action.webhook_deliveries_due` finds due ones across organisations. `receipt_id` has no foreign key: the receipt is written after the side effects are decided.
  - Why: outbound webhooks as side effects, signed and retried, the receipt recording delivery and not effect (20.4, 42.6).
- D115 (implementation 2026-11-15, as-of and history questions compiled; spec 26.4, 69.6, 69.16): the model's plan in names may carry `asOf` (a date written YYYY-MM-DD, or a date and time with its offset, and the asker's words) or `history` (a period expression and the asker's words); compile turns the moment, and a between's ends, into parameters, so the plan holds none. The instructions say when to use each, and that each reads one object type without aggregate, hops or a node period, never together; a plan that combines them otherwise is refused, not repaired (`compile.plan_invalid`). The planner takes an as-of date as the end of that day in the organisation's calendar. An Ask thread's stored plan in names carries the as-of or history words, for its later turns.
- D116 (implementation 2026-11-15, large aggregates across one link from the Warehouse; spec 69.6, 27.7): a large aggregate grouped on the root type, with measures over the root and over the objects one link away, is answered from the Warehouse when the plan has exactly one hop from the root along the link's default route, with no junction, no filter on the far type and no group on its properties. `aggregateWarehouse` takes the hop (link type, far object type, direction) and a measure's `node` (0 the root, 1 the far type); the generator reads each side's current state with the engine's dispute rules, joins the root's groups to the link rows and the far type's rows, and computes the far measures over each group's distinct linked objects, so an object linked to several roots in a group counts once. The answer's watermark is the earliest of the two types' and the link's (`warehouseCoverage` now reports link watermarks), and the set counts as large when either type's row count passes the bound. Every other multi-type plan (several hops, a junction, a filter or group on the far type, a period on a node) still goes to the sources and is merged there.
- D117 (implementation 2026-11-15, the tenant migration bundle streamed; spec 6.4): the bundle is written and read as a stream, so no process holds an organisation whole. Format `silo.tenant_bundle.v2`: the header as before, then segments, each at most 1 MiB of payload gzipped and sealed under AES-256-GCM with its own nonce, its associated data the header, the segment's number and whether it is the last, so a segment altered, dropped, moved or added, a bundle cut short at a segment's end, or a header altered, refuses to open. The payload is a sequence of records in a fixed order (the organisation's keys, operators, its row, member users, each table and its rows in batches, the migration and its history, the checksums, each stored file and its bytes in 1 MiB chunks, an end record); the load refuses records out of that order, a table's rows outside it, a file short or long, or a bundle with no end. Each table is read at both ends through a cursor in byte order of its rows' text (`collate "C"`), batch at a time, and its checksum (SHA-256 over the sorted rows, unchanged) is worked out as the rows pass; rows held in memory (the organisation's row, member users) are sorted by their bytes to match. Object storage gained streamed uploads (`openUpload`: a GCS resumable upload, an S3 multipart upload in 16 MiB parts); the destination reads the bundle by range. The export and the load each allow ten minutes idle in transaction, since they wait on object storage between statements. The destination's verifying stage reads only the first record, the keys. No schema change.
- D118 (implementation 2026-11-15, the organisation export's bundle streamed; spec 2.6): `bundle.tar.gz` is uploaded as it is written (`openUpload`), one artefact at a time, so the export holds one artefact, never the bundle. Each file's header, bytes and padding are gzip members of their own (RFC 1952 lets a file hold several; gunzip and tar read them as one stream), and the bundle's size and SHA-256 are worked out as it is written. The manifest is now the archive's last file, since it lists every file's checksum. `ORG_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES` now bounds one artefact (each is still built in memory), not the bundle. A failed run abandons the upload, leaving no bundle. No schema change.
- D119 (implementation 2026-11-15, Fleet's SBOM checks; spec 11.1, 11.2, 11.6; directory database): "SBOMs are checked for vulnerabilities daily; a critical one in a reachable component blocks stable." Tables in `fleet`: `release_sboms` (each SBOM the signed manifest names, received only when its SHA-256 matches), `release_components` (by package URL, with the OSV ecosystem and name), `advisories` and `advisory_packages` (a mirror of OSV records, reduced to what matching needs), `advisory_feeds` (per ecosystem: how far it is synced, and a replica's lease), `vex_statements`, `release_findings` and `sbom_checks`. Decided with the user: advisories come from OSV's exports, mirrored rather than queried, so the check is complete and fresh, no SBOM leaves Silo, and the sovereign tier runs the same code against a UK mirror or a `file:` copy (a Google host is refused there, spec 6.5); reachability is what a VEX document in the release says, never assumed. A feed is loaded whole from `all.zip` the first time (read by range; zip64), then from `modified_id.csv` back to its last sync less a day's margin. A finding is a component an advisory affects by OSV's evaluation, with order per ecosystem (Semantic Versioning, PEP 440, dpkg, apk); a range that cannot be ordered counts as affected. Severity is the record's highest: a CVSS v3 score, or the database's rating; a malicious-package record is critical; an unrated record takes the rating of records sharing an alias. A critical finding blocks unless the latest VEX statement (OpenVEX or CycloneDX VEX, uploaded by the security officer: `fleet.release.expedite`) says not_affected or fixed. Promotion into stable, sovereign and their agent channels needs every SBOM of the channel's artefacts, every feed they draw on synced within `FLEET_ADVISORY_MAX_AGE_HOURS` (48), and no blocking finding, checked again in the promotion's transaction. The worker syncs each feed daily (`FLEET_ADVISORY_SYNC_HOURS`) and checks every live release again; `syncAdvisories` runs it now.
- D120 (implementation 2026-11-15, change windows and freezes for dedicated cells; spec 11.2 wave 5, 11.5; directory database): stable's waves no longer hold the dedicated cells. Once stable's head has passed its shared waves, each dedicated cell gets a rollout of its own (`fleet.rollouts.cell_id`, one running per cell): one wave of that cell, soaked 24 hours, gated and rolled back like any other, alone. It carries the notice (`notice`, `noticed_at`): the release, whether it is a security fix, the release before, the earliest start (`FLEET_CHANGE_NOTICE_HOURS`, 72, after the notice; a security fix at once) and the SBOM difference of the images (added, removed, changed versions; marked incomplete where either release lacks an SBOM). It starts only when the notice has stood, the moment is inside one of the customer's weekly windows in their time zone (a window may run past midnight; none means any time), and no freeze is in force, unless the release is a security fix the named change authority approved for that freeze. The customer's policy is `fleet.cell_change_policies`, replaced whole by `putCellChangePolicy` from the cell's Fleet agent (not built yet: it waits with `desiredRelease` and `reportVerdict`); `desiredRelease` gives a dedicated cell its own rollout's answer and the notice with what holds it (notice, window or freeze), for the customer to see in advance. A newer head replaces one still waiting; one under way finishes first; a release the cell was rolled back from is not offered again. So one customer's freeze holds no other customer's release, and no channel. Decided here (the spec puts every dedicated cell in one wave 5, which a freeze would hold for everyone). Still to come: the customer setting windows, freezes and the change authority in their cell, and the agent carrying them.
- D121 (implementation 2026-11-16, the customer's change windows and freezes in their cell; spec 11.5, 11.6): `gov.change_policies` (the weekly windows in the organisation's time zone and the named change authority), `gov.change_freezes` (from a moment to a moment, ended early by hand) and `gov.change_exceptions` (the change authority's written approval of one release in one freeze: the statement is the writing; never changed). Set through policy's `setChangePolicy`, `setChangeFreeze` (the caller names the freeze, so a retry finds it) and `endChangeFreeze`, each needing `org.change_window.manage` across the organisation; `approveFreezeException` is the named change authority's alone, whatever permissions anyone else holds. A freeze set, ended or excepted raises `change_freeze_set` (now catalogued, with the policy events). Any member reads the policy; on a shared commercial cell it reads as not applying and the setters refuse (`policy.change_windows_not_applicable`). `gov.change_policies_for_fleet` (security definer, read-only) gives every organisation's policy, freezes not yet over and their approvals in fleet-control's `putCellChangePolicy` shape, through `listChangePoliciesForFleet`, for the cell's Fleet agent to carry (D120); both ends of that carry wait for the agent.
- D122 (implementation 2026-11-16, Fleet's own events; spec 11.6; directory database): the global tier has no organisation's audit log, so fleet-control keeps `fleet.events`: each event appended in the transaction that made the change, under fleet-control's lock (one order), its hash SHA-256 over the previous event's hash and its own canonical content, so an event altered, removed or put out of order breaks the chain from there (`verifyFleetEvents` names where). `fleet_writer` may only add. Recorded: `release_built` and `release_signed` at registration; `release_promoted` (and `release_expedited`) when a promotion applies, then the `rollout_started` it causes; `rollout_gate_failed` (a failing gate, or a missing signal, with the cells and gates) and `rollout_rolled_back` (with why, and the release gone back to), also on a manual halt; `rollout_completed`; a dedicated cell's own rollout starting when its window opens; `change_freeze_set` when a cell's policy brings a new freeze; `sovereign_release_countersigned` in the sovereign fleet-control's own log; `migration_applied` once per cell, release and migration (`reportMigrationApplied`, checked against the release's manifest). Events about one dedicated cell carry it, and its Fleet agent reads them (`listCellEvents`) to write into the customer's audit log; that and the migration report wait for the agent. Staff read them (`/staff/v1/fleet/events`, by release or cell) and check the chain. `bundle_verified` and `bundle_refused` belong to the on-premises Fleet agent's local audit log, still to come.
- D123 (implementation 2026-11-16, Silo Agent stage A1: pools, enrolment tokens and the agent CA; spec 10.2, 10.3, 10.9): the Silo Agent is written in Go, in `agent/` beside `app/server` (decided with the user, settling 10.1's open decision). The cell side starts here, on the schema the catalogue already had. connect-registry: `createAgentPool` and `issueAgentEnrolmentToken` (`agent.enrol`; a `silo_enr_` token shown once, kept as its hash, single use, 24 hours), `listAgentPools` (`agent.view`; a production pool with fewer than two live agents is marked under-provisioned, 10.3) and `revokeAgent` (`agent.manage`; the agent and its service principal revoked in one transaction). connect-runtime serves agent.<cell> (`AGENT_ENDPOINT_PORT`, TLS 1.3 only, HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1, behind a TCP pass-through load balancer since the mutual TLS ends there) where `POST /v1/enrol` takes the token, a PKCS#10 request for a P-256 key the agent generated and keeps, and what the agent is. In one transaction it consumes the token (`connect.resolve_enrolment_token`, which names the organisation), has the cell's agent CA issue a 30-day client certificate (client authentication only, naming the agent and organisation, `urn:silo:agent:<id>`), and records an `agent` service principal and the agent (offline until its tunnel connects) with the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint. A request the CA refuses rolls it all back, so it does not spend the token. The CA's key and certificate come from the deployment (`AGENT_CA_KEY`, `AGENT_CA_CERT_FILE`, P-256), as the SAML key does; the code signs with `@peculiar/x509` (2.2.0, the version passkeys already use, so one ASN.1 tree loads) and never generates a key. `agent_pool_created`, `agent_enrolment_token_issued`, `agent_enrolled` and `agent_revoked` are now raised. Next: the tunnel (A2), the Go agent (A3), reads through it (A4).
- D124 (implementation 2026-11-16, Silo Agent stage A2: the tunnel; spec 10.2, 10.3, 10.6, 10.7): the agent holds one HTTP/2 connection to agent.<cell> with its client certificate. `POST /v1/tunnel` stays open: heartbeats go up (every 10 s: version, active calls, CDC readers, whether discovery is off locally) and work and close frames come down; each piece of work is answered on its own stream, `POST /v1/work/:id`, ending with done or error. Frames are newline-delimited JSON (`contracts/connect-runtime/agentTunnel.contract.ts`), which the Go agent speaks too. The tunnel and work routes need a certificate the agent CA issued and still valid. The agent is found by the certificate's fingerprint (`connect.resolve_agent`), checked again on every heartbeat and before every piece of work: a revoked agent gets no work, and its tunnel closes at its next heartbeat at the latest; a second tunnel from one agent replaces the first. Three missed heartbeats mark an agent unhealthy (`agent_unhealthy`, and it gets no work); the next marks it recovered (`agent_recovered`); a closed tunnel leaves it offline (a revoked one stays revoked). Its row is written on each change of health, and an unchanged heartbeat at most once a minute. Work goes to the least-loaded healthy agent of the pool (the calls it reports plus those given it since) and is answered only by that agent, within its deadline; with none connected, it is refused at once as source unreachable, never queued (10.6). connect-runtime's SQL engine now reads and writes through the tunnel (`tunnelChannel`): rows collected, a transaction's row counts returned, a source's refusal kept as its SQLSTATE alone. One replica holds an agent's tunnel; giving work to a pool's agents held by another replica is still to come. Also: `fast-xml-parser` 5.12.1 (GHSA-474x-hrwr-fgx4).
- D150 (implementation 2026-11-17, backend stage B6: KEK rotation; spec 61.1, 61.2, 61.9): a member of Silo staff holding key.rotate (a new staff capability carrying the spec's name: a Silo operator role in the cell, never a tenant permission) starts a rotation through the admin portal, naming the new key in the cell's provider; the credential service checks it exists there and wraps (Silo never creates a key) and makes it the active key version, the old one decrypt_only (one rotation at a time). A sweep in the credential service then re-wraps every sealed row's DEK (connection credentials, identity providers, MFA factors, organisation keys) under the new version, one transaction a row: unwrapped under the old version and wrapped under the new inside the provider, each with the row's binding and the version as context; the ciphertext is never opened. Rows sealed under the old version meanwhile by a process whose registry had not yet moved are swept too. When no live row references the old version it is retired (the existing guard refuses otherwise). The registry and the rows span every organisation and user, so the steps run through narrow security-definer functions only silo_credential may execute (start, list references with their wrapped DEKs and binding fields, re-wrap one row, retire). key_rotation_started (with the operator), key_version_retired and key_rotation_completed are written to every organisation's audit log, since each one's secrets are re-wrapped. A connection's secret replacing a live one now raises credential_rotated. startup_refused_no_kms_key is the credential service's own log event when its start-up key check fails: no organisation is involved before it starts. The PKCS#11 HSM adapter (graphene-pk11) was already built and tested; the coverage line saying otherwise was stale.
- D151 (implementation 2026-11-17, backend stage B7: association analysis, outcomes and investigation; spec 38.6, 38.8): association analysis runs on demand (recognition.run) over the whole organisation, so each computation is one set superseding the last (supersedes_computation_id). Populations are named: the objects a detector's current findings name on a type, and designated outcomes. An outcome (recognition.outcome_designations, new; outcome.designate, revoked never deleted) is a yes/no property the designator may examine, read under the computing actor's access when associations are computed, or a detector (finding kind); designation never touches what a detector raises. Within a type every pair is stated with its co-occurrence and sample size (the largest population of each detector's latest run, never below the populations' union); a pair touching an outcome is stated even at zero, other pairs only where they co-occur. Across each active link type joining two types with populations, the pairs are read through the executor (one plan rooted at the link's from type, one hop) and stated in both directions ("is linked through"), on two new columns: associations.link_type_id and link_direction, with checks that both or neither are set and that a same-type association has no link. A link type with several routes and no default is not guessed. Temporal order uses evidence, not raised_at (every run re-raises, so raised_at only says when the detector last ran): per detector and object, the start of the current episode (the first run naming it since a run that examined it and did not) and that latest absent run; A precedes B on an object only when a run of B examined it and did not name it while A already named it, otherwise the order is unordered. Statements are fixed language ("occurs together with", "precedes in N of M instances", "is linked through"); a name that would carry a causal word or "fraud" is replaced by its API name or a neutral phrase, and a final guard refuses a statement that still would (the table's no-causal check remains). Reading applies the reader's access: both types, and for each side the property it names or every property and marking on its detector's current findings; the rest is counted as withheld. Investigation (recognition.run) answers gaps (empty values, records standing alone, properties one system holds, open resolution proposals; history: when a property became empty and from which connection), contradictions (disputed values, disagreement findings; history: on the disputed objects, which connection changed the value last and since when), anomalies (the federated detectors' findings or why they have none; history: timing deviation and drift) and clusters (history throughout: recurrence, associations over designated outcomes, shared identifiers). Whether history is held comes from a new siloes-capture read, readCaptureCoverage: the type's captured properties the reader may read in full. Without it the answer is the current part plus a statement naming what needs Capture; with it, a property that is not captured is named as unanswerable rather than answered from current state. Investigation never names fraud. resolution's listResolutionProposals gains recognition as a caller. The redis key audit now returns bounded samples of the keys it counts and takes a match glob; its test counts its own keys rather than whole-instance deltas, which drifted as other tests' keys expired.
- D152 (implementation 2026-11-17, backend stage B8a: receipt purge; spec 46.1, 48.2, 65.3, 70): receipts are the one place record values persist by default, so they are purged under chapter 70's rules. Purging a mutation's values nulls every value it kept, the receipt's document, the mutation's intent, diff and manifest values, the prior states, the read-back values and a revert's conflict values, and fails a webhook delivery still waiting (payload cleared, last_error receipt_purged); the hash, references and counts stay, so the audit ledger's hash still matches. The tables' purge guards admit only silo_migrate, so actions runs one narrow definer function, action.purge_mutation_values, that purges exactly one mutation in the caller's organisation (app.org_id). A sweep purges receipts past retention_until (730 days) with the rest of their mutation's values (receipt_purged, reason retention), run by actions' worker across organisations (action.organisations_with_receipts_due) and by staff through the existing organisation retention operation, which now also returns the receipts swept. On request, a holder of silo.purge asks for one receipt or every receipt of a commit on an object (an erasure, 65.3), recorded in action.receipt_purges (new); as every wipe, it routes through the organisation's default approval policy where one requires approvals (a new approval-chain subject, receipt_purge, approved by holders of silo.purge other than the requester), otherwise it runs at once. It raises chapter 70's purge_requested, purge_approved or purge_rejected, and purge_completed with the counts. A purged receipt is not purged again. The Action ledger's values for the purged receipts are cleared where the Warehouse's ledger holds values (prior_values and new_values; references and outcomes stay), with ledger_purged. Separately, a webhook delivery's sealed payload is now cleared once the delivery ends (payload nullable, payload_cleared_at, cleared once and never changed), so values do not outlive their use.
- D153 (implementation 2026-11-17, backend stage B8b/c: webhook effect and private targets; spec 20.4, 10.4): an outbound webhook target may declare a status endpoint (connect.webhook_endpoints.status_url, HTTPS). Then the receipt records effect, not delivery alone (reason effect_read_from_status_endpoint; the preview's side effect says records: effect), and after delivery notify asks the endpoint GET with the delivery id, signed as a delivery is over the timestamp and the delivery id, for {"state": "applied" | "pending" | "failed"}: applied or failed ends it (failed raises outbound_webhook_failed, reason effect_failed); pending, or no answer, is asked again with the delivery backoff until 24 hours after delivery, then the effect is unconfirmed (webhook_deliveries.effect, effect_attempts, next_effect_check_at, effect_checked_at; action.webhook_effects_due). A mutation's deliveries and their effects are read at GET /actions/mutations/:id/webhook-deliveries. A target on a connection reached through the Silo Agent is posted by the agent inside the customer's network: the request is the one statement of a write, so each attempt asks actions for an execution grant (signWebhookGrant: only for a pending delivery on a live agent target) over SHA-256 of the statements as the agent receives them; connect-runtime checks it and that the address is the registered target's (or its status endpoint's) before the work leaves the cell, and the Go agent checks it again and spends it (work kind http.send). The agent reaches only hosts its owner allows (targets, at the allowed addresses), over HTTPS with the system's roots plus an optional customer CA (webhookCaFile), never follows a redirect, carries only a webhook's headers, and returns the status code and a status endpoint's state, never a body. A status read through the agent needs no grant. The ledger stays the Warehouse's (69.14 lists action_ledger among the Warehouse's tables), so the coverage line asking for an Import Silo copy is closed without one.
- D154 (implementation 2026-11-17, backend stage B9a/b: OData and the AI builder from typed descriptions; spec 14.4, 16.3): OData is a protocol with its own engine (protocol kind odata, versions 4.0 and 2.0; source kind odata naming the service path, the entity set, each property's EDM type and maxPages), because SAP S/4HANA and ECC are reached through it (14.4). Pushdown compiles natively, as SQL's does, so an OData filter declares no CEL patch: $filter from comparisons, in as a disjunction (portable to 4.0 and 2.0), contains (2.0: substringof) and startswith, and null checks; $orderby; $top; $select of the fields read. Every value is a typed literal the engine formats from the property's EDM type (a string's quotes doubled; numbers, GUIDs and times checked and written in the version's form), so a value never becomes syntax. Version 4.0 reads value and pages by @odata.nextLink; 2.0 reads d.results and d.__next with $format=json, its /Date(ms)/ values read as instants. A next link is followed only within the connection's base URL; one leaving it is refused (odata.next_link_foreign), and pages past maxPages are refused, never truncated. Writes are written by the engine (a manifest declares create, update, updateFull, delete, upsert with no request): POST to the entity set, PATCH to the typed key (2.0: MERGE tunnelled through POST, as SAP Gateway expects), PUT, DELETE, and upsert as PATCH on 4.0 only; a create reads its key from the entity returned. The visual builder and the AI builder draft from $metadata with no model: entity sets with primitive keys become objects, EDM types become field types and are kept for literals, filters are declared by type, sort and limit, and relationships come from referential constraints (4.0 navigation properties, 2.0 associations); writes are left undeclared, since $metadata does not say whether a service accepts them. The AI builder now also takes a WSDL, a GraphQL introspection result or SDL, or $metadata (documentation kinds wsdl, graphql, odata): compiled as the visual builder imports them, never charged; its probe reads each object as declared (a sample), an object that does not read is left out and named, conformance runs and removes failing pushdown from the manifest directly, and the mapping is proposed from the declared fields and links weighed by fill rate. OData is read from the cell in this release (an agent sends webhooks, not reads); the pushdown explanation shows the entity set and the query with typed literals.
- D155 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B9c: email fallback; spec 14.4, 16.1, 62.5): a system with no API is connected by its notifications. Protocol kind email, objects of source kind email (never read on demand: a read is refused, email.not_readable, the records being held live in the state plane or by a Capture Silo), and a changeStream.email block: the senders taken (addresses or @domains) and rules, each a set of conditions (the sender, subject or text containing a line of plain text, ignoring case) and fields (the text after a label, to the line's end, the next word or a closing text), with upsert or delete. Templates, never regular expressions, so no message can make extraction slow, and a rule must extract its object's identifier. Enabling the stream mints an address, c-<26 base-32 characters>@<INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN>, in connect.email_addresses (new: token hash unique across the cell, live per connection, counts of messages taken and set aside, revoked on disable, never deleted), resolved by connect.resolve_email_address since the relay posts with no organisation in hand. The cell's mail relay (a provider's inbound route, or the self-managed SMTP relay) posts each message whole to the gateway's POST /api/v1/hooks/email with the envelope recipient and an HMAC-SHA256 signature under INBOUND_EMAIL_SECRET over the recipient, a dot and the message; change-stream checks the signature before parsing. A small MIME reader in utils (headers, encoded words, base64 and quoted-printable, charsets, multipart, HTML reduced to text, bounded) gives the sender, subject, text, Date and Message-ID; a message forwarded as an attachment is read as the notification it carries. A matching rule gives one change, published as any source's (declared fields only, typed from the text; the Message-ID as the source sequence, so a repeat delivery is dropped); a message from another sender, matching no rule, or without its identifier is set aside and counted. No message is stored or logged. An email connection is confirmed without the conformance suite's read classes, which cannot apply to it. The AI builder takes sample notifications (documentation kind email) and drafts the rules in the cell with no model: spec 62.5 allows no carve-out but Import extraction, and notifications carry record values. Samples are grouped by subject shape; a rule's condition is the longest run of words its subjects share, its fields the labelled lines most of its samples carry, typed (a unit closing a number ends the field), its identifier the #reference every subject carries or an identifier-like label; the rules are tried on the samples and seldom-extracted fields left out. Only counts are kept, never a sample; the build's probe and conformance say they do not apply, and the mapping is proposed from the fields.
- D156 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B10: Import definitions and Explorer facets; spec 68.3, 69.3, 34.1): a definition is drafted from a document as well as a tabular file. The document is sent to the model under the 62.5 carve-out (refused until it is acknowledged for the Silo), which proposes objects and fields, each read by its label as printed or, in prose, by an instruction; the proposal is validated on the way out of the model and refused rather than repaired (import.draft_invalid), then probed by extracting from the same document with it; the answer holds names, types and counts, never a value, and the draft is charged as a document extraction. The prebuilt catalogue ships common formats as definitions, structure only (invoice, purchase order, delivery note and receipt read by labels; bank statement and timesheet exports read by columns, never a model); publishing one names its key and must publish the catalogue's own document (import.prebuilt_changed otherwise: a changed one is published through the builder), and the key is in silo_definition_published. Explorer's facet counts and ranges over indexed properties are served from a fresh Object Index: a run with the new trigger explorer_facet whose plan is a count by at most one property, or a range (min, max, count), of one node may be answered from the index's entries, counted in the engine and stated as of the refresh, falling back to the sources as any index answer does. Every other aggregate (anything that might feed an Action preview, spec 69.3's binding rule) reads the sources or the Warehouse. The web client's facets will run with the facet trigger when the client resumes. S3 signed uploads are not built: signed URLs are GCS's (decision 2026-11-14). Moving Silo contents held in BigQuery in a tenant migration, and multi-type questions from the Warehouse, remain.
- D157 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B11: Crons that mutate resolvable types and Action types with parameters; spec 40.5): a mutate action takes the Action type's parameter values, set by the person attaching it and checked against the type (each required one given, none undeclared, each of its type); they are sealed to the action's row (automation_actions.parameter_values, a new sealed column, mutate only), only their names kept in its configuration, never shown back, and opened by actions when the Cron proposes. A Cron's question now runs with references (a new runPlan option, part of the result's cache key): each root object carries the source records it was merged from (connection, source object, identifier: identifiers only), and the runner names every record of every object, so a type several systems feed is mutated through each record in a system the Action type may write through (actions keeps those, refusing a run with none, mutation.cron_no_writable_record). The single-source and primary-key restriction is gone; a single-source type's run takes its one record the same way, tested end to end, and a resolvable type's records come from the same merged objects.
- D158 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B12: tenant reads under a break-glass session; spec 13.3): a tenant_read session reads the tenant's tables on the reporting replica (PG_REPORT_URL) as silo_report, never on the primary. Which tables and columns it may read is the role's grants, read from the catalogue (has_column_privilege): a table with organisation_id the role holds SELECT on, its readable columns only and never a bytea (sealed) one, so a partial reader never sees a sealed column; identifiers come from the catalogue, never from the request (an unlisted table is staff.table_unknown). Row-level security binds the read to the session's organisation and every read filters on it as well. Each listing and each page is counted against the session and recorded in the customer's audit log as operator_access_resource_touched naming the route and the table (tenant_tables, tenant_rows:schema.table). A cell with no reporting replica refuses the read (config.reporting_replica); a metadata_read session is refused (operator_access.level_too_low). No new table.
- D159 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B13a: the AI FDE's last three metrics; spec 54.1): every metric of 54.1 now cites its events, so none is named as not measured. The events they need are raised: the state plane audits subscription_opened (the set, its source connection and object, the object count, live or polled; after the viewer has its snapshot) and subscription_closed (the reason; once, by whichever replica ends the row), both in a new high-volume class; Studio audits app_opened on every open (version, whether the published version, whether reduced; high volume; not named in 35.13, needed by 54.1); an ontology merge names the elements it changed (ontology_proposal_merged.element_ids, up to a hundred). Time to first live clone is working hours from agent install to the first live subscription with objects on a connection whose mapping was confirmed before it; time to first app is working days to the first open of the published version of an app the engagement created, by someone other than the person who accepted it; post-handover reversal rate is, of the artefacts the engagement created before handover (its accepted proposals' applied targets), those retired, reverted or revised within ninety days of fde_engagement_handed_over, over the artefacts created, as it stands while the window runs. What counts per kind: an element deprecated, retired or changed by a merge to main; an Action type retired or given a later version; an app archived, rolled back, withdrawn or given a version after its first; a dashboard's view archived; a Cron deleted or paused by a person (not the scheduler); an edge revised or retired; a field authority revoked; write enablement's connection with writes disabled. Kinds a person does not revise as such, or whose events do not name them (estate entries, discovery findings, heal reviews, connector manifests and mappings, resolution pairs, aliases, time fields, detector configurations) count on neither side. Found on the way (not fixed): live.test showed a backfill re-read can leave out an object an out-of-order change touched, depending on when the watch worker first sees the group; to investigate.
- D160 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B13b: the AI FDE drafts a connector from documentation; spec 49.3, 51.4): a person holding fde.engage lists a system for an engagement with its documentation (fde.fde_engagement_systems, new: an OpenAPI document, a WSDL, a GraphQL result or SDL, an OData $metadata, or documentation written for the schema; never email samples, 62.5), its base URL, owning scope and parameters; listing puts it in scope (inScope now counts listed systems: drafted ones by their connection, the rest as pending, which stage 2's exit waits on). In stage 2 the Integration principal drafts its connector through the builder (draftConnector, a new caller), probes it, and its manifest and mappings go to a person as before; a refused draft fails the task at parse, naming the code. The principal acts under connector.build, which policy bounds by its engaging administrator: the registry admits an AI FDE principal (kind fde, not other principals) to create connectors, manifest versions and connections, move a draft it made to its next version and to probing, recording it as creator (connections gain created_by_service_principal_id, exactly one creator); a connection it creates is owned by its owner, the engaging administrator. Conformance runs a build's suite and schema inference probes for the principal that drafted the connection; metering charges a principal's operation to its engagement. The AI FDE never holds a secret (52.1): the drafted connection waits for the credential its owner gives through the credential path (the system shows awaitingCredential, from the count of live secrets through the safe view), and the probe starts once one is live. Confirming and verifying stay a person's. A system listed after stage 2 has begun is drafted on the stage's next attempt; withdrawing a system takes it out of scope and leaves any drafted connection a draft its owner can revoke. Audit: fde_system_listed and fde_system_withdrawn (not named in 52.8).
- D161 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B14: agent catalogues and allowlist audit; spec 19.2 to 19.4, 10.5, 10.7): the Silo Agent introspects the catalogues of MySQL (and MariaDB), SQL Server and Oracle as it does Postgres's, for the connections it holds credentials for and only where the system is one of the scan's targets: per dialect a fixed list of statements compiled in (agent/internal/discovery/catalogue_sql.go) reading information_schema, sys views or ALL_ views, never a table, structure only (schemas, tables and views, columns and types, primary, unique and foreign keys); row counts are the engine's own statistics (table_rows with the session's statistics cache off, sys.partitions, num_rows), never a count; MySQL and Oracle read in a read-only transaction (Oracle's own SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY, which must succeed), SQL Server runs only the selects; system schemas are skipped (MySQL's own, shipped objects, Oracle-maintained users). A refused login or privilege is reported as refused. The shared catalogue builder now assembles all four dialects' findings within the existing bounds. The cell types a promoted finding's fields with what its dialect means where the SQL engine says (connect-runtime/protocols/sql/catalogueTypes.protocol.ts: Oracle's NUMBER without scale is an integer and its DATE a moment; MySQL's tinyint(1) a boolean), by the type's name otherwise. Allowlist audit: agent_target_refused (not named in 10.9, read like agent_write_grant_refused) whenever the agent refuses a system its host's owner does not allow, through a sealed login (via login) or a request to send (via request), with the work kind and connection. No new table, no new module (the drivers were already approved and in use).
- D162 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B15a: live-clone events and field aliases; spec 32.7, 30.4, 21.6, 26.7): the state plane audits source_declared_stale (each time a source's clones stopped being current: status, objects and subscriptions summed over the replica's groups, age, the replica) and source_recovered (how long they were not current), once per organisation and connection per replica until it turns; subscription_projection_changed when a policy change narrows or ends what a subscriber sees (counts granted and withheld, ended), as the state plane's act with the holder as subject; subscription_resynced when a subscriber is sent its group anew; subscription_snapshot_mode when a subscriber falls behind (30.4): the gateway, which has no database, reports its subscribers' buffer mode to the state plane (reportLiveBufferMode, holder-scoped: only the subscription's own holder's report counts). The last two are high volume. live_bounds_changed is not raised: live bounds are fixed defaults with no setting yet. Field aliases (21.6) are built: setFieldAlias, removeFieldAlias and listFieldAliases (ontology; set and remove under ontology.confirm, by a person; a column has one live alias and an alias names one column of a connection, case-insensitively; setting replaces; removal marks the row removed), audited as field_alias_set (with the alias it replaced) and field_alias_removed, never the alias's words; derivation names a property built over an aliased column by its alias; compile hears each alias as a name for every property mapped from the column (26.7). property_unmapped is raised when a type's write drops mappings, by count. No new table (ontology.field_aliases existed); no new module.
- D163 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B15b: policy authority and OAuth housekeeping; spec 14.7, 44.4, 15.3, 15.6): a super admin sets a connection's policy authority (setConnectionPolicyAuthority, connection.policy_authority decided organisation-wide): owner_set, delegated to one active member, or locked; the database already holds approval policies to it (a locked connection takes policy only from a super admin, a delegated one only from its delegate). Each change records policy_authority_changed (from, to; newly catalogued, 44.8), policy_authority_delegated naming the delegate and policy_authority_revoked naming the one it was taken from (their policies stand). An organisation withdraws its own OAuth client (revokeOAuthClient, oauth_client.manage; Silo's clients are Silo's): revoked_at set, its sealed secret crypto-shredded by the credential service (revokeOAuthClientSecret), oauth_client_revoked. Sign-ins left unfinished past their expiry are marked expired by a sweep in the oauth service (a minute by default), found across organisations by connect.oauth_flows_expired (security definer, identifiers only) and marked in each one's own organisation, each recorded once as oauth_flow_expired, the oauth service's act naming who started it. No new table.
- D164 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B15c: the organisation calendar and web search; spec 26.6, 62.8): the organisation calendar is read by any member and changed under calendar.manage (organisation-wide) through compile (getOrganisationCalendar, setOrganisationCalendar: the IANA time zone, the financial year's start month and day and its label, the week's first day; a financial year has a start and a label or neither; the change names the organisation version it read; the database refuses an unknown zone). calendar_changed (newly catalogued, standard class, the event a reviewer reads first) records which of time zone, financial year and week start changed, the zones from and to, the new start month and week day, in the same transaction as the change. Every relative period resolves against it on its next run. web_search_sent (62.8, high volume) records each web search that leaves the cell, with its status and result count; the query stays on Ask's ask_web_context_added. Left unraised, with reasons: incident_declared and incident_resolved (the status page is global, outside any organisation's log); type_dropped_from_plan (the planner does not count unsatisfied markings per hidden type yet); template_reviewed and template_withdrawn (concept templates are Fleet's, cross-tenant). No new table.
- D165 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B15d: app invalidation and tenant placement; spec 35.13, 6.7): an app's published version that an ontology change has left with invalid widgets (they open unavailable, never altered) records app_invalidated_by_ontology_change once per version and ontology version, as studio's finding with the app's owner as subject (workspace.app_versions gains invalidated_at_ontology_version, set by the open that finds it). Sign-up records tenant_placed in the new organisation's own log (the cell, the plan, the route), beside organisation_signed_up. B15 closes with 26 catalogued events not raised, each named in the coverage document with what it waits for: features not built yet (Ask's other tools and ad-hoc intents, Action type rejection and blocking, marketplace payout calculation and approval, view and lineage export, per-connection coalescing), the web client's interactions, events outside an organisation's log, and phase 9.
- D166 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17a: rejecting and blocking Action types; spec 42.10, 42.11): a holder of action.define rejects a proposed Action type with a closed-set reason (rejectActionType): it becomes rejected (a new status beside the spec's four, with rejected_at; never a version; the guard allows proposed to rejected only), audited as action_type_rejected; a confirmed type is retired, never rejected. A confirmed type whose operations a permitted connection's manifest no longer declares (the operation, the source object, a custom action) is found at the next mutation proposal, blocked (action_type_blocked naming the connection and operation) and the proposal refused (mutation.type_blocked); a blocked type takes no mutation until a new version is published, checked against the manifest as it is, which unblocks it. Reverts are unaffected.
- D167 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17b: a view's export recorded on the view; spec 37.9, 37.12, 41.2): an export Files makes from a saved view records view_exported on the view (naming the frozen file and its marking count) beside the file's own file_exported. Lineage export (lineage_exported, 59) waits on an export of a lineage graph, which Files does not take as a source yet.
- D168 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17c: contractual live bounds; spec 9.5, 30.5, 32.7): a contract may set the organisation's live bound (billing.contracts.live_objects_limit, 1 to 100,000,000; null keeps the cell's default of 1,000,000), carried into each entitlement it brings (billing.entitlements.live_objects_limit) and amended like any term; the state plane refuses a subscription past the open entitlement's bound, or the default. live_bounds_changed (newly catalogued) records each change, from and to, when an entitlement takes effect with a different bound. Correction to D159's note: the suspected backfill race was the test's fake provider applying a deliberately stale webhook (an older sequence) to its own records, so a recovery backfill rightly read the source's value; the fake now ignores an event older than the last it applied for that record, and the live tests also set aside frames received before what they wait for. No product change was needed.
- D169 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17d: per-connection coalescing; spec 18.4, 18.6, 18.10): each state-plane replica counts the changes it receives per connection each second; past 1,000 (the spec's target; configurable per process) the connection coalesces: each record's changes are held for the second and applied as one (each property its latest value in the record's order, by source sequence or observation time; a deletion wins unless the record changed after it), the delta frame carrying how many changes it stands for (coalesced), which the clone states. A connection back under its rate for a second returns to change by change. stream_coalesced records each episode once (the rate reached, the threshold, the replica). The per-subscriber limit of 500 a second stays with the gateway's coalescing and snapshot mode. No new table.
- D170 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17e: OAuth providers the catalogue does not know; spec 15.4, 15.6): the credential service reads a provider's discovery document through the cell's egress (discoverOAuthMetadata: the URL as given, or an issuer's RFC 8414 address then its OIDC one; the issuer on the document's origin, endpoints on its scheme) and registers Silo as a client where the provider implements RFC 7591 (registerOAuthDynamicClient: authorisation code with refresh, the cell's redirect URI, the manifest's scopes and client authentication; the returned secret and registration access token sealed with no connection, named by id). A person holding oauth_client.manage discovers a provider for a manifest (discoverOAuthProvider). Starting a sign-in with neither the organisation's own client nor Silo's, for a manifest that names its metadata URL, discovers and registers dynamically (connect.oauth_clients origin dynamic_registration, its metadata URL and sealed registration token kept) and proceeds as that client; a provider without registration, or one that refuses, falls back to bringing your own client (oauth.client_missing). oauth_metadata_discovered (newly catalogued, 15.6) and oauth_client_registered (origin dynamic_registration) record it. No new table.
- D171 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17f: the AI builder's address inputs; spec 16.3 inputs 1 to 3): the builder takes a specification or documentation URL (documentation kind url) and a base URL alone (kind base_url). The credential service reads a public document through the cell's egress (fetchDocument: GET, no credential, at most three redirects each checked as any request, text only, 2 MiB; a 404 or a non-text body is an answer, not a failure). What is read is recognised from what it says: an OpenAPI document (JSON or YAML), an OData $metadata, a WSDL, a GraphQL introspection result or SDL, each compiled without a model; anything else is documentation for people (an HTML page's text, scripts and navigation dropped, titled by the page, cut to the model's 20,000 characters with the cut noted), drafted through the model. A base URL alone tries the usual description addresses in turn (/openapi.json, /openapi.yaml, /swagger.json, /v3/api-docs, /api-docs, /swagger/v1/swagger.json, /.well-known/openapi.json, /$metadata, ?wsdl) and drafts the first description found; finding none, the parse stops asking for documentation (build.parse_no_description); the live credential follows at the probe. The parse findings record the input, where the document was found and any cut. An AI FDE engagement may list a system by URL (fde_engagement_systems.documentation_kind url). No new table.
- D172 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17g: the organisation's logo; spec 56.2): a super admin (org.logo.manage, organisation-wide) sets the logo through Files (setOrganisationLogo): PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG, its type sniffed from its bytes (never the client's header) and its pixel size read from its own header (utils/image.util.ts; an SVG's declared width and height or viewBox), at most 2 MB and 1024 pixels a side; an SVG is rebuilt from svg.util.ts's allowlist and kept as rebuilt. The object is stored under the organisation's own path with a new key each time (the old one stays for the recovery window), the key alone in iam.organisations; it is served to members through a membership-checked route (getOrganisationLogo), never a public bucket. logo_replaced (newly catalogued) records type, size, pixels and whether one was replaced. No new table.
- D173 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17h: exporting a lineage graph; spec 59.4, 59.7): a reviewer holding lineage.read (organisation-wide) exports the upstream or downstream of a resource (lineage.exportLineage, keyed) as JSON or as CSV (node and edge rows in one table, under a head naming its markings, the query, its bounds and what was withheld). It is the reviewer's walk: the same depth and node bounds (at most 2,000 nodes, the lineage writer's input limit), refused with the bound named rather than truncated, and nodes the reviewer's markings do not reach counted in the document, never named. Files stores it as an export: every node it names is a lineage input (exported_from), so it carries their markings, printed in it; it is decided on lineage.read rather than file.export, accepted only from the lineage service, and runs no query (run_reference null). files.file_provenance gains source_lineage_node_id (the node the walk began at, foreign key to gov.lineage_nodes; source_kind 'lineage'). Export inputs are bounded at 2,000 (was 500). lineage_exported names the file. The 59.6 build check also holds the app version, simulation result and finding producers now.
- D174 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17i: type_dropped_from_plan; spec 21.15, 57.11): policy's resolveAccess now says, for each connection and object type asked about, which of its markings the actor does not satisfy (for the services' use, never shown to the actor). The planner's reader access lists each type left out because the reader lacks a marking on it or on a contributing connection, with the count of distinct markings lacking, and compile records each as type_dropped_from_plan before the model is asked: the object type as the resource, the count and the ontology version, never the question. It is a query event (the high-volume class, spec 63.4), one per dropped type per compiled question, written in one transaction. No schema change.
- D175 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17j: the generic governed edit; spec 42.9): silo.edit is Silo's own Action type, made the first time an organisation needs it (its settings read or its first edit): it has no proposer (action_types' proposer check is now none for the system row, exactly one otherwise) and its versions no confirming member (action_type_versions.confirmed_by is nullable, the insert guard allowing null only for silo.edit). A version carries no content of its own: one is published for each ontology version an edit compiles against, so a mutation records the version it compiled against. An edit (proposeMutation's or checkMutation's `edit`: update setting or clearing properties, create giving them, delete; values are record values, sealed as its parameters) compiles its own definition against main's head: plain data types only, contributing connections that write over a writing transport, never a physical object, declaring the operations; checked as a published version is; never a custom action or webhook, risk class data. It passes the full mutation path; the mutation's manifest keeps the definition (its source objects, read by execution and a revert, which is a generic edit too); mutations.generic_edit is set and shown on the mutation view, so it is countable; generic_edit_compiled (read first by a reviewer) records the object type, operation and counts. mutation.policy organisation-wide disables or allows it (setGenericEdit; generic_edit_policy_set, an event chapter 77 does not name); disabled, an edit is refused with the offer to propose an Action type to a holder of action.define. silo.edit is not listed among Action types; the settings name its id.
- D176 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17k: a change asked for in Ask; spec 42.9, 36.4): compileQuestion takes intents (Ask sets it for answer and propose_action, never find_objects); only then is the model told it may return an intent (the object type, update, create or delete, the properties to set with the values written in the question, the properties to clear, and filters naming the records) and given that output structure. Compile checks it as it checks a plan (every name in the reader's vocabulary, every property shown in clear and stored); the records an update or delete changes become a plan that finds them, bounded, kept and bound under the turn. It binds the intent (compile/intent.service.ts): the confirmed Action types on that object type whose rules make the change from parameters (update: property and link rules only; create; delete) and whose required parameters the intent fills, each with its parameters pre-filled (action_intent_bound names the one bound, or the count the person chooses among); none fits, the generic governed edit where the organisation allows it (getActionSettings), else refused with the offer to propose an Action type. Charged as a compile; never executed. Ask records the turn as a proposal (ask_turns.outcome 'proposal', tool propose_action, the new proposal column: references only, the candidates, object type, operation and property names) and raises ask_action_proposed; the reply carries the draft (each candidate's parameters, or the generic edit) once, never stored, for proposeMutation; the plan's records come from re-running the turn.
- D177 (implementation 2026-11-18, backend stage B17l: Ask's explanation and navigation tools; spec 36.4): askQuestion's tool takes explain_lineage, explain_finding and open_clone, each with a subject by reference (the contract refuses a subject without its tool, or of the wrong kind): explain lineage of a turn's answer (its plan's ask_prompt node), a property (its identity's node) or an object (its type's sources), read through lineage's getLineage under the asker (lineage.view; what their markings withhold is withheld); explain a finding through recognition's getFinding (Ask is now a caller of the finding reads); open a clone (an object's view or a type's Clone Canvas) after policy says the asker may see the type (clone.view and its markings; not visible and not there are one answer), navigation only.
