Compile, when the reader may see more object types than `COMPILE_NARROW_TYPES` (20), asks ontology's `rankObjectTypes`: the question is embedded as a query and each type scores the best similarity of its own description, its properties' and its links'. The question is compiled against the top 20 with their properties and the links between them, plus any type it names exactly, the type it is asked from, the types of the thread's earlier plans, and any type not yet embedded. Where the model says the question is outside that vocabulary, or the plan names a type, property or link it lacks, compile widens once to the whole vocabulary. The compile outcome carries the set used and whether it widened (`narrowing`); the `plan_validated` event records that it was narrowed, the set's size and a digest of it, and whether it widened. No ranking (no embedding route, a failure): the whole vocabulary, as before.
- D102 (implementation 2026-11-15, uploads in Files; spec 41.4 to 41.6): no table change; `files.claim_expired_files` now claims exports only. An upload (`POST /files/uploads`, file.upload) is stored by siloes-import against an enabled Import Silo, which keeps the bytes (`siloes.silo_files`, so it sits inside the Siloes disclosure): stored, in the Silo's own `files` upload source with no definition and marked processed at once (the import worker never reads it); or ingested through a named source with a definition, read as any import. siloes-import checks silo.import and every marking on the Silo, takes the type from the bytes, and rebuilds an SVG from an allowlist of elements and attributes (fragment-only links, `url(#id)` only; a DTD or entity refused unread). Files keeps the entry (`kind = 'upload'`, `silo_file_id`, `ingestion_state`), the Silo's retention as its `retention` and `expires_at`, and the Silo's markings as the file's; audited `file_uploaded` (and `file_ingested`). Uploads are bounded as exports are (one reply opens each). Opening one passes the entry's checks and then the Silo's (silo.import, its markings); a share that reaches someone who cannot open the Silo is refused as `silo_access` and recorded (`file_download_refused`). Deleting one requests a purge of its Silo file (silo.purge, through the purge approval chain where one is configured); when a file or whole-Silo purge completes, siloes-capture tells Files, which marks the entries deleted with the purge's receipt as theirs (`files.file_deletions.purge_receipt_id`). Uploads expire with their Silo's retention, not the Files sweep.
- D101 (implementation 2026-11-15, finding conditions on Crons; spec 40.3, 40.12 step 2): `automation.automation_run_state.findings_checked_at` (timestamptz, null): when the last run read the findings its finding conditions name. A finding condition (stored with its `detector_id` and `object_type_id`; checked at creation against the detectors and the owner's vocabulary) is evaluated each run over the findings recognition gives the Cron's own principal for that detector and type, superseded ones included and no Lens applied (a finding silenced in the owner's Lens still counts): `raised` is met by any raised since the last check (the Cron's creation before its first run), `score_above` by one of those scoring above the threshold, `recurred` by one whose latest earlier finding on the same objects had been superseded before it was raised (a run raising it again straight after supersedes it at the same instant, so that is not a recurrence). Findings that cannot be read are indeterminate. `listFindings` takes a detector id, and each finding says when it was superseded. The Cron still runs its question; the condition decides whether its actions are taken. Also: a Silo purge's wipe step is tried again (four attempts, backing off) when a store refuses it for a moment, since a wipe only deletes.
- D100 (implementation 2026-11-15, markings on functions and interfaces; spec 21.15): no table change. A marking applied to a function or an interface (`gov.resource_markings.function_id`, `interface_id`) now withholds it: policy's `resolveAccess` decides functions and interfaces as it does link and action types (visible only where every marking on them is held); the reader's vocabulary leaves out a computed property whose function is withheld (so it is never named, filtered or computed), and keeps the interfaces it may see (part of the result cache key); an object set over a withheld interface is refused whole as unavailable, without saying why. Markings on object types, link types and action types were already enforced; object sets carry their types' and traversals' as before.
- D99 (implementation 2026-11-15, concept templates; spec 22.7): no table change. Derivation reads the reviewed set (`ontology.concept_templates`, row-level security shows a tenant nothing else; Fleet writes it) and names an object's proposal from the template whose field names it holds best: at least two of them, and at least half, compared without case or separators; the highest share, then the most, then the name. The proposal takes the template's name (API name, display and plural), its evidence says which template and how many names matched, and the decision carries the template's id, which the commit writes on the new `object_types` row (`template_id`, frozen from insert by `object_types_frozen`, so it is set at creation or never). A template never decides anything else; a person still confirms, corrects or renames.
- D98 (implementation 2026-11-15, value overlap; spec 22.4): no table change. Derivation (on by default; `overlap: false` skips it) pairs, within bounds, an existing active type's match keys and identity-named properties (an email, a registration, a code), each mapped plainly from another connection, with same-typed fields of the derived connection's objects whose names point at the same thing. For each pair it reads up to 1,000 distinct values from the new side (a bounded read) and asks the other side which it holds (an `in` filter in chunks of 200): a semi-join whose values live in the deriving process's memory only, as for inferred links (D75), never in the control plane, a proposal or a model. A pair counts where at least 10 values are shared and the chance that at least a fifth of those sampled are held is at least 0.9; it then proposes the object contributing to that type, matched on the property, its same-named fields mapped, and no primary key (it becomes resolvable), with the counts as evidence. `overlap_computed` records the object, field, type, property and the two counts. Below the threshold nothing is proposed.
- D97 (implementation 2026-11-15, drafts from WSDL and GraphQL descriptions; spec 14.4, 16.4): no table change. The visual builder's `importDraft` (gateway `POST /connect/builder/imports`, connector.build) compiles a service's own description to a draft manifest without a model, the person then editing, trying and publishing it as any draft; nothing is saved. A WSDL 1.1 (document/literal; namespaces resolved, a DTD refused unread; the SOAP 1.1 port preferred) gives an object per operation whose response holds a repeated complex element: its request element's simple children as parameters, the record's simple children and those of a child element once nested as fields, token or page paging and equality filters where the names say so, the port's address and the binding's action. A GraphQL introspection result or SDL gives an object per Query field that lists objects (a list, edges.node or nodes): its arguments as variables, cursor paging and the limit from first, after and pageInfo, equality filters where an argument names a field. Neither describes authentication (noted); every expression is written from fixed templates with names as CEL literals.
- D96 (implementation 2026-11-15, the SOAP protocol engine; spec 14.4): no table change. A manifest may name the `soap` protocol (version 1.1 or 1.2) and SOAP sources: the operation's request element and namespace, its declared parameters (child elements in order, qualified or not), constants, the path of element names to the records under the Body, and token paging. The engine builds the envelope (names from the manifest, checked at save; every value escaped element text, a character XML cannot carry refused), sends it through the credential service with HTTP-level credentials (a prepared request may now carry an XML body with one of SOAP's content types; 1.1's action in the SOAPAction header, 1.2's in the content type), and reads the Body with prefixes removed, entities decoded once and nil as null; a response carrying a DTD is refused unread. A Fault decides by its code (Client, Sender and version or header faults are the request's and not retried, though 1.1 sends them with 500), after the manifest's rules and except 401, 403 and 429. Pushdown and paging set declared parameters only; the pushdown compiler explains a SOAP step as its operation and the parameters set. Not yet: writes, WS-Security in the envelope, the agent's SOAP execution, and drafting from a WSDL.
- D95 (implementation 2026-11-15, 69.6 routing, states in the Object Index; decision 2026-11-14): each index table's nominated property gains `<property>__state` (STRING: the value's state as the engine decided it at the refresh: declared, agreed, only, disputed, empty, or unchecked where the Silo's principal sees it masked or redacted). A disputed value stays null. The planner's read returns each value's state and treats disputes as the engine does: a disputed value is never empty, and an entry whose first unmet filter is disputed is left out and counted (`excludedByDispute`). So a type several systems feed is answered from the index too; one whose table predates the states (until its next refresh, which rewrites every entry since the row hash now covers states) declines as not refreshed and is read live. Split plans stay single-system. A change-stream observation is applied only to a property one system maps; one several systems map waits for the next refresh, as one system cannot decide it.
- D94 (implementation 2026-11-15, 69.6 routing, split plans; decision 2026-11-14): no table change. Where the Object Index does not hold every property a single-source lookup uses, it may still narrow it: when the system cannot apply some filter itself, the index holds every filtered property and the type's identifier and is fresh within the tolerance, and the system applies `in` on its identifier (pushdown-compiler says), the executor takes the identifiers of the matching entries from the index (bounded by the keys a hop may carry) and reads the system live by key, applying the filters again to the live values. An object that stopped meeting them since the refresh is left out; one that started is missed until the next refresh, so each figure's lineage carries `narrowedBy` (index, as of its refresh, and why) beside the live read time of its values. A decline or too many keys reads the system whole.
- D93 (implementation 2026-11-15, 69.6 routing, large aggregates from the Warehouse; decision 2026-11-14): no table change. A single-type aggregate that no source computes per group goes to the Warehouse where it holds every property used (none computed by Silo), the set is larger than one source read may hold (the current table's row count against the step bound) and its watermark is within the freshness tolerance; otherwise the sources. warehouse-schema's `aggregateWarehouse` computes it in BigQuery with the engine's rules for disputes: an object whose first unmet filter is disputed is left out and counted, a disputed group key leaves the object out of the groups and counted, each measure over its non-null values with their count (min and max as numbers, times as epoch milliseconds); per property, values and disputes over the population for the answer's coverage. The answer's `aggregateForm` is `warehouse` and every figure's lineage says so, as of the watermark; a decline at run time reads the sources. Coverage gains the current table's row count. The as-of read is bounded by the merged-result bound (one row per object), refused as `query.bound_merged_result`. BigQuery jobs for these reads are labelled `warehouse_read`.
- D92 (implementation 2026-11-15, 69.6 routing, the Warehouse as an as-of source; decision 2026-11-14): the Warehouse's current tables gain `_first_observed_at` (TIMESTAMP: when the row was first written; never updated by a merge). A plan may carry `asOf` (an instant parameter and the asker's words; one node, no aggregate, no period). warehouse-schema answers the planner's coverage (`warehouseCoverage`: held properties, the watermark from the current table's last sync, the history from when the history table began) and the executor's read (`readWarehouseAsOf`: the objects first observed by the instant, each property as the previous value of its first change after the instant, else its current value; filters applied in the engine over a bounded read; the same gates as the Object Index, with every marking on what the Warehouse holds of the type). An as-of question is the Warehouse's or refused (`plan.as_of_unavailable`, naming the property not held or how far the history reaches; `plan.as_of_future`; `query.as_of_unavailable` where the Warehouse declines at run time): no live fallback, as no system holds the past. Lineage carries `servedBy` (warehouse, as of the instant asked) and the explanation states the instant and the watermark. A property nominated later has history only from then; a value the history cannot tell apart from empty reads as empty. Still to come: large aggregates on current state, split plans, and multi-node plans.
- D91 (implementation 2026-11-15, 69.6 routing, first part; decision 2026-11-14): no table change. The planner's source chooser (coverage first; live by default for current state; the Object Index for lookup, search and filtering when within the freshness tolerance, 15 minutes by default; the Warehouse for history, as-of, aggregation over large sets and Silo-only properties; stale gives way to live; ties to the fresher then the cheaper; a stale Silo source chosen only where nothing else holds the property, flagged). index-builder answers the planner's coverage (`objectIndexCoverage`: held properties and the watermark, `last_refreshed_at`) and the executor's read (`readObjectIndex`: filters, a split plan's keys, every marking satisfied, the same gates as search). A single-node, single-source lookup or filter with no period is answered by a fresh Index; the result's column lineage carries `servedBy` (index, as of its refresh, and why). The index holds a disputed value as empty, so types several systems feed are read live until it records disputes. Still to come: the Warehouse as a source, split plans, and multi-node plans.
- D90 (implementation 2026-11-14, the PKCS#11 HSM; decision 2026-11-14): no table change. `pkcs11_hsm` key management through graphene-pk11 (key URI `pkcs11:object=<label>`): AES-GCM wrapping with the binding context as additional data, SHA256-HMAC, RSA-OAEP-SHA256 import decryption and the import key's public half, all in the HSM, keys found by label and never created. The sovereign cell's Thales Luna and on-premises HSMs; commercial cells keep Cloud KMS, whose HSM protection level is Cloud HSM.
- D89 (implementation 2026-11-14, Ask web context per scope; decision 2026-11-14): `workspace.ask_web_policies` (one per scope: enabled, allowed and blocked domains, the markings an admin satisfying them covered, who). For a member: off where the organisation, or any scope they sit in or under, turned it off, or those scopes own connections carrying markings not covered; otherwise the deepest allowlist and every blocklist filter the results. Each web call's audit event carries its scope and the query sent.
- D88 (implementation 2026-11-14, PNG export jobs; decision 2026-11-14): `clone.render_jobs` (queued, rendering, completed into Files, failed with a code, or expired after an hour; the exporter's session kept to file the image under) and `clone.claim_render_job` (security definer: the oldest queued job across organisations, marked rendering, identifiers only). The renderer is deferred until the web client exists; its claim, complete and fail endpoints are fixed now.
- D87 (implementation 2026-11-14, map tiles; decision 2026-11-14; the signed URL replaced by D227's tiles through the gateway): no table change. A `tiles` bucket (`OBJECT_BUCKET_TILES`) holds the Protomaps PMTiles basemap (`MAP_TILES_KEY`); `GET /map-tiles` (clone.view) gives an hour's V4 signed read URL through `@google-cloud/storage`, for MapLibre GL's range requests, with the data's attribution.
- D86 (implementation 2026-11-14, resources and capacity; decision 2026-11-14): `simulation.dependency_edges.consumption`, `capacity_property_id`, `demand_property_id`, `capacity_period` (a resource edge's: units of the resource one unit of the dependant consumes, the resource's numeric capacity property, the dependant's numeric demand property, the period; all four on a confirmed resource edge, none on any other). `simulation.simulation_results.capacity_shortfall` and `capacity_period`: a dependant whose resource cannot meet demand, demand being the sum of consumption times units over the resource's dependants and the capacity left being reduced capacity's share (none when unavailable); the shortfall is the share of demand unmet. Constrained dependants are reported, not walked further.
- D85 (implementation 2026-11-14, mobile push; decision 2026-11-14): `workspace.push_devices` (a member's provider token per platform, `fcm` or `apns`; live tokens unique; revoked when the provider reports the token gone). A `mobile_push` notification goes to the recipient's live devices on the cell's platform as a title, an unread count and a link only; it is delivered when one device took it. FCM HTTP v1 with a service account's token in the commercial cells; APNs directly over HTTP/2 with an ES256 provider token in the sovereign build (FCM refused there by configuration).
- D84 (implementation 2026-11-14, Ask's web context; decision 2026-11-14): `iam.organisations.ask_web_enabled` (default true; `ask.web.manage`), `workspace.ask_turns.outside_context` (jsonb: the query sent, when, and each result's title, URL and snippet, or unavailable). The query is the question's own wording with quoted text, addresses, links, dates, numbers and anything holding a digit removed; it is sent to Brave only after an answer exists, only where the cell has a provider (none in the sovereign build); audit events carry counts only.
- D83 (implementation 2026-11-14, unavailable for a period; decision 2026-11-14): `simulation.simulation_results.unavailable_for` (interval): how long a reached object is out, the longer of the outage reaching it and its recovery lead time (the median observed lead time where the edge has history, otherwise its stated lead time). A stated failure of form `unavailable_for_period` states its `period`; a hard edge carries the outage on, a soft edge makes its dependant late by the outage less its buffer.
- D82 (implementation 2026-11-14, two detectors; decision 2026-11-14): `recognition.detectors` gains `uniqueness` (federated, needs at least two properties: objects agreeing on every one, filled, undisputed, after trimming and case folding, one finding per group, `duplicate_entities`) and `timeliness` (federated, needs a time field: an age in days far above the population's median by the modified z-score, one-sided, 3.5 or 5 under 30 objects, `age_robust_z`). Neither states a record value. The spec's ten detectors are now all named.
- D81 (implementation 2026-11-14, declassifiers and purpose approval; decision 2026-11-14): `gov.declassifier_memberships` (a membership or a scope's members named for a marking, with justification, granter, a second person's approval, optional expiry, revocation; append-only: frozen columns, approved once and revoked once, no delete grant, apart from roles). A live, approved grant meets 58.10's "a membership named for that marking" for requesting a declassification; satisfying the marking and another approver are still required. `gov.purpose_definitions.use` (analysis, export, external_sharing, write_back, ai_or_simulation; anything but analysis requires approval, checked). `gov.purpose_sessions.requires_approval`, `approved_by`, `approved_at`: such a declaration reaches nothing until a holder of purpose.define other than the declarer approves it within its time (policy's live-session read requires it; the hot copy is written only then).
- D80 (implementation 2026-11-14, AI FDE stage exits; decision 2026-11-14): `fde.fde_engagements.owner_membership_id` (null: the engaging administrator), the customer's named engagement owner, never the supervising engineer (checked). Only the owner confirms a stage exit; stage 5, whose work writes to sources, also needs its confirmer to hold `mutation.policy` on every connection in scope; Silo staff and the supervising engineer confirm nothing. `fde_owner_named` is audited.
- D79 (implementation 2026-11-14, email domains; decision 2026-11-14): `iam.organisation_domains` (domain, a verification token published as the TXT record `_silo-verification.<domain>` = `silo-verification=<token>`, status pending, verified or removed). A verified domain is claimed: one claim per domain in the cell (partial unique index), and `iam.domain_claimed` (security definer, yes or no only) lets sign-up refuse a new organisation for an address at it. Claims are per cell: the directory holds no domain.
- D78 (implementation 2026-11-14, self-serve sign-up; decision 2026-11-14): `iam.signups` (cell-level, no RLS, auth only): the address, the organisation's name and slug, plan (Standard or Business), term and seats, the hash of a one-time link token (kind `sup`), its expiry (24 hours), and once completed `completed_at` and `created_organisation_id` (a reference, not a tenant key). No password or name is kept before verification; unverified rows are deleted a day after expiry. `iam.grant_founding_super_admin` (security definer, executable by silo_auth) makes the founder's Super admin grant, only in the organisation's own context, only where it has no assignment, only for an active member of it. The directory places a sign-up (`POST /v1/signup/place` on its public listener) in the chosen residency's active commercial cell with the fewest live organisations, never across residency, never in a sovereign directory. Completing a sign-up registers the slug and the person with the directory, signs the founder in and starts the checkout as them; until the provider's webhook writes the subscription the organisation has no entitlement.
- D77 (implementation 2026-11-14, SCIM groups; decision 2026-11-14): `iam.scim_groups` (display name, external id, soft-deleted), `iam.scim_group_members` (who is in each group now) and `iam.scim_group_mappings` (an admin's mapping of a group to a role at a scope or organisation-wide, removable, never edited). `iam.role_assignments.scim_group_mapping_id` marks a grant a mapping gave: given as the mapping's creator under the delegation trigger, revoked as its granter when no live mapping of a live group the member is in gives that role at that scope any more. `iam.memberships.scim_managed` marks a member SCIM created; policy refuses a hand edit of such a member's roles, and of any mapped grant (`role.scim_managed`). Unmapped groups grant nothing; no role is created from a group name; a mapping is by group id, so a rename grants nothing new.
- D76 (implementation 2026-11-14, plan gates; decision 2026-11-14 amending 71.2): `billing.entitlements.connections_limit` (integer, null for unlimited), written from the plan (Standard and Business figures still to be given, so unlimited until then; contracts unlimited). `capabilities` gains `ai_connector_builder` and `nocode_connector_builder`, which every contract's entitlements carry and no self-serve plan does. A connection counts against the limit while not revoked, a Silo's own source excepted; the count is taken under a transaction advisory lock per organisation, so two additions cannot both take the last place. A self-serve entitlement (from a subscription) lists and connects certified prebuilt connectors only. An organisation with no entitlement row is not gated.
- D75 (implementation 2026-11-11, inferred links; decision 2026-11-11): `ontology.link_type_routes.origin` gains `inferred`: a route proposed from value overlap where the organisation turned link inference on, accepted by a person. Derivation reads identifiers and candidate key values (bounded, in memory only) through connect-runtime.
- D74 (implementation 2026-11-11, probabilistic matching): no table change. An inferred pair list is an ordinary `pair_list` resolution proposal whose body carries `inference` (fields compared, each pair's probability and agreement pattern, the statement); decided ones are the evidence the next inference learns its agreement rates from.
- D73 (implementation 2026-11-11, finding usefulness): no table change; computed on read from the organisation's dispositions of the detector's findings on the type.
- D72 (implementation 2026-11-11, simulation priors): `simulation.simulation_runs.inferred` (the organisation's switch at the run); `simulation.simulation_results.path_mode` gains `inferred`, which like `probabilistic` carries a probability and spread.
- D71 (implementation 2026-11-11, inference switches; decision 2026-11-11): `iam.organisations.inference_simulation`, `inference_resolution`, `inference_links`, `inference_findings`, all false by default; permission `org.inference.manage` (Super admin). Each lets Silo go beyond observed evidence in one place, overriding the spec's binding rules (39.5 observed-only distributions; links never inferred; deterministic matching; findings never a judgement) only where an organisation turns it on.
- D70 (implementation 2026-11-10, Cron execute authorisations): `automation.automation_authorisations.expiry_recorded_at`, set once by maintenance's sweep when an execute authorisation's expiry passes (`automation_authorisation_expired`); the revoke-only trigger allows it. An expired execute authorisation no longer withdraws the Cron's reach: its mutate action proposes for a person instead of executing (40.6).
- D69 (implementation 2026-11-10, directory registration retry): `iam.directory_registrations` (user id, attempts, next attempt, last error code), cell-level like `iam.users`, no organisation and no RLS: a registration the directory missed, retried by auth's worker with backoff (`DIRECTORY_RETRY_SECONDS`, doubling to a day) until made.
- D68 (implementation 2026-11-10, webhook payloads): `action.webhook_deliveries.payload` is sealed bytea (was jsonb): an Action type's JSONata payload may carry its parameter values, so the queued body is a record value bound to its row (`action.webhook_deliveries`, column `payload`). notify joins `RECORD_VALUE_CALLERS` to open it when posting.
- D67 (implementation 2026-11-10, source-field markings): `gov.marking_declassifications.resource_type` gains `property_mapping`. A field marking is a `gov.resource_markings` row on `property_mapping_id` (58.3: "the id of the field map entry"); it is resolved by connection and field path across every mapping row, so it outlives the type version it was applied on.
- D66 (implementation 2026-11-10, canary sample): `iam.organisations.canary_sample_rows` (1 to 9,999, null for the default 100), written by actions with `mutation.policy` across the organisation (45.4).
- D65 (implementation 2026-11-10, deprecation notices):
  - `workspace.notifications.ontology_element_id` (no foreign key: an object type, link type, shared property, interface or function), a new source arm, with kinds `element_deprecated` and `element_retiring`; unique per recipient, kind, channel and element.
  - `ontology.retirement_reminders`: one per deprecation, written in its transaction, `remind_on` seven days before `retire_after`; sent once (`sent_at`) or cancelled (`cancelled_at`) when the element is retired first, deprecated again or brought back by a rollback. One open reminder per element. `ontology.retirement_reminders_due` finds due ones across organisations for the ontology service's sweep.
  - Owners of dependants are read from the dependency index joined to each dependant's owner (an app's, saved view's, object set's, Cron's or scenario's owner, a lens's holder); a dependant with no single owner (an Action type, a function, an interface implementation) names none.
  - Why: owners of every dependant are told at deprecation and seven days before retirement (25.7).
- D63 (implementation 2026-11-10, principal expiry): `iam.service_principals.expiry_recorded_at`, set once by maintenance's sweep when `expires_at` has passed, which records `service_principal_expired` (60.8). A principal is refused from `expires_at` whether or not the sweep has run.
